words.tr:
n. 释放；发布；
v. 释放；发布；
words.ex: The release of the prisoner made everyone happy.
words.ex_cn: 囚犯的释放让每个人都高兴。
words.en: To release something means to let it go or to allow it to be free, or to make something available to the public.

words.ex: The horror of the dark made her scream.
words.ex_cn: 对黑暗的恐惧让她尖叫。
words.en: A feeling of great fear, shock, or disgust.

words.tr:
n. 污点；
v. 玷污；
words.ex: There is a coffee stain on the table.
words.ex_cn: 桌子上有一个咖啡污点。
words.en: A stain is a mark on something that is difficult to remove, especially one made by a liquid such as blood or coffee. To stain something means to leave a mark on it that is difficult to remove.

words.ex: The body expels waste through the kidneys.
words.ex_cn: 身体通过肾脏排出废物。
words.en: If someone is expelled from a school or organization, they are officially told to leave because they have behaved badly or broken the rules.

words.ex: He lingered by the door, not wanting to leave.
words.ex_cn: 他逗留在门口，不想离开。
words.en: If you linger somewhere, you stay there for a longer time than is necessary, for example because you are enjoying yourself.

words.ex: The company will reimburse you for your travel expenses.
words.ex_cn: 公司会报销你的旅行费用。
words.en: If you reimburse someone for something, you pay them back the money that they have spent or lost because of it.

words.ex: The storm sundered the old tree.
words.ex_cn: 风暴把那棵老树劈开了。
words.en: To break or split apart, especially along a natural line or grain.

words.tr:
adj. 苦行的；禁欲主义的
n. 苦行者；禁欲者
words.ex: He lives an ascetic life with no luxury.
words.ex_cn: 他过着简朴的生活，没有任何奢侈。
words.en: An ascetic person has a way of life that is simple and strict, usually because of their religious beliefs.

words.tr:
n. 化妆舞会；伪装
v. 伪装；冒充
words.ex: We went to a masquerade last night.
words.ex_cn: 我们昨晚去参加了一个化妆舞会。
words.en: A masquerade is a party or dance where people wear masks and costumes, or it refers to the act of pretending to be someone or something else.

words.ex: He bought some miscellaneous items at the store.
words.ex_cn: 他在商店里买了一些各种各样的东西。
words.en: Consisting of a variety of ingredients or parts.

words.ex: The hurricane destroyed many houses.
words.ex_cn: 飓风摧毁了许多房屋。
words.en: A hurricane is an extremely violent wind or storm.

words.ex: The two events happened simultaneously.
words.ex_cn: 这两个事件同时发生了。
words.en: Happening, existing, or done at the same time.

words.ex: They will renovate the old house next month.
words.ex_cn: 他们下个月将翻新那栋老房子。
words.en: To renovate means to restore something to a good state of repair or to make it as good as new.

words.tr:
v. 潜伏；隐藏
n. 潜伏；埋伏
words.ex: A cat lurks behind the bush.
words.ex_cn: 一只猫躲在灌木丛后。
words.en: To lurk means to wait or move in a secretive way so that you cannot be seen, especially because you are about to attack someone or do something wrong.

words.tr:
n. 光；灯；光线；
adj. 轻的；浅的；少量的；明亮的；
v. 点燃；照亮；
words.ex: The light from the window brightened the room.
words.ex_cn: 窗户透进来的光让房间变亮了。
words.en: Light is the natural agent that stimulates sight and makes things visible. It is also used to describe something that is not heavy or a source of illumination.

words.tr:
n. 海峡；渠道；河床；频道；
v. 引导；
words.ex: The English Channel separates England from France.
words.ex_cn: 英吉利海峡将英格兰与法国分隔开。
words.en: A channel is a television station and the programs that it broadcasts. A channel is also a method or system that people use to send information, goods, etc. to each other.

words.ex: He feigns sleep to avoid talking.
words.ex_cn: 他假装睡觉以避免交谈。
words.en: If someone feigns a particular feeling, attitude, or physical condition, they try to make other people think that they have it or are experiencing it, although this is not true.

words.ex: I have three apples.
words.ex_cn: 我有三个苹果。
words.en: The number equivalent to the sum of one and two; one more than two.

words.ex: He expressed dissent about the new rule.
words.ex_cn: 他对新规定提出了异议。
words.en: Dissent is strong disagreement or dissatisfaction with a decision or opinion, especially one that is supported by most people or by people in authority.

words.ex: He concluded that the experiment failed.
words.ex_cn: 他得出结论说实验失败了。
words.en: If you conclude that something is true, you decide that it is true using the facts you know as a basis.

words.ex: He has pyromania and loves to light fires.
words.ex_cn: 他有纵火癖，喜欢点火。
words.en: A mental disorder characterized by an irresistible impulse to start fires.

words.ex: He fractured his arm during the soccer game.
words.ex_cn: 他在足球比赛中摔断了手臂。
words.en: If something such as a bone fractures or is fractured, it breaks or cracks.

words.tr:
v. 声称；索赔；
n. 声称；索要；
words.ex: He claims that he saw a UFO last night.
words.ex_cn: 他声称自己昨晚看到了不明飞行物。
words.en: If you say that someone claims that something is true, you mean they say that it is true but you are not sure whether or not they are telling the truth.

words.tr: adj. 无定形的；无组织的；
words.ex: The glass is amorphous because it lacks a regular shape.
words.ex_cn: 玻璃是无定形的，因为它没有规则的形状。
words.en: Lacking a clear shape or form; not clearly defined or structured.

words.ex: The trees showed bright foliage in autumn.
words.ex_cn: 秋天时，树木呈现出鲜艳的叶子。
words.en: The leaves of a plant or tree, or the leaves on trees and plants collectively.

words.tr:
v. 逝去；过去
n. （光阴）逝去
words.ex: Two hours elapsed while he waited for the bus.
words.ex_cn: 他等公交车时，两个小时过去了。
words.en: If time elapses, it passes.

words.ex: A problem arose during the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 会议中出现了一个问题。
words.en: If a situation or problem arises, it begins to exist or people start to become aware of it.

words.ex: I am awaiting the bus.
words.ex_cn: 我正在等公交车。
words.en: If you await someone or something, you wait for them.

words.ex: The country fell into anarchy after the war.
words.ex_cn: 战争之后，这个国家陷入了混乱。
words.en: Anarchy is a state of disorder due to absence or nonrecognition of authority or other controlling systems.

words.tr: adj. 无道德观念的；不辨是非的
words.ex: He made an amoral decision to lie for money.
words.ex_cn: 他为了钱做出了一个不道德的决定。
words.en: If you describe someone as amoral, you mean that they do not consider whether their behavior is morally right or wrong.

words.ex: The boy has an abnormal heartbeat.
words.ex_cn: 这个男孩的心跳不正常。
words.en: Deviating from what is normal or usual, typically in a way that is undesirable or worrying.

words.tr:
n. 滥用；虐待；辱骂；
v. 滥用；虐待；辱骂；
words.ex: The abuse of power led to many problems.
words.ex_cn: 权力的滥用导致了许多问题。
words.en: Abuse is the improper usage or treatment of a thing, often to unfairly or improperly gain benefit. Abuse can come in many forms, such as physical or verbal maltreatment, injury, assault, violation, rape, unjust practices, crimes, or other types of aggression.

words.tr:
n. 提倡者；
v. 提倡；
words.ex: He is an advocate for clean water.
words.ex_cn: 他是清洁用水的提倡者。
words.en: If you advocate a particular action or plan, you recommend it publicly.

words.ex: He gave her a gift to appease her anger.
words.ex_cn: 他送她一份礼物来平息她的怒气。
words.en: If you try to appease someone, you try to stop them from being angry by giving them what they want.

words.ex: His ambition is to become a president.
words.ex_cn: 他的野心是成为总统。
words.en: An ambition is a strong desire to achieve something, typically requiring determination and hard work.

words.ex: The frog is an amphibian.
words.ex_cn: 青蛙是一种两栖动物。
words.en: An amphibian is a type of animal that can live both on land and in water. Frogs, toads, and salamanders are examples of amphibians.

words.ex: He wakes up at antemeridian.
words.ex_cn: 他在上午醒来。
words.en: Relating to the period of time before noon (midday).

words.ex: The guests waited in the anteroom before being called for dinner.
words.ex_cn: 客人们在被叫去吃饭之前在前厅等候。
words.en: A small room leading to a main one, often used as a waiting area.

words.tr:
adj. 逆时针方向的
adv. 逆时针方向地
words.ex: The fan turns anticlockwise.
words.ex_cn: 风扇逆时针旋转。
words.en: If something is moving anticlockwise, it is moving in the opposite direction to the direction in which the hands of a clock move.

words.ex: The doctor gave me an antibiotic for my infection.
words.ex_cn: 医生给我开了抗菌素治疗感染。
words.en: A substance that can kill or inhibit the growth of bacteria and other microorganisms.

words.ex: He drives an automobile to work every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天开车去上班。
words.en: A vehicle that is powered by an engine and is used for carrying passengers on roads.

words.ex: The factory uses automation to make cars.
words.ex_cn: 工厂使用自动化来制造汽车。
words.en: The use of largely automatic equipment in a system of manufacturing or other production process.

words.tr: v. 使静止不动；使停泊
words.ex: The wind helps to becalm the boat.
words.ex_cn: 风帮助船平静下来。
words.en: To becalm means to make something calm or still, especially in the context of making the sea calm so that a sailing ship cannot move because there is no wind.

words.tr: v. 以朋友态度对待；帮助
words.ex: He decided to befriend the new student.
words.ex_cn: 他决定结交那个新生。
words.en: To befriend someone means to act as a friend to them by offering help, support, or companionship.

words.ex: Bad luck may befall anyone at any time.
words.ex_cn: 坏运气可能随时降临到任何人身上。
words.en: If something bad or unlucky befalls you, it happens to you.

words.ex: He looked at the catalogue to find the book.
words.ex_cn: 他翻看目录来找那本书。
words.en: A catalogue is a list of things such as the goods you can buy from a particular company, the objects in a museum, or the books in a library.

words.tr:
n. 弹弓；石弩；弹射器
v. 用弩炮（等）发射；（使）突然处于…情况
words.ex: The boys used a catapult to launch stones.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们用投石机发射石头。
words.en: A catapult is a device used to throw or hurl a projectile a great distance without the aid of explosive devices—particularly various types of ancient and medieval siege engines. In a more modern context, it can also refer to a device that launches aircraft from a ship, or metaphorically, to propel someone to fame or success suddenly.

words.tr: n. 回路；环行；电路；巡回；
words.ex: The battery connects to the circuit to make the light work.
words.ex_cn: 电池连接到回路，使灯亮起来。
words.en: A circuit is a roughly circular line, route, or movement that starts and finishes at the same place. It can also refer to the complete path that an electric current travels along.

words.ex: The circumference of the circle is 31.4 cm.
words.ex_cn: 这个圆的周长是31.4厘米。
words.en: The circumference of a circle is the distance around it.

words.ex: They collaborate to finish the project.
words.ex_cn: 他们合作完成这个项目。
words.en: to work jointly with others or together especially in an intellectual endeavor

words.tr:
v. 防止；战斗；抑制；
n. 战斗；
words.ex: The new law aims to combat pollution.
words.ex_cn: 这项新法律旨在防止污染。
words.en: Combat refers to fighting, especially during a war. It can also mean to try to stop something harmful from happening or increasing.

words.ex: They cooperate to finish the project on time.
words.ex_cn: 他们合作以按时完成项目。
words.en: If you cooperate with someone, you work with them or help them for a particular purpose.

words.tr:
n. 相反；
adj. 相反的；
words.ex: The contrary of hot is cold.
words.ex_cn: 热的相反是冷。
words.en: If you say that something is true contrary to other people's beliefs or opinions, you are emphasizing that it is true and that they are wrong.

words.tr: n. 对应物；相当之物；副本；
words.ex: The CEO's counterpart in China signed the agreement.
words.ex_cn: 中国方面的对应人物签署了协议。
words.en: Someone's or something's counterpart is another person or thing that has a similar function or position in a different place.

words.tr:
n. 下降；衰退；
v. 下降；衰退；
words.ex: There was a sharp decline in sales last month.
words.ex_cn: 上个月销售额大幅下降。
words.en: If something declines, it becomes less in quantity, importance, or strength.

words.ex: The train will derail if the tracks are broken.
words.ex_cn: 如果铁轨损坏，火车就会脱轨。
words.en: To cause a train or other vehicle to leave its tracks accidentally; to divert or cause to deviate from an intended course.

words.ex: The sun can dehydrate your skin quickly.
words.ex_cn: 太阳会很快使你的皮肤脱水。
words.en: To dehydrate something means to remove all the water from it, often in order to preserve it. If you dehydrate, you lose too much water from your body, usually because of illness or extreme heat.

words.ex: The president will declare a holiday next week.
words.ex_cn: 总统将在下周宣布放假。
words.en: If you declare something, you state it formally, publicly, or officially.

words.tr:
n. 离婚；
v. 和…离婚；
words.ex: They filed for divorce after ten years of marriage.
words.ex_cn: 他们结婚十年后申请了离婚。
words.en: Divorce is the formal ending of a marriage by law.

words.ex: She will divide the cake into two parts.
words.ex_cn: 她将把蛋糕分成两部分。
words.en: If you divide something, you separate it into two or more parts.

words.ex: The dialogue in the movie was very funny.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影中的对白非常幽默。
words.en: A dialogue is a conversation between two or more people in a book, play, or film.

words.ex: He showed distaste for loud noises.
words.ex_cn: 他对嘈杂的声音感到反感。
words.en: If you feel distaste for someone or something, you dislike them and consider them to be unpleasant, unattractive, or morally unacceptable.

words.ex: Can you differentiate between the two colors?
words.ex_cn: 你能区分这两种颜色吗？
words.en: To differentiate means to recognize or express the difference between things or people.

words.ex: The teacher will distribute the books to students.
words.ex_cn: 老师将把书分发给学生。
words.en: If you distribute things, you hand them or deliver them to a number of people.

words.tr:
n. 伪装；伪装物；
v. 伪装；掩饰；
words.ex: He wore a hat and glasses as a disguise.
words.ex_cn: 他戴了帽子和眼镜作为伪装。
words.en: To disguise means to change your appearance or behavior so that people will not recognize you, or to make something seem different from what it really is.

words.ex: The company plans to enlarge its office space.
words.ex_cn: 公司计划扩大其办公空间。
words.en: To make something bigger or more extensive.

words.tr: v. 使遭危险或伤害；危害；危及
words.ex: Pollution can endanger animals.
words.ex_cn: 污染会危及动物。
words.en: To put someone or something at risk or in danger.

words.ex: The epidemic spread quickly across the country.
words.ex_cn: 这种流行病迅速蔓延到全国。
words.en: An epidemic is a large number of cases of an infectious disease occurring at the same time.

words.ex: The book opens with an epigraph from a famous philosopher.
words.ex_cn: 这本书以一位著名哲学家的题词开篇。
words.en: An epigraph is a short quotation or saying at the beginning of a book or chapter, intended to suggest its theme.

words.ex: He believes in eugenic ideas to improve humans.
words.ex_cn: 他相信优生学理念来改善人类。
words.en: Relating to the study or practice of improving the genetic quality of the human population.

words.ex: He used a euphemism to say he lost his job.
words.ex_cn: 他用了一个委婉语来表示他失业了。
words.en: A euphemism is a polite word or expression that is used to refer to things which people may find upsetting or embarrassing to talk about.

words.ex: The exterior of the house is painted white.
words.ex_cn: 这所房子的外观是白色的。
words.en: The outer surface or structure of something.

words.tr:
n. 交换；兑换；交易所；
v. 交换；
words.ex: They made an exchange of books.
words.ex_cn: 他们进行了书籍的交换。
words.en: If you exchange something, you give it to someone and receive something else in return.

words.ex: He pointed at the map with his forefinger.
words.ex_cn: 他用食指指着地图。
words.en: The forefinger is the finger next to the thumb; it is the index finger.

words.tr: n. 先见；预见；先见之明
words.ex: He showed foresight by saving money for the future.
words.ex_cn: 他通过为未来存钱展现了远见。
words.en: The ability to predict or the action of predicting what will happen or be needed in the future.

words.ex: He has hypertension and takes medicine every day.
words.ex_cn: 他有高血压，每天吃药。
words.en: Hypertension is a condition in which the force of the blood against the artery walls is too high.

words.tr: adj. 过敏的；易受冒犯的
words.ex: He is hypersensitive to pollen and gets sneezing easily.
words.ex_cn: 他对花粉过敏，容易打喷嚏。
words.en: If someone is hypersensitive, they are extremely sensitive to certain situations or to the behaviour of other people, often reacting in an exaggerated or extreme way.

words.ex: Hypotension can lead to dizziness and fainting.
words.ex_cn: 血压过低可能导致头晕和昏厥。
words.en: Hypotension is a condition in which a person's blood pressure is abnormally low, which can lead to symptoms such as dizziness and fainting.

words.ex: The small boat docked at the inlet.
words.ex_cn: 小船停靠在小水湾。
words.en: An inlet is a narrow strip of water that leads from a sea or lake into the land or between islands.

words.ex: The company wants to innovate its production process.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司想改革它的生产流程。
words.en: To innovate means to introduce changes and new ideas in the way something is done or made.

words.ex: It is impossible to finish the race in five minutes.
words.ex_cn: 五分钟内完成比赛是不可能的。
words.en: If something is impossible, it cannot be done or cannot happen.

words.ex: This product is inferior to the other one.
words.ex_cn: 这个产品比另一个差。
words.en: If one person or thing is inferior to another, they are not as good, important, or valuable as the other person or thing.

words.ex: The city needs better infrastructure for roads and water.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市需要更好的道路和供水设施。
words.en: The basic physical and organizational structures and facilities (e.g., buildings, roads, power supplies) needed for the operation of a society or enterprise.

words.ex: He works for an international company.
words.ex_cn: 他在一家国际公司工作。
words.en: International means involving or relating to more than one country.

words.tr: n. 独白；独角戏；长篇大论
words.ex: He gave a monologue on stage.
words.ex_cn: 他在舞台上发表了一段独白。
words.en: A monologue is a long speech by one person, especially in a play or film, or a long speech by one person during a conversation.

words.ex: The boy rides a monocycle in the park.
words.ex_cn: 这个男孩在公园里骑独轮车。
words.en: A monocycle is a vehicle with a single wheel, typically ridden for entertainment or sport.

words.ex: He lost his keys by a mischance.
words.ex_cn: 他不小心弄丢了钥匙。
words.en: An unlucky event or accident.

words.ex: He mistrusts strangers who ask for money.
words.ex_cn: 他不信任向他要钱的陌生人。
words.en: Mistrust is the feeling that you cannot trust someone or something.

words.tr:
adj. 多媒体的；
n. 多媒体；
words.ex: The school uses multimedia tools to teach students.
words.ex_cn: 这所学校使用多媒体工具来教学。
words.en: Multimedia is the use of computers to present text, graphics, video, animation, and sound in an integrated way.

words.ex: The multinational company has offices in five countries.
words.ex_cn: 这家跨国公司在五个国家设有办事处。
words.en: A multinational company or business operates in several different countries.

words.tr: adj. 使用多种语言的；说多种语言的；
words.ex: He is a multilingual teacher who speaks three languages.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位会说三种语言的多语言教师。
words.en: Using or able to use several languages.

words.ex: He is nonaligned with any political party.
words.ex_cn: 他不属于任何政党。
words.en: Not allied with any other nation or group; neutral.

words.ex: The king oppresses the poor people.
words.ex_cn: 国王压迫穷人。
words.en: If someone oppresses people, they treat them cruelly or unfairly and prevent them from having the same rights as other people.

words.tr:
n. 物体；
v. 反对；
words.ex: The ball is a simple object.
words.ex_cn: 球是一个简单的物体。
words.en: An object is a thing that you can see or touch but that is not usually a living animal, plant, or person.

words.ex: The outbreak of the flu surprised everyone.
words.ex_cn: 流感的爆发让所有人都感到惊讶。
words.en: An outbreak of something unpleasant, such as violence or a disease, is a sudden occurrence of it.

words.ex: We had an outdoor picnic last Sunday.
words.ex_cn: 上个星期天我们进行了户外野餐。
words.en: relating to or done in the open air; not inside a building

words.ex: He outperforms his classmates in math tests.
words.ex_cn: 他在数学考试中表现优于同学。
words.en: To perform better than someone or something else.

words.tr:
n. 溢出；
v. 泛滥；
words.ex: The rain caused an overflow of the river.
words.ex_cn: 雨水导致河水溢出。
words.en: If a liquid or a river overflows, it flows over the edges of the container or place it is in.

words.ex: The car drove under the overpass.
words.ex_cn: 汽车从立交桥下开过。
words.en: An overpass is a bridge that carries one road or railway line over another.

words.ex: The sky is overcast today.
words.ex_cn: 今天天空多云。
words.en: If the sky or the day is overcast, it is covered with cloud; dull and not sunny.

words.tr:
adj. 平行的；
n. 类似的事物；
words.ex: The two lines are parallel and never meet.
words.ex_cn: 这两条线是平行的，永远不会相交。
words.en: Something that is parallel to something else is similar to it in many ways, or happens at the same time as it.

words.ex: He paraphrased the poem in simple words.
words.ex_cn: 他用简单的语言意译了这首诗。
words.en: To paraphrase means to express the meaning of something written or spoken using different words, especially to achieve greater clarity.

words.tr: n. 阳伞; n. （Parasol）人名；（法）帕拉索尔
words.ex: She holds a parasol to shade herself from the sun.
words.ex_cn: 她撑着一把阳伞来遮挡阳光。
words.en: A parasol is an object like an umbrella that provides shade from the sun.

words.ex: They found paradise on a small island.
words.ex_cn: 他们在一个小岛上找到了天堂。
words.en: Paradise is a place of ideal beauty or loveliness, or a state of supreme happiness.

words.ex: He made a permanent change to his lifestyle.
words.ex_cn: 他对自己的生活方式做出了永久的改变。
words.en: Something that is permanent exists or happens all the time, or exists for a long time without changing.

words.tr: adj. 不忠的；背信弃义的
words.ex: The perfidious traitor betrayed his comrades.
words.ex_cn: 那个背信弃义的叛徒背叛了他的同伙。
words.en: If you describe someone as perfidious, you mean that they have betrayed someone or cannot be trusted.

words.ex: He drew a pentagon, which is a polygon.
words.ex_cn: 他画了一个五边形，它是一个多边形。
words.en: A polygon is a flat shape with three or more straight sides and angles.

words.tr:
adj. 多种语言的；通晓数种语言的
n. 通晓数种语言的人
words.ex: He is a polyglot who speaks five languages.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位会说五种语言的多语者。
words.en: A polyglot is a person who knows and is able to use several languages.

words.ex: The postwar economy grew quickly.
words.ex_cn: 战后经济迅速增长。
words.en: occurring or existing after a war

words.tr:
n. 研究生；
adj. 大学毕业后的；
words.ex: He is a postgraduate at Beijing University.
words.ex_cn: 他是北京大学的一名研究生。
words.en: A postgraduate is a student who continues studying after obtaining a first degree, usually in order to obtain a higher qualification.

words.ex: The weather prediction says it will rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 天气预测说明天会下雨。
words.en: A prediction is a statement about what you think will happen in the future.

words.ex: The book begins with a short prologue.
words.ex_cn: 这本书以一个简短的序言开始。
words.en: A prologue is an introduction to a book, play, or other written work that sets the scene or provides background information.

words.tr:
n. 返回；归还；
v. 返回；归还；
words.ex: The return of the train was delayed.
words.ex_cn: 火车的返回被推迟了。
words.en: To go or come back to a place or person. To give, send, or put something back to its original place or condition.

words.ex: We can reuse plastic bottles to reduce waste.
words.ex_cn: 我们可以再使用塑料瓶来减少浪费。
words.en: To use something again after it has been used once.

words.ex: I asked for a refund after the product broke.
words.ex_cn: 产品坏了之后，我要求退款。
words.en: A refund is a sum of money that is returned to you, for example because you have paid too much or because you have returned goods to a shop.

words.ex: The rebel fought against the king's rules.
words.ex_cn: 这位叛逆者反抗国王的法令。
words.en: A rebel is a person who opposes or fights against people in authority.

words.tr:
adj. 分开的；分离的；单独的；
v. 分离；隔离；
words.ex: They live in separate houses.
words.ex_cn: 他们住在分开的房子里。
words.en: To cause to move or be apart; to divide or keep apart.

words.ex: I take the subway to work every day.
words.ex_cn: 我每天坐地铁去上班。
words.en: An underground railway system in a city, usually operated by electricity, which provides a rapid means of transportation.

words.ex: The subtropic climate is warm and dry.
words.ex_cn: 亚热带气候温暖而干燥。
words.en: relating to or characteristic of regions adjacent to or bordering on the tropics

words.ex: The subeditor checked the article for any grammatical errors.
words.ex_cn: 副编辑检查了文章中的语法错误。
words.en: A subeditor is a person who assists the main editor in preparing text for publication, often by checking for errors and ensuring clarity.

words.ex: China is a superpower in the 21st century.
words.ex_cn: 中国是21世纪的一个超级大国。
words.en: A superpower is a country that has the ability to influence events or project power on a worldwide scale, often due to its economic, military, and cultural strength.

words.ex: The supreme leader makes the final decision.
words.ex_cn: 至上的领导人做出最终决定。
words.en: If you say that something is supreme, you mean that it is the most important or the best of its kind.

words.ex: The garden has superabundant flowers in spring.
words.ex_cn: 春天，这个花园里花朵非常多。
words.en: Exceeding what is necessary or normal; excessively abundant.

words.ex: I feel sympathy for the poor children.
words.ex_cn: 我对那些可怜的孩子感到同情。
words.en: If you have sympathy for someone who is in a bad situation, you are sorry for them, and show this in the way you behave towards them.

words.ex: He listened to a beautiful symphony last night.
words.ex_cn: 他昨晚听了一首美妙的交响乐。
words.en: A symphony is a long piece of music that is usually in four parts and is performed by an orchestra.

words.ex: He can translate words into pictures.
words.ex_cn: 他能把词语转化为图画。
words.en: To translate means to change written or spoken words from one language into another, or to explain something in a way that is easier to understand.

words.tr:
n. 运输；
v. 运输；
words.ex: He uses public transport to go to work.
words.ex_cn: 他乘坐公共交通去上班。
words.en: To transport something or someone is to move them from one place to another, especially over long distances.

words.tr: adj. 不快乐的；不高兴的；
words.ex: He looked unhappy after losing the game.
words.ex_cn: 他输掉比赛后看起来不快乐。
words.en: If you are unhappy, you are sad and depressed.

words.ex: The small mistake was unimportant.
words.ex_cn: 这个小错误不重要。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as unimportant, you mean that they do not have much influence, effect, or value, and are therefore not worth serious consideration.

words.tr:
adj. 地下的；
n. 地铁；地下；
adv. 在地下；
words.ex: The underground tunnel connects two buildings.
words.ex_cn: 这条地下的隧道连接了两座建筑。
words.en: Something that is underground is below the surface of the ground. It can also refer to secret activities or organizations.

words.ex: He underestimated the difficulty of the test.
words.ex_cn: 他低估了考试的难度。
words.en: If you underestimate something, you do not realize how large, great, or serious it is.

words.ex: He withdrew $100 from the ATM.
words.ex_cn: 他从自动取款机里提取了100美元。
words.en: If you withdraw something from a place, you remove it or take it away.

words.tr:
adj. 一致的；统一的；
n. 制服；
words.ex: The students wear a uniform shirt to school.
words.ex_cn: 学生们穿一致的衬衫去学校。
words.en: A uniform is a special set of clothes which some people, for example soldiers or the police, wear to work in and which some children wear at school. It is also used to describe something that is the same in all parts and does not vary.

words.ex: He has a dual role as teacher and coach.
words.ex_cn: 他同时担任老师和教练的双重角色。
words.en: Having two parts or aspects.

words.ex: The two countries signed a bilateral agreement.
words.ex_cn: 这两个国家签署了一项双边协议。
words.en: Involving or affecting two parties, countries, etc.

words.ex: The triangle has three sides.
words.ex_cn: 这个三角形有三条边。
words.en: A triangle is a shape consisting of three straight lines and three angles.

words.tr:
v. 成为三倍；使增至三倍；
n. 三倍的数；三个一组；
adj. 三部分的；
words.ex: The company's profits tripled last year.
words.ex_cn: 该公司去年的利润增长了三倍。
words.en: To triple something means to make it three times as much in size or number.

words.ex: The captain sailed the ship across the ocean.
words.ex_cn: 船长驾驶船穿越了海洋。
words.en: A captain is the person in charge of a ship or an aircraft, or a leader of a team or group.

words.tr:
adj. 美国的；美洲的；
n. 美国人；美洲人；
words.ex: She bought an American car.
words.ex_cn: 她买了一辆美国车。
words.en: relating to the United States of America or its people, culture, or language

words.tr: n. 孤儿；失去生母的幼小动物
words.ex: The boy lives with his uncle because he is an orphan.
words.ex_cn: 这个男孩和叔叔住在一起，因为他是个孤儿。
words.en: An orphan is a child whose parents are dead.

words.tr:
n. 素食者；食草动物；
adj. 素食者的；素菜的；
words.ex: He is a vegetarian and doesn't eat meat.
words.ex_cn: 他是一名素食者，不吃肉。
words.en: A vegetarian is someone who does not eat meat or fish, and sometimes other animal products, especially for moral, religious, or health reasons.

words.ex: He works as an accountant in a small company.
words.ex_cn: 他在一家小公司当会计师。
words.en: An accountant is a person whose job is to keep, inspect, and analyze financial accounts.

words.ex: He is a liar because he told a lie.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个骗子，因为他撒了谎。
words.en: A liar is someone who tells lies.

words.ex: The beggar sat on the street with a cup.
words.ex_cn: 那个乞丐坐在街上，手里拿着一个杯子。
words.en: A beggar is a person who lives by asking people for money or food.

words.ex: The secretary types letters for the manager.
words.ex_cn: 秘书为经理打字。
words.en: A secretary is a person whose job is to do office work, such as typing letters, answering phone calls, and arranging meetings.

words.tr:
n. 提倡者；
v. 提倡；
words.ex: He is an advocate for clean water.
words.ex_cn: 他是清洁用水的提倡者。
words.en: If you advocate a particular action or plan, you recommend it publicly.

words.ex: He is a candidate for the mayor position.
words.ex_cn: 他是市长职位的候选人。
words.en: A candidate is someone who is being considered for a position, for example someone who is running in an election or applying for a job.

words.ex: He is the nominee for best actor.
words.ex_cn: 他是最佳男演员的提名人。
words.en: A nominee is someone who is proposed for an official position or for an honour or award.

words.ex: He is an engineer who builds bridges.
words.ex_cn: 他是一名建造桥梁的工程师。
words.en: An engineer is a person who designs, builds, or maintains engines, machines, or public works.

words.tr:
n. 志愿者；
v. 自愿做；
words.ex: He is a volunteer at the local hospital.
words.ex_cn: 他是当地医院的一名志愿者。
words.en: A volunteer is someone who does work without being paid for it, especially work that involves helping people.

words.tr:
n. 业余爱好者；
adj. 业余的；
words.ex: He is an amateur who paints on weekends.
words.ex_cn: 他是个周末画画的业余爱好者。
words.en: An amateur is someone who does something as a hobby and not as a job.

words.ex: The lawyer helped her client with the contract.
words.ex_cn: 律师帮助她的客户处理合同。
words.en: A client is a person or organization receiving services or advice from a professional or company.

words.ex: The student reads a book every day.
words.ex_cn: 这个学生每天读书。
words.en: A student is a person who is studying at a university or college.

words.ex: The princess lived in a big castle.
words.ex_cn: 公主住在一座大城堡里。
words.en: A princess is a female member of a royal family, especially a daughter or granddaughter of a king and queen, or the wife of a prince.

words.ex: The actress sings in the movie.
words.ex_cn: 这位女演员在电影中唱歌。
words.en: An actress is a woman whose profession is acting on the stage, in films, or on television.

words.ex: The waitress brought us water and menus.
words.ex_cn: 女服务员给我们端来了水和菜单。
words.en: A waitress is a woman who works in a restaurant, serving food and drink to customers.

words.tr:
n. 理想主义者；唯心论者
adj. 唯心主义的
words.ex: He is an idealist who believes in world peace.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个相信世界和平的理想主义者。
words.en: An idealist is someone who believes that very good things can be achieved, often when this does not seem likely to others.

words.ex: The journalist wrote a story about the earthquake.
words.ex_cn: 记者写了一篇关于地震的文章。
words.en: A journalist is a person whose job is to collect news and write about it for newspapers, magazines, television, or radio.

words.tr: n. 检查员；巡视员；视察员；
words.ex: The inspector checked the building for safety.
words.ex_cn: 检查员检查了建筑物的安全性。
words.en: An inspector is a person whose job is to inspect something.

words.ex: The teacher helps students with math.
words.ex_cn: 老师帮助学生学习数学。
words.en: A teacher is a person whose job is to teach in a school or college.

words.ex: The gangster stole money from the bank.
words.ex_cn: 这个黑帮分子偷了银行的钱。
words.en: A gangster is a member of a group of violent criminals.

words.ex: The youngster rode his bike to school every day.
words.ex_cn: 这个年轻人每天骑自行车去上学。
words.en: A youngster is a young person, especially a child or teenager.

words.ex: An icicle hangs from the roof.
words.ex_cn: 一个冰锥挂在屋顶上。
words.en: An icicle is a pointed piece of ice that is formed when dripping water freezes, typically hanging from a surface.

words.ex: Dust particles float in the air.
words.ex_cn: 灰尘微粒漂浮在空气中。
words.en: A particle is a very small piece or amount of something.

words.ex: She took a tiny morsel of cake and savored it slowly.
words.ex_cn: 她咬了一小口蛋糕，慢慢地品味着。
words.en: A morsel is a small piece or amount of something, especially food.

words.ex: The fishing vessel sailed out at dawn.
words.ex_cn: 那艘渔船在黎明时出海。
words.en: A vessel is a large boat or a container for holding liquids.

words.ex: He picked up a small pebble from the ground.
words.ex_cn: 他从地上捡起了一颗小石子。
words.en: A pebble is a small, smooth, round stone, especially one found on a beach or in a river.

words.ex: He bought a cigarette at the store.
words.ex_cn: 他在商店买了一支香烟。
words.en: A cigarette is a small roll of finely cut tobacco for smoking, enclosed in a wrapper of thin paper.

words.ex: He read the booklet about the new rules.
words.ex_cn: 他读了那本关于新规则的小册子。
words.en: A booklet is a small, thin book that has a paper cover and that gives you information about something.

words.ex: The boy lives in an orphanage.
words.ex_cn: 这个男孩住在孤儿院。
words.en: An orphanage is a place where children who have lost their parents or who have been abandoned by them are cared for and live.

words.ex: He was born in a small village.
words.ex_cn: 他出生在一个小村庄。
words.en: A village is a small group of houses in the country, smaller than a town.

words.ex: He goes to the library every afternoon.
words.ex_cn: 他每天下午去图书馆。
words.en: A library is a building where books, documents, CDs, and sometimes videos and music are kept for people to read, study, or borrow.

words.ex: I bought fresh bread from the bakery.
words.ex_cn: 我从面包房买了新鲜面包。
words.en: A bakery is a place where bread, cakes, and pastries are made or sold.

words.ex: He works in a laboratory on Fridays.
words.ex_cn: 他在星期五去实验室工作。
words.en: A laboratory is a place equipped for scientific research, experiments, or teaching.

words.ex: The crowd cheered loudly at the stadium.
words.ex_cn: 观众在体育场里大声欢呼。
words.en: A stadium is a large structure for open-air sports or entertainments, consisting of a field or stage surrounded partly or completely by a tiered structure designed to allow spectators to stand or sit and view the event.

words.ex: We visited a museum last weekend.
words.ex_cn: 我们上周末参观了一个博物馆。
words.en: A museum is a building where a large number of interesting and valuable objects, such as works of art or historical items, are kept, studied, and displayed to the public.

words.tr: n. 现代主义；现代派；现代思想
words.ex: He likes modernism in art and design.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢艺术和设计中的现代主义。
words.en: Modernism is a style or movement in the arts that aims to break with classical and traditional forms.

words.ex: He called his friend a comrade.
words.ex_cn: 他称他的朋友为同志。
words.en: A comrade is a companion who shares one's activities or is a fellow member of an organization.

words.tr:
n. 阻塞；封锁
v. 封锁
words.ex: The blockade stopped all ships from entering the port.
words.ex_cn: 封锁阻止了所有船只进入港口。
words.en: A blockade is an action to prevent goods or people from entering or leaving a place.

words.ex: His attitude toward homework is very positive.
words.ex_cn: 他对作业的态度非常积极。
words.en: An attitude is a way of thinking or feeling about something, which is often reflected in a person's behavior.

words.ex: He enjoys solitude in the woods.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢在森林中独处。
words.en: The state or situation of being alone.

words.ex: He showed patience while waiting for the bus.
words.ex_cn: 他在等公交车时表现出了耐心。
words.en: The ability to stay calm and not get angry, especially when there is a difficulty or you have to wait a long time.

words.tr: n. 外观；外表；出现；露面；
words.ex: The appearance of the house surprised everyone.
words.ex_cn: 这所房子的外观让所有人都感到惊讶。
words.en: The way that someone or something looks or the act of coming into view.

words.tr:
n. 服务；
v. 保养；
words.ex: The restaurant offers excellent service.
words.ex_cn: 这家餐厅提供出色的服务。
words.en: The act of helping or doing work for someone; a system that provides something the public needs, such as transport, communications, or utilities.

words.ex: He believed his destiny was to become a doctor.
words.ex_cn: 他相信自己的命运是成为一名医生。
words.en: Destiny is the force which some people believe controls the things that happen to you in your life.

words.ex: His bravery saved the children from the fire.
words.ex_cn: 他的勇敢救了孩子们于火海之中。
words.en: Bravery is the quality of being brave; courage.

words.ex: Wearing a helmet improves your safety.
words.ex_cn: 戴头盔能提高你的安全。
words.en: Safety refers to the condition of being protected from or unlikely to cause danger, risk, or injury.

words.tr: n. 破产；倒闭；无偿付能力
words.ex: The company filed for bankruptcy last year.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司去年申请了破产。
words.en: Bankruptcy is a legal status of a person or other entity that cannot repay the debts it owes to creditors.

words.ex: He remembers his childhood as a happy time.
words.ex_cn: 他记得自己的童年是一段快乐的时光。
words.en: Childhood is the period of a person's life when they are a child.

words.ex: There is a high likelihood of rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 明天很大可能会下雨。
words.en: The likelihood of something happening is how likely it is to happen.

words.ex: The addition of a new chair made the room more comfortable.
words.ex_cn: 增加一把新椅子让房间更舒适了。
words.en: An addition is something that is added to something else, often to improve it or make it larger.

words.ex: He looked at her with suspicion.
words.ex_cn: 他带着怀疑的眼神看着她。
words.en: A feeling or thought that something is possible, likely, or true, especially something bad or wrong, without having proof.

words.tr: n. 扩展；延长期；延伸；电话分机；
words.ex: The company added an extension to its office building.
words.ex_cn: 公司为办公楼加了一个扩建部分。
words.en: An extension is a part that is added to something to make it longer or larger, or the act of adding this part.

words.ex: He has awareness of the environmental problems.
words.ex_cn: 他意识到环境问题。
words.en: Knowledge or perception of a situation or fact.

words.ex: The darkness made it hard to see the path.
words.ex_cn: 黑暗使我看不清道路。
words.en: The absence of light in a place, making it difficult or impossible to see.

words.tr: n. 运动；动作；活动；乐章；
words.ex: The movement of the sun changes the shadow.
words.ex_cn: 太阳的运动改变了影子。
words.en: The act or process of moving or being moved; a change of position or place.

words.ex: The company made a statement about the new policy.
words.ex_cn: 公司就新政策发布了一项声明。
words.en: A statement is something that you say or write which gives information in a formal or definite way.

words.ex: He faced many hardships during the war.
words.ex_cn: 他在战争期间经历了许多困苦。
words.en: Hardship refers to a situation that is difficult to endure because of lack of money, resources, or other basic necessities.

words.tr: n. 领导才能；领导地位；
words.ex: His leadership helped the team win the match.
words.ex_cn: 他的领导才能帮助团队赢得了比赛。
words.en: Leadership is the ability to lead, guide, or direct a group, organization, or country.

words.ex: He felt sad after the failure of his business.
words.ex_cn: 他的生意失败后，他感到很难过。
words.en: The lack of success in achieving or doing something.

words.ex: The recipe calls for a mixture of flour and water.
words.ex_cn: 这个食谱需要一种面粉和水的混合物。
words.en: A mixture is a substance made by combining other substances together.

words.ex: His behavior at the party was very polite.
words.ex_cn: 他在派对上的举止非常礼貌。
words.en: The way in which one acts or conducts oneself, especially towards others.

words.ex: His humor makes everyone laugh.
words.ex_cn: 他的幽默让大家都笑了。
words.en: The quality of being amusing or comic, especially as expressed in literature or speech.

words.ex: The stars are visible at night.
words.ex_cn: 夜晚可以看到星星。
words.en: If something is visible, it can be seen.

words.ex: The water is drinkable after boiling.
words.ex_cn: 水煮沸后可以饮用。
words.en: If a liquid is drinkable, it is safe or suitable to drink.

words.ex: The national flag flies high every morning.
words.ex_cn: 每天早上国旗都高高飘扬。
words.en: relating to or characteristic of a nation; common to a whole nation

words.ex: The arrival of the train was delayed by 20 minutes.
words.ex_cn: 火车的到达晚了20分钟。
words.en: The act of coming to a place or the moment when something or someone arrives.

words.ex: The teacher gave her approval for the project.
words.ex_cn: 老师对这个项目表示了赞成。
words.en: If you give your approval to something, you agree with it or allow it to happen.

words.ex: His refusal to apologize made everyone angry.
words.ex_cn: 他拒绝道歉，让所有人都生气了。
words.en: The act of refusing to do something or to accept something.

words.tr:
n. 病人；
adj. 有耐心的；
words.ex: The doctor helped the patient feel better.
words.ex_cn: 医生帮助病人感觉好些了。
words.en: A patient person is able to wait for a long time or deal with a difficult situation without becoming angry or upset.

words.tr: adj. 卓越的；极好的；明亮的；灿烂的；
words.ex: He gave a brilliant answer to the math question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这道数学题给出了卓越的回答。
words.en: A brilliant person, idea, or performance is extremely clever or skilful.

words.tr: adj. 考虑周到的；体贴的；
words.ex: He is considerate and always asks if others need help.
words.ex_cn: 他很体贴，总是问别人是否需要帮助。
words.en: Someone who is considerate pays attention to the needs, wishes, or feelings of other people.

words.ex: The clock shows accurate time.
words.ex_cn: 这个钟显示的时间很精确。
words.en: Correct in all details; exact.

words.ex: Be careful when you cross the street.
words.ex_cn: 过马路时要小心。
words.en: If you are careful, you give serious attention to what you are doing, in order to avoid harm, damage, or mistakes.

words.ex: She is a beautiful girl.
words.ex_cn: 她是一个美丽的女孩。
words.en: Pleasing the senses or mind aesthetically.

words.tr:
adj. 典范的；典型的；
n. 文学经典；名著；优秀的典范；
words.ex: This movie is a classic comedy.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影是一部典范的喜剧。
words.en: A classic is something that is judged to be of the highest quality and outstanding of its kind.

words.ex: This is a basic math skill.
words.ex_cn: 这是一个基本的数学技能。
words.en: You use basic to describe things, activities, and principles that are very important or necessary, and on which others depend.

words.tr:
adj. 固体的；坚固的；可靠的；
n. 固体；
words.ex: Ice is a solid form of water.
words.ex_cn: 冰是水的固体形式。
words.en: A solid substance or object stays the same shape whether it is in a container or not.

words.tr:
n. 液体；
adj. 液态的；
words.ex: Water is a common liquid.
words.ex_cn: 水是一种常见的液体。
words.en: A liquid is a substance which is not solid but which flows and can be poured, for example water.

words.tr: adj. （女人）似男人的; 男子般的; 有男子特性的; 男子气的
words.ex: Her mannish haircut made her look more like a boy than a girl.
words.ex_cn: 她那男子气的发型使她看起来更像男孩而不是女孩。
words.en: If you describe a woman as mannish, you mean that her appearance or behavior are like those of a man.

words.tr: adj. 女人似的；娘娘腔的
words.ex: He was criticized for his womanish mannerisms.
words.ex_cn: adj. 他因为娘娘腔的举止而受到批评。
words.en: resembling or characteristic of a woman, especially in being weak, timid, or overly refined.

words.tr: adj. 选择性的；精挑细选的；
words.ex: He is selective about what he eats.
words.ex_cn: 他对吃的东西很挑剔。
words.en: If you are selective, you choose things carefully, for example, the things that you buy or do.

words.tr: adj. 有竞争力的；竞争的；
words.ex: She is a competitive runner who wins many races.
words.ex_cn: 她是一个有竞争力的跑步者，赢得了许多比赛。
words.en: Competitive is used to describe situations or activities in which people or firms compete with each other.

words.ex: He had a sleepless night because of the noise.
words.ex_cn: 因为噪音，他彻夜未眠。
words.en: If you are sleepless, you are unable to sleep.

words.ex: He made a careless mistake on the test.
words.ex_cn: 他在考试中犯了一个粗心的错误。
words.en: If you are careless, you do not pay enough attention to what you are doing, and so you make mistakes, or cause harm or damage.

words.ex: He did voluntary work at the hospital.
words.ex_cn: 他在医院做志愿工作。
words.en: If something is voluntary, you do it because you choose to, and not because you have to.

words.ex: The teacher gave a satisfactory grade.
words.ex_cn: 老师给了一个令人满意的分数。
words.en: If something is satisfactory, it is good enough or acceptable.

words.ex: The cake tastes delicious.
words.ex_cn: 这个蛋糕味道很美味。
words.en: If you describe food or drink as delicious, you mean that it has a very pleasant taste.

words.tr: adj. 话多的；健谈的；喋喋不休的
words.ex: He is a loquacious man who talks all day.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个整天喋喋不休的人。
words.en: If you describe someone as loquacious, you mean that they talk a lot.

words.ex: He is a handsome boy.
words.ex_cn: 他是个英俊的男孩。
words.en: A handsome man is good-looking, usually in a way that is attractive to women. Something that is handsome is large in quantity or impressive in quality.

words.tr: adj. 令人烦恼的；讨厌的；
words.ex: The noisy neighbors are troublesome.
words.ex_cn: 那些吵闹的邻居令人烦恼。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as troublesome, you mean that they cause you a lot of problems or worries.

words.ex: The slow internet frustrates me.
words.ex_cn: 慢速的网络让我感到沮丧。
words.en: If something frustrates you, it upsets or angers you because you are unable to deal with the problems it creates.

words.ex: They will nominate her for the award.
words.ex_cn: 他们将提名她获得这个奖项。
words.en: If someone is nominated for a job or position, their name is formally suggested as a candidate for it.

words.ex: The fire blackened the pot.
words.ex_cn: 火把锅烧黑了。
words.en: To make or become black or dark, especially by the action of fire, smoke, or dirt; to defame someone's character.

words.ex: She tried to whiten her teeth with a special toothpaste.
words.ex_cn: 她尝试用一种特殊的牙膏使牙齿变白。
words.en: To make or become white or whiter.

words.ex: She will beautify her garden with flowers.
words.ex_cn: 她将用花朵美化她的花园。
words.en: To make something more attractive or beautiful.

words.ex: The machine purifies water by removing dirt.
words.ex_cn: 这台机器通过去除杂质来净化水。
words.en: To purify something means to make it clean and pure by removing dirty or harmful substances from it.

words.ex: The country wants to industrialize quickly.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家想快速工业化。
words.en: To industrialize means to develop industry in a country or region on a wide scale.

words.ex: They want to commercialize the new app.
words.ex_cn: 他们想将这个新应用商业化。
words.en: To commercialize something means to organize or develop it in such a way that it becomes intended to make a profit.

words.ex: He wavers when choosing between two jobs.
words.ex_cn: 他在两个工作之间摇摆不定。
words.en: If you waver, you cannot decide about something or you are uncertain about what you should do.

words.tr: v. 蹒跚；踉跄；摇摇欲坠
words.ex: The old man totters when he walks.
words.ex_cn: 这位老人走路时摇摇晃晃。
words.en: To move in a feeble or unsteady way.

words.tr:
n. 闪光；闪烁；活力
v. 闪光；焕发活力
words.ex: The diamond showed a tiny sparkle in the sunlight.
words.ex_cn: 钻石在阳光下显示出一丝闪光。
words.en: If something sparkles, it shines brightly with a lot of small points of light.

words.ex: The loud noise startle the bird.
words.ex_cn: 巨大的噪音惊动了那只鸟。
words.en: If something or someone startles you, they surprise and frighten you slightly.

words.ex: The noise will diminish after midnight.
words.ex_cn: 午夜后噪音会减少。
words.en: If something diminishes, or if something diminishes it, it becomes reduced in size, importance, or intensity.

words.tr: v. 布置家具；配备；供给；提供
words.ex: He will furnish the apartment with new furniture.
words.ex_cn: 他将为公寓配备新家具。
words.en: To furnish a place means to put furniture and other things into it.

words.ex: He hardly ate anything at dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他晚餐几乎没吃东西。
words.en: You use hardly to modify a statement when you want to emphasize that it is only a small amount or degree which is true, or that it is not true at all.

words.ex: He barely slept last night.
words.ex_cn: 他昨晚几乎没睡觉。
words.en: You use barely to say that something is only just true or only just the case.

words.tr:
adv. 向下地；
adj. 向下的；
words.ex: The leaves fell downward slowly.
words.ex_cn: 树叶慢慢向下飘落。
words.en: Moving or leading towards a lower place or level

words.tr:
adv. 向上地；
adj. 向上的；
words.ex: The balloon moved upward slowly.
words.ex_cn: 气球缓慢地向上移动。
words.en: Moving or directed toward a higher place or level.

words.ex: His rude words detract from the beauty of the speech.
words.ex_cn: 他粗鲁的话贬损了演讲的优美。
words.en: If one thing detracts from another, it makes it seem less good or impressive.

words.ex: He tries to protract the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他试图延长会议。
words.en: To protract something means to make it last longer than usual or necessary, often in a way that is annoying or inconvenient.

words.ex: The problem is intractable and no one can solve it.
words.ex_cn: 这个问题很难处理，没人能解决。
words.en: If you describe a problem or a person as intractable, you mean that it is very difficult to deal with or to change.

words.ex: He tried to retract his words after the argument.
words.ex_cn: 他在争吵后试图收回他的话。
words.en: If you retract something that you have said or written, you say that you did not mean it.

words.ex: Subtract 5 from 10 to get 5.
words.ex_cn: 从10中减去5得到5。
words.en: If you subtract one number from another, you take the first number away from the second.

words.tr:
n. 合同；契约；
v. 收缩；
words.ex: They signed a contract to buy the house.
words.ex_cn: 他们签署了一份购买房子的合同。
words.en: A contract is a legal agreement between two or more parties. It can also mean to become smaller or tighter, or to catch a disease.

words.tr:
v. 提取；
n. 摘录；提取物；
words.ex: They extract oil from plants.
words.ex_cn: 他们从植物中提取油。
words.en: To remove or take out something, especially by effort or force.

words.ex: He never derogates his colleagues.
words.ex_cn: 他从不贬低他的同事。
words.en: To derogate means to take away from something, especially in a way that is unfair or undeserved. It can also mean to detract from the value or importance of something.

words.ex: The car depreciates every year.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车每年都会贬值。
words.en: If something such as a currency depreciates or if something depreciates it, it loses some of its original value.

words.ex: The president may be impeached for lying.
words.ex_cn: 总统可能因撒谎而被弹劾。
words.en: If a government official is impeached, they are formally charged with a serious crime in a special government court.

words.tr: n. 弹劾；控告；怀疑；指摘
words.ex: The president faced impeachment for breaking the law.
words.ex_cn: 总统因违法而面临弹劾。
words.en: Impeachment is a formal process in which an official is accused of unlawful activity, the outcome of which, depending on the country, may include the removal of that official from office as well as criminal or civil punishment.

words.tr:
v. 会谈；谈判
n. 会谈；谈判
words.ex: The two sides agreed to parley in order to resolve their differences.
words.ex_cn: 双方同意进行会谈以解决分歧。
words.en: A parley is a discussion between two opposing sides in a conflict, especially a discussion of terms for a truce.

words.ex: The two sides started negotiation to solve the conflict.
words.ex_cn: 双方开始了谈判以解决冲突。
words.en: Negotiation is a discussion aimed at reaching an agreement.

words.ex: He will perjure himself in court.
words.ex_cn: 他将在法庭上作伪证。
words.en: If someone perjures themselves in a court of law, they lie, even though they have promised to tell the truth.

words.tr: vt. 恳请，恳求；起誓；（以起誓或诅咒等形式）命令
words.ex: She adjured him to tell the truth.
words.ex_cn: 她恳求他讲出真相。
words.en: If you adjure someone to do something, you earnestly request or command them to do it.

words.ex: The wizard conjure a fireball with ancient words.
words.ex_cn: 巫师用古老的咒语召唤出一个火球。
words.en: If you conjure something out of nothing, you make it appear as if by magic.

words.tr: v. 公开放弃；发誓断绝
words.ex: He had to abjure his old beliefs.
words.ex_cn: 他不得不放弃他的旧信仰。
words.en: If you abjure something such as a belief or way of life, you state publicly that you will give it up or that you reject it.

words.ex: He was charged with perjury after lying in court.
words.ex_cn: 他在法庭上撒谎后被控伪证罪。
words.en: The crime of telling a lie in a court of law after having sworn to tell the truth.

words.ex: The coach endorses the new player.
words.ex_cn: 教练支持这位新球员。
words.en: If you endorse someone or something, you say publicly that you support or approve of them.

words.ex: The dorsal fin helps the fish swim steadily.
words.ex_cn: 背鳍帮助鱼稳定游动。
words.en: Relating to the back or posterior part of an organism or structure.

words.tr: n. 支持；认可；名人代言；违章驾驶记录
words.ex: He got an endorsement from his boss.
words.ex_cn: 他得到了老板的支持。
words.en: An endorsement is a statement or action which shows that you support or approve of something or someone.

words.tr: v. 捐赠；订阅；订购；签署；认购（股份）
words.ex: He decided to subscribe $50 to the charity each month.
words.ex_cn: 他决定每月向慈善机构捐赠50美元。
words.en: If you subscribe to a magazine or a service, you pay to receive it regularly.

words.ex: His countenance showed surprise.
words.ex_cn: 他的面容流露出惊讶。
words.en: A person's face or facial expression; support or approval.

words.tr: n. 派系；派系斗争；内讧
words.ex: The faction argued loudly about the new rule.
words.ex_cn: 这个派别就新规定激烈争论。
words.en: A faction is a group of people within a larger group who have different opinions and beliefs from the rest of the group.

words.tr: adj. 派系的；与派系相关的；好争论的
words.ex: The factious group refused to cooperate with others.
words.ex_cn: 这个分裂的团体拒绝与其他人的合作。
words.en: If you describe a group or activity as factious, you mean that it is divided into groups that have strong and unfriendly disagreements.

words.ex: The character is fictitious and does not exist in real life.
words.ex_cn: 这个角色是虚构的，现实中不存在。
words.en: Fictitious means invented and not true or not existing.

words.tr: n. 做作；假装；装模作样
words.ex: His laugh was an affectation to seem cool.
words.ex_cn: 他的笑声是一种装模作样的表现，以显得很酷。
words.en: An affectation is a deliberate pretense or exaggerated display of a particular quality or manner.

words.tr: adj. 轻率的；肤浅的；易做到的
words.ex: He gave a facile answer to the hard question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个难题给出了一个简单的答案。
words.en: If you describe someone's arguments or suggestions as facile, you are criticizing them because their ideas are too simple and indicate a lack of careful, intelligent thinking.

words.tr: v. 促进；使便利；使容易；
words.ex: The teacher facilitates learning by asking questions.
words.ex_cn: 老师通过提问来促进学习。
words.en: To make an action or process easier or more likely to happen.

words.tr: n. 派系；小集团；小圈子
words.ex: She found it hard to break into the clique at school.
words.ex_cn: 她发现很难融入学校的小圈子。
words.en: A clique is a small group of people who spend their time together and do not allow others to join them.

words.ex: The broken bridge is a menace to drivers.
words.ex_cn: 这座破桥对司机来说是个危险物。
words.en: If you say that someone or something is a menace, you mean that they are likely to cause serious harm.

words.ex: He felt intimidation when the teacher shouted at him.
words.ex_cn: 当老师对他大喊时，他感到害怕。
words.en: Intimidation is the act of making someone feel frightened or threatened, especially in order to make them do something.

words.ex: The farmer milks the cow every morning.
words.ex_cn: 农夫每天早上给母牛挤奶。
words.en: A cow is a large female animal that is kept on farms for its milk.

words.ex: They tried to coerce him into signing the paper.
words.ex_cn: 他们试图强迫他签署那份文件。
words.en: If you coerce someone into doing something, you make them do it, even though they do not want to.

words.ex: She tried to browbeat him into submission.
words.ex_cn: 她试图恫吓他屈服。
words.en: To intimidate or bully someone into doing something, especially by using threats or aggressive behavior.

words.ex: He bullies his little brother every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天都欺负他的弟弟。
words.en: To bully someone means to use your strength or power to hurt or frighten them, often forcing them to do something they do not want to do.

words.ex: The two countries made a pact to stop fighting.
words.ex_cn: 这两个国家达成了一项停止战斗的协议。
words.en: A pact is a formal agreement between two or more people, organizations, or governments to do a particular thing or to help each other.

words.ex: The book has a compact design.
words.ex_cn: 这本书的设计很紧凑。
words.en: A compact object or substance is small and dense, with all its parts closely packed together.

words.ex: The armistice was signed to end the conflict.
words.ex_cn: 停战协议的签署结束了冲突。
words.en: An armistice is a formal agreement of warring parties to stop fighting. It is not necessarily the end of a war, since it might be just a cessation of hostilities while an attempt is made to negotiate a lasting peace.

words.ex: Two countries signed a treaty to stop the war.
words.ex_cn: 两个国家签署了一项条约以停止战争。
words.en: A treaty is a formal agreement between two or more countries or groups, especially one that is written down and signed by their leaders.

words.ex: The two countries signed a protocol to stop the war.
words.ex_cn: 这两个国家签署了一项停止战争的协议。
words.en: A protocol is a set of rules or a system of rules about the correct way to act in formal situations.

words.ex: The two countries signed an accord to stop the war.
words.ex_cn: 这两个国家签署了一项协议以停止战争。
words.en: An accord is an official agreement or treaty. It can also refer to a state of agreement or harmony.

words.ex: He showed xenophobia toward people from other countries.
words.ex_cn: 他对来自其他国家的人表现出恐外心理。
words.en: Xenophobia is a strong feeling of dislike or fear of people from other countries.

words.ex: He feels dizzy because of his acrophobia when he looks down from the tall building.
words.ex_cn: 他从高楼往下看时因为恐高而感到头晕。
words.en: An extreme or irrational fear of heights.

words.tr: n. 对同性恋的憎恶或恐惧
words.ex: The campaign aims to raise awareness about homophobia in schools.
words.ex_cn: 该活动旨在提高人们对学校中恐同现象的认识。
words.en: Homophobia is a strong and irrational dislike or fear of homosexual people.

words.ex: He feels panic in small rooms because of claustrophobia.
words.ex_cn: 他因为幽闭恐惧症在小房间里感到恐慌。
words.en: A morbid fear of being closed in a confined space.

words.tr: phrase. 社交恐惧症；对社交场合或人际互动产生强烈恐惧或焦虑的心理障碍
words.ex: He has social phobia and avoids talking to people.
words.ex_cn: 他有社交恐惧症，避免和人交谈。
words.en: Social phobia is an anxiety disorder characterized by intense fear in social situations, leading to avoidance of social interactions.

words.ex: Don't meddle in my affairs.
words.ex_cn: 别插手我的事情。
words.en: To meddle means to interfere in something that is not one's concern.

words.tr: adj. 好管闲事的；爱干预的
words.ex: She was always meddlesome, poking her nose into everyone's business.
words.ex_cn: 她总是爱管闲事，把鼻子伸进每个人的事务中。
words.en: If you describe a person as meddlesome, you are criticizing them because they try to influence or change things that do not concern them.

words.ex: He tries to mediate between the two friends.
words.ex_cn: 他试图在两个朋友之间调解。
words.en: To intervene between people or parties in order to bring about an agreement or reconciliation.

words.ex: The castle is a medieval building.
words.ex_cn: 这座城堡是一座中世纪的建筑。
words.en: Relating to the Middle Ages, the period in European history from about the 5th century to the 15th century.

words.ex: The movie was mediocre and not worth watching.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影很平庸，不值得看。
words.en: If you describe something as mediocre, you mean that it is of average quality but you think it should be better.

words.ex: Don't interfere when I am working.
words.ex_cn: 我工作时不要打扰。
words.en: To interfere means to involve oneself in a situation where one is not wanted or needed, often causing problems or hindering progress.

words.ex: The teacher intervened when the students argued.
words.ex_cn: 当学生们争吵时，老师进行了干涉。
words.en: If you intervene in a situation, you become involved in it and try to change it.

words.tr: phrasal verb. 插嘴；干涉；打扰
words.ex: He always butts in when others are talking.
words.ex_cn: 他总是在别人说话时插嘴。
words.en: To interrupt a conversation or activity, especially in a rude or intrusive manner.

words.tr: adj. 爱管闲事的；爱打听的
words.ex: The nosy neighbor always asks too many questions.
words.ex_cn: 那个爱管闲事的邻居总是问太多问题。
words.en: If you describe someone as nosy, you mean that they are too interested in things that do not concern them, especially other people's affairs.

words.tr: adj. 爱发号施令的；多管闲事的
words.ex: The officious clerk refused to help unless I filled out another form.
words.ex_cn: 那位爱多管闲事的职员拒绝帮忙，除非我再填一份表格。
words.en: If you describe someone as officious, you are critical of them because they are eager to tell people what to do when you think they should not.

words.ex: The autocratic leader made all decisions without asking others.
words.ex_cn: 这位独裁的领导人独自做出所有决定，从不询问他人。
words.en: If you describe someone as autocratic, you are criticizing them because they have complete power and make decisions without asking anyone else's advice.

words.tr: n. 贵族政治；贵族统治；贵族
words.ex: The aristocracy lived in big castles long ago.
words.ex_cn: 很久以前，贵族住在巨大的城堡里。
words.en: The highest class in certain societies, especially those holding hereditary titles or offices.

words.tr: n. 官僚主义；官僚机构
words.ex: He hates the bureaucracy in government offices.
words.ex_cn: 他讨厌政府办公室里的官僚主义。
words.en: Bureaucracy refers to a system of government or business that has many complicated rules and ways of doing things.

words.ex: People vote in democracy to choose their leaders.
words.ex_cn: 人们在民主制度下投票选择他们的领导人。
words.en: A system of government by the whole population or all the eligible members of a state, typically through elected representatives.

words.tr: n. 富豪；财阀；财阀政治；富豪统治
words.ex: The country is often criticized for being a plutocracy where wealth determines political power.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家经常因为财富决定政治权力的富豪统治而受到批评。
words.en: A plutocracy is a society or system that is ruled or controlled by people of great wealth or income.

words.tr: n. 专家治国制度；技术官僚政治；技术专家政府
words.ex: The country is ruled by a technocracy of engineers and scientists.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家由一群工程师和科学家统治。
words.en: A technocracy is a system of governance where decision-makers are selected on the basis of their expertise in a given area of responsibility, particularly with regard to scientific or technical knowledge.

words.tr: adj. 不透明的；难懂的；晦涩的
words.ex: The glass is opaque, so I cannot see through it.
words.ex_cn: 这扇玻璃是不透明的，所以我看不到它后面的东西。
words.en: If an object or substance is opaque, you cannot see through it.

words.ex: The ancient Romans built an aqueduct to bring water to the city.
words.ex_cn: 古罗马人建造了一条渡槽来为城市供水。
words.en: An aqueduct is a structure designed to carry water from a remote source to a desired location, often using gravity as the driving force. It is a critical component of urban water supply systems, especially in ancient civilizations.

words.tr: adj. 水生的；水栖的；水中的；
words.ex: The fish live in aquatic plants.
words.ex_cn: 这些鱼生活在水生植物中。
words.en: Relating to water; living in or near water or taking place in water.

words.ex: The village gets water from a deep aquifer.
words.ex_cn: 这个村庄的水源来自一个深层地下蓄水层。
words.en: An aquifer is a body of permeable rock which can contain or transmit groundwater.

words.tr: v. 在潮湿路面上打滑；乘滑水板滑行; n. 滑水板
words.ex: The car aquaplaned on the wet road.
words.ex_cn: 汽车在湿滑的路面上打滑了。
words.en: An aquaplane is a board on which a person stands to ride on the surface of water, especially when being pulled by a motorboat. As a verb, it means to ride on such a board.

words.ex: It was sheer luck that he won the game.
words.ex_cn: 他赢了比赛完全是运气。
words.en: Sheer is used to emphasize that a state or situation is complete and does not involve or is not mixed with anything else.

words.tr:
v. 同意；赞成
n. 同意；赞成
words.ex: He gave his assent to the plan.
words.ex_cn: 他同意了这个计划。
words.en: If you assent to something, you agree to it or agree with it.

words.ex: He asked for her consent before starting the project.
words.ex_cn: 他在开始这个项目之前征求了她的同意。
words.en: Consent is permission for something to happen or agreement to do something.

words.ex: He expressed dissent about the new rule.
words.ex_cn: 他对新规定提出了异议。
words.en: Dissent is strong disagreement or dissatisfaction with a decision or opinion, especially one that is supported by most people or by people in authority.

words.ex: The city has a curfew at 10 p.m.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市晚上10点实行宵禁。
words.en: A curfew is an order given by the authorities that people must stay indoors between certain hours, typically at night.

words.ex: He tried to usurp the throne from his brother.
words.ex_cn: 他试图从他兄弟手中篡夺王位。
words.en: If you say that someone usurps a job, role, title, or position, they take it from someone when they have no right to do this.

words.ex: He paid high usury on his loan.
words.ex_cn: 他支付了高额的高利贷。
words.en: The practice of lending money at an exorbitant interest rate.

words.tr: v. 使焦虑；使不安；扰乱
words.ex: The noise perturbs the baby.
words.ex_cn: 噪音让婴儿不安。
words.en: If something perturbs you, it makes you feel anxious or worried.

words.ex: The political turbulence caused many people to leave the country.
words.ex_cn: 政治骚乱导致许多人离开了这个国家。
words.en: A state of conflict or confusion; irregular atmospheric motion especially when characterized by up-and-down currents.

words.tr: adj. 浑浊的；污浊不清的；
words.ex: The river water looks turbid after the rain.
words.ex_cn: 雨后河水看起来浑浊。
words.en: If you describe something as turbid, you mean that it is cloudy, dirty, or muddy.

words.ex: The children caused a big commotion in the classroom.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在教室里制造了很大的喧闹。
words.en: A commotion is a lot of noise, confusion, and excitement.

words.ex: The city had a blackout during the war.
words.ex_cn: 战争期间，这座城市实行了灯火管制。
words.en: A blackout is a period of time during which there is no electricity, or when the lights are turned off, especially as a result of an emergency or for a theatrical effect. It can also refer to a temporary loss of memory or consciousness.

words.ex: The relentless rain flooded the streets.
words.ex_cn: 无情的雨水淹没了街道。
words.en: Someone who is relentless is determined to do something and refuses to give up, even if what they are doing is unpleasant or cruel.

words.tr: adj. 无情的；冷酷的；残忍的；
words.ex: The ruthless boss fired employees without warning.
words.ex_cn: 这位无情的老板未经警告就解雇了员工。
words.en: If you say that someone is ruthless, you mean that you disapprove of them because they are very harsh or cruel, and will do anything that is necessary to achieve what they want.

words.ex: The storm caused a brutal flood that destroyed many homes.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴引发了残酷的洪水，摧毁了许多房屋。
words.en: A brutal act or person is cruel and violent.

words.ex: The ferocious wind knocked down the tree.
words.ex_cn: 强烈的风把树吹倒了。
words.en: A ferocious animal or person is very fierce and violent.

words.tr: adj. 野兽的；野兽般的；极残忍的
words.ex: The bestial treatment of the prisoners shocked everyone.
words.ex_cn: 对囚犯的兽性对待震惊了所有人。
words.en: If you describe behavior or a situation as bestial, you mean that it is very unpleasant or disgusting.

words.tr: adj. 残暴的；恶劣的；糟透的
words.ex: The dictator committed atrocious acts against his people.
words.ex_cn: 这位独裁者对人民犯下了残暴的罪行。
words.en: If you describe something as atrocious, you are emphasizing that its quality is very bad.

words.tr: adj. 重罪的；恶毒的；凶恶的
words.ex: He committed a felonious act last year.
words.ex_cn: 他去年犯下了一项重罪行为。
words.en: Involving or relating to a felony; criminal.

words.tr: adj. 宽厚的；仁慈的；不严格的；
words.ex: The teacher was lenient with students who were late.
words.ex_cn: 老师对迟到的学生很宽厚。
words.en: If you are lenient with someone, you are not strict in the way you treat them, especially when they have done something wrong.

words.ex: The clement teacher gave students extra time.
words.ex_cn: 这位仁慈的老师给了学生更多时间。
words.en: Mild or merciful in disposition or character; lenient; compassionate.

words.tr: v. 逐渐削弱；暗中损害；
words.ex: Constant criticism can undermine your confidence.
words.ex_cn: 不断的批评会逐渐削弱你的信心。
words.en: To undermine something means to weaken it or make it less effective, often in a gradual or sneaky way.

words.tr: n. 失败者；处于劣势的一方
words.ex: The underdog team won the match against all expectations.
words.ex_cn: 这支被视为失败者的球队出人意料地赢得了比赛。
words.en: An underdog is a person or group in a competition, usually in sports and creative works, who is popularly expected to lose.

words.ex: The teacher underscored the importance of homework.
words.ex_cn: 老师强调了作业的重要性。
words.en: To emphasize the importance of something or to draw a line underneath a word or phrase.

words.tr: v. 轻描淡写；打折扣地说；少说
words.ex: He understated the cost of the repair.
words.ex_cn: 他轻描淡写了维修的费用。
words.en: If you understate something, you describe it in a way that suggests it is less important or serious than it really is.

words.ex: He underrates his own talent.
words.ex_cn: 他低估了自己的才华。
words.en: To underrate something or someone means to fail to recognize their true value or importance.

words.ex: Strong foundations underpin the building.
words.ex_cn: 坚固的地基支撑着这栋建筑。
words.en: To support, strengthen, or provide a foundation for something.

words.tr: v. 轻描淡写；表演不充分
words.ex: He underplays his talent to avoid jealousy.
words.ex_cn: 他故意低估自己的才华，以避免引起嫉妒。
words.en: To represent something as being less important or significant than it really is.

words.tr: v. 承担经济责任；承保；承销
words.ex: The bank will underwrite the new project.
words.ex_cn: 银行将为这个新项目提供担保。
words.en: To agree to pay for a possible loss or damage, especially in insurance; to agree to buy all the shares that are not bought by the public in a new company, or to arrange for this to be done.

words.ex: The project involves the contiguity of several different disciplines.
words.ex_cn: 这个项目涉及几个不同学科的连续性。
words.en: The state of bordering or being in contact with something.

words.ex: The proximity of the school to the park makes it nice for kids.
words.ex_cn: 学校靠近公园，对孩子们来说很好。
words.en: Proximity refers to the state of being near in space or time.

words.ex: The park is in the vicinity of my house.
words.ex_cn: 公园在我家附近。
words.en: The area or region near or about a place; the surrounding district.

words.ex: The two cities have adjacency on the map.
words.ex_cn: 这两个城市在地图上是相邻的。
words.en: The state of being adjacent or next to something.

words.ex: Don't jeopardize your health by skipping meals.
words.ex_cn: 不要因为不吃饭而危及你的健康。
words.en: To jeopardize something means to do something that may destroy it or cause it to be lost.

words.tr: adj. 不安全的；危险的；不稳当的；
words.ex: The ladder was precarious and might fall.
words.ex_cn: 梯子不安全，可能会倒。
words.en: If a situation is precarious, it is uncertain or dangerous, and could get worse or fail.

words.ex: The hikers faced great peril in the storm.
words.ex_cn: 徒步者在风暴中面临巨大危险。
words.en: Peril refers to serious and immediate danger.

words.ex: The house has a small annex for storage.
words.ex_cn: 这所房子有一个用于存放物品的小附属物。
words.en: To annex means to take control of a country, region, etc., especially by force; to add an area or region to a country, state, etc. : to take control of (a territory or place).

words.ex: The two companies will merge next year.
words.ex_cn: 这两家公司明年将合并。
words.en: To combine or unite to form a single entity.

words.ex: The lock uses a simple combination of three numbers.
words.ex_cn: 这个锁使用三个数字的简单组合。
words.en: A combination is a mixture of things or people that are combined.

words.ex: The cat occupies the sofa all day.
words.ex_cn: 这只猫整天占据着沙发。
words.en: If people or things occupy a place, they are in it or fill it.

words.ex: He tried to repress his anger.
words.ex_cn: 他试图抑制自己的愤怒。
words.en: If you repress a feeling, you deliberately do not express it, often because it is considered unacceptable or inappropriate.

words.ex: He tried to suppress his anger.
words.ex_cn: 他试图抑制自己的愤怒。
words.en: To suppress something means to prevent it from being expressed, known, or continuing.

words.ex: The king oppresses the poor people.
words.ex_cn: 国王压迫穷人。
words.en: If someone oppresses people, they treat them cruelly or unfairly and prevent them from having the same rights as other people.

words.tr: adj. 紧迫的； v. 按；“press”的现在分词；
words.ex: The pressing issue is finding clean water.
words.ex_cn: 紧迫的问题是找到干净的水。
words.en: If something is pressing, it needs to be dealt with immediately because it is important or urgent.

words.ex: He compresses the file to save space.
words.ex_cn: 他压缩文件以节省空间。
words.en: To compress something means to press it or squeeze it so that it takes up less space.

words.tr: vt. 使减压，使解除压力; vi. 减压
words.ex: After the dive, the divers must decompress slowly to avoid the bends.
words.ex_cn: 潜水后，潜水员必须缓慢减压以避免减压病。
words.en: To decompress means to reduce pressure or stress, or to convert compressed data back to its original form.

words.tr:
v. 谴责；责难；指责
n. 谴责；责难；指责
words.ex: The teacher censured the student for cheating.
words.ex_cn: 老师谴责了那个作弊的学生。
words.en: If you censure someone for something that they have done, you tell them that you strongly disapprove of it.

words.tr:
n. 审查员；检查员
v. 检查；审查
words.ex: The censor removed the bad words from the movie.
words.ex_cn: 审查员从电影中删除了粗俗用语。
words.en: A censor is a person who supervises conduct and morals: in particular, one who examines books, films, or other material for objectionable matter.

words.ex: The government imposed censorship on the news.
words.ex_cn: 政府对新闻实施了审查。
words.en: Censorship is the censoring of books, plays, films, or reports, especially by government officials, because they are considered immoral or secret in some way.

words.ex: The government does a census every ten years.
words.ex_cn: 政府每十年进行一次人口普查。
words.en: A census is an official count or survey of a population, typically recording various details of individuals.

words.ex: The team reached a consensus on the project plan.
words.ex_cn: 团队就项目计划达成了共识。
words.en: A consensus is general agreement among a group of people.

words.ex: My mom scolded me for coming home late.
words.ex_cn: 妈妈因为我回家晚而责备了我。
words.en: If you scold someone, you speak angrily to them because they have done something wrong.

words.ex: The public condemned the corrupt politician.
words.ex_cn: 公众谴责了这位腐败的政客。
words.en: If you condemn something, you say that it is very bad and unacceptable.

words.tr:
v. 责备；指责
n. 责备；指责
words.ex: She reproached him for being late.
words.ex_cn: 她责备他迟到了。
words.en: To express disapproval or disappointment towards someone because of their actions or behavior.

words.ex: The teacher reproved the student for being late.
words.ex_cn: 老师因为学生迟到而责骂了他。
words.en: If you reprove someone, you speak angrily or seriously to them because they have behaved in a wrong or foolish way.

words.tr: n. 骚动；骚乱；心烦意乱
words.ex: The crowd caused a tumult after the game.
words.ex_cn: 比赛后，人群引起了混乱。
words.en: A tumult is a state of confusion, noise, and excitement, often involving a large group of people.

words.ex: The doctor found a tumor in his lung.
words.ex_cn: 医生在他的肺里发现了一个肿瘤。
words.en: A tumor is a mass of tissue that's formed by an accumulation of abnormal cells. Normally, the cells in your body age, die, and are replaced by new cells. With cancer and other tumors, something disrupts this cycle. Tumor cells grow, even though the body does not need them, and unlike normal old cells, they don't die. As this process goes on, the tumor continues to grow as more and more cells are added to the mass.

words.ex: The infection caused the tissue to tumefy.
words.ex_cn: 感染导致组织肿胀。
words.en: To cause to swell or become swollen.

words.tr: adj. 肿大的；肿胀的；浮夸的
words.ex: His tumid face looked swollen after the insect bite.
words.ex_cn: 他的脸在被昆虫叮咬后显得肿胀。
words.en: Swollen or distended; pompous or bombastic in style.

words.tr: n. 拒不服从；藐视法庭
words.ex: His contumacy led to a contempt of court charge.
words.ex_cn: 他的拒不服从导致了他被指控藐视法庭。
words.en: Contumacy is the refusal to obey or comply with authority, often characterized by stubborn resistance or disobedience.

words.ex: He bore the contumely with dignity.
words.ex_cn: 他以尊严承受了侮辱。
words.en: Insolent or insulting language or treatment.

words.tr: n. 混乱；动荡；骚乱；恐慌
words.ex: The storm caused turmoil in the town.
words.ex_cn: 风暴给小镇带来了混乱。
words.en: A state of great disturbance, confusion, or uncertainty.

words.ex: The announcement caused an uproar in the town.
words.ex_cn: 这个公告在小镇上引起了轩然大波。
words.en: A loud and impassioned noise or disturbance.

words.ex: The teacher designated him as the group leader.
words.ex_cn: 老师指派他为组长。
words.en: If you designate someone or something as a particular thing, you formally give them that description or name.

words.tr: v. 委托；交付；托运；寄售
words.ex: He will consign the package to the post office.
words.ex_cn: 他将把包裹寄到邮局。
words.en: If you consign something to someone, you give it to them to keep or to sell.

words.ex: The red light signifies stop.
words.ex_cn: 红灯表示停止。
words.en: If an event, a sign, or a symbol signifies something, it is a sign of that thing or represents that thing.

words.ex: The boss appointed Tom as the new manager.
words.ex_cn: 老板任命汤姆为新经理。
words.en: If you appoint someone to a job or official position, you formally choose them for it.

words.tr: v. 给予选举权；释放（奴隶）
words.ex: The law will enfranchise all adults over 18.
words.ex_cn: 这项法律将赋予所有18岁以上成年人选举权。
words.en: To enfranchise someone means to give them the right to vote in elections.

words.ex: He bought a franchise to open a coffee shop.
words.ex_cn: 他购买了一个特许经营权来开一家咖啡店。
words.en: A franchise is an authorization granted by a government or company to an individual or group enabling them to carry out specified commercial activities, e.g., acting as an agent for a company's products.

words.tr: n. 束缚；奴隶的身份；奴役（等于 thralldom）
words.ex: He escaped from the thraldom of debt.
words.ex_cn: 他摆脱了债务的束缚。
words.en: The state of being under the control of another person or of a powerful influence.

words.ex: He was held in thrall by his addiction.
words.ex_cn: 他被他的瘾所束缚。
words.en: If you say that someone is in thrall to a person or thing, you mean that they are completely in their power or are greatly influenced by them.

words.ex: He felt trapped in bondage.
words.ex_cn: 他感到被困在束缚中。
words.en: Bondage refers to the state of being a slave or being under the control of another person.

words.tr: v. 剥夺…的权利（尤指选举权）
words.ex: The law disenfranchises many poor people.
words.ex_cn: 这项法律剥夺了许多穷人的投票权。
words.en: To disenfranchise someone means to take away their right to vote or to deprive them of a privilege or a right.

words.tr:
v. 征收；征税；征募
n. 征兵；征税
words.ex: The government will levy a new tax next month.
words.ex_cn: 政府下个月将征收一项新税。
words.en: To levy means to impose or collect a tax, fee, or fine. It can also refer to the act of enlisting or drafting individuals into military service.

words.tr:
n. 杠杆；杠杆作用；影响力
v. 举债经营；充分利用
words.ex: The mechanic used a lever to lift the car.
words.ex_cn: 机械师用杠杆来抬起汽车。
words.en: Leverage refers to the use of a lever or the mechanical advantage gained by using a lever. In finance, it refers to the use of borrowed capital to increase the potential return of an investment.

words.ex: His joke brought some levity to the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他的笑话为会议带来了一些轻松气氛。
words.en: Levity refers to a lack of seriousness, especially at an inappropriate time, often characterized by frivolity or lightness of manner.

words.ex: Drugs can alleviate pain.
words.ex_cn: 药物可以减轻疼痛。
words.en: To make something less severe or intense.

words.ex: Exercise can elevate your mood.
words.ex_cn: 锻炼可以提升你的情绪。
words.en: To elevate something means to raise it to a higher position or level, either physically or in terms of its status or importance.

words.tr: vt. 使轻轻浮起；使飘浮空中; vi. 轻轻浮起；飘浮空中
words.ex: The magician claimed he could levitate objects with his mind.
words.ex_cn: 魔术师声称他可以用意念使物体飘浮。
words.en: To rise or cause to rise into the air and float in apparent defiance of gravity.

words.tr: adj. 群体的；社区的；公有的；
words.ex: They share a communal kitchen.
words.ex_cn: 他们共用一个群体厨房。
words.en: Communal means relating to or shared by all the members of a community.

words.ex: The village decided to communalize the land for all farmers.
words.ex_cn: 村庄决定将土地公有化，供所有农民使用。

words.tr:
n. 共产主义者；
adj. 共产主义的；
