words.en: If you say that there is ambiguity in something, you mean that it is unclear or confusing, or it can be understood in more than one way.

words.ex: The frog is an amphibian.
words.ex_cn: 青蛙是一种两栖动物。
words.en: An amphibian is a type of animal that can live both on land and in water. Frogs, toads, and salamanders are examples of amphibians.

words.tr: n. 圆形剧场；竞技场；梯形教室
words.ex: The students watched a play in the old amphitheater.
words.ex_cn: 学生们在旧的圆形剧场里观看了戏剧。
words.en: An amphitheater is a large open area surrounded by rows of seats sloping upwards. Amphitheaters were used in ancient Greece and Rome for public entertainments.

words.ex: He felt ambivalent about accepting the job offer.
words.ex_cn: 他对接受这份工作邀约感到矛盾。
words.en: If you say that someone is ambivalent about something, you mean that they have mixed feelings about it or are unsure whether they want it or not.

words.ex: The denizen of the forest knows all the paths.
words.ex_cn: 森林的居民知道所有的路。
words.en: A denizen of a particular place is someone who lives there or is often there.

words.ex: The inhabitant lives in a small house.
words.ex_cn: 这位居民住在一所小房子里。
words.en: An inhabitant of a place is one of the people who live there.

words.tr:
adj. 居住的；常驻的；
n. 常住居民；
words.ex: The resident population grew last year.
words.ex_cn: 居住人口去年增加了。
words.en: A resident is someone who lives in a particular place or a person who has their home in a place.

words.ex: The cave dweller lives alone in the mountain.
words.ex_cn: 洞穴居民独自住在山里。
words.en: A dweller is a person or animal that lives in or at a specified place.

words.ex: The occupant of the room is sleeping.
words.ex_cn: 房间里的住户正在睡觉。
words.en: An occupant is someone who lives in or uses a particular room, building, or area of land.

words.ex: Every citizen must follow the law.
words.ex_cn: 每个公民都必须遵守法律。
words.en: A citizen is a person who is legally recognized as a member of a country or state, either by birth or by naturalization, and who is entitled to its protection and privileges.

words.ex: She bought a new garment for the party.
words.ex_cn: 她为派对买了一件新衣服。
words.en: A garment is a piece of clothing; used especially in contexts where you are talking about the manufacture or sale of clothes.

words.tr:
n. 服装；制服；装束
v. 穿衣
words.ex: He wore old garb to the party.
words.ex_cn: 他穿着旧衣服去参加派对。
words.en: Garb refers to clothing, especially of a distinctive or special kind.

words.tr:
v. （在食物上）加装饰菜；装饰
n. （食物上的）装饰菜；装饰
words.ex: She puts a lemon slice to garnish the drink.
words.ex_cn: 她放一片柠檬来装饰这杯饮料。
words.en: To garnish something means to decorate it with something, especially food with small amounts of different foods.

words.tr: adj. 俗艳的；花哨的；过分装饰的
words.ex: The room was decorated in a garish pink that hurt the eyes.
words.ex_cn: 房间被装饰成刺眼的粉红色，令人眼睛不适。
words.en: If you describe something as garish, you mean that it is excessively bright, colorful, or elaborate in a way that is considered tasteless or unattractive.

words.ex: She bought new apparel for the party.
words.ex_cn: 她为派对买了新衣服。
words.en: Clothing, especially outer garments; attire.

words.ex: He wore formal attire to the wedding.
words.ex_cn: 他穿了正式服装去参加婚礼。
words.en: Clothes, especially fine or formal ones.

words.ex: He wore a funny costume for the party.
words.ex_cn: 他为派对穿了一套滑稽的服装。
words.en: A costume is a set of clothes in a style typical of a particular country or historical period, or a set of clothes worn by an actor for a particular role.

words.ex: Blue jeans are in vogue this year.
words.ex_cn: 今年牛仔裤很时髦。
words.en: If something is in vogue, it is very popular and fashionable.

words.ex: His answer was vague and hard to understand.
words.ex_cn: 他的回答不明确，难以理解。
words.en: If something written or spoken is vague, it does not explain or express things clearly.

words.tr: n. 时尚；一时流行的狂热
words.ex: Wearing those shoes is just a fad.
words.ex_cn: 穿那双鞋只是个短暂的潮流。
words.en: A fad is an activity or topic of interest that is very popular for a short time.

words.tr:
n. 假发
v. 痛骂；严责；给…装假发
words.ex: She wore a wig to cover her bald head.
words.ex_cn: 她戴了一顶假发来遮盖她光秃的头。
words.en: A wig is a covering of false hair which you wear on your head, for example because you are bald or because you want to cover up your own hair.

words.tr: n. 假发；17至18世纪流行的长假发
words.ex: The king wore a large periwig to look fancy.
words.ex_cn: 国王戴着一顶大假发以显得华丽。

words.ex: He wears a toupee to cover his bald head.
words.ex_cn: 他戴一顶假发来遮盖秃头。
words.en: A toupee is a small wig or hairpiece worn to cover a bald spot.

words.tr: n. 牙托； 一副假牙
words.ex: He wears a denture to eat food.
words.ex_cn: 他戴假牙来吃东西。
words.en: A denture is a removable plate or frame holding one or more artificial teeth.

words.ex: He walks with an artificial limb after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他在事故后用假肢走路。

words.ex: He bought a repair kit for his bike.
words.ex_cn: 他买了一套自行车维修工具。
words.en: A kit is a group of items that are kept together, often in the same container, because they are all used for similar purposes.

words.ex: She bought a new outfit for the party.
words.ex_cn: 她为派对买了一套新衣服。
words.en: An outfit is a set of clothes worn together, especially for a particular occasion or purpose.

words.ex: He bought a new gizmo to fix his phone.
words.ex_cn: 他买了一个新小装置来修他的手机。
words.en: A gizmo is a small device or tool, especially one whose name you do not know or cannot remember.

words.ex: He bought a new gadget to clean his kitchen.
words.ex_cn: 他买了一个新的小器具来清洁厨房。
words.en: A gadget is a small device or machine with a particular purpose.

words.ex: The house has a commodious living room.
words.ex_cn: 这所房子有一个宽敞的客厅。
words.en: A commodious room or building is large and has a lot of space.

words.ex: The new house has a spacious living room.
words.ex_cn: 这所新房子有一个宽敞的客厅。
words.en: A spacious room, building, or place is large in size or area, so that you can move around freely in it.

words.tr: adj. 狭窄的； v. “cramp”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The tiny room was cramped and hard to move in.
words.ex_cn: 这个小房间很狭窄，很难活动。
words.en: If a place is cramped, it is not big enough for the people or things in it, so that it is difficult to move around or to use things properly.

words.tr:
v. 闲逛；漫步
n. 闲逛；漫步
words.ex: We decided to saunter along the beach.
words.ex_cn: 我们决定沿着海滩漫步。
words.en: If you saunter somewhere, you walk there in a slow, relaxed way.

words.tr:
v. 闲逛；散步；漫步；
n. 闲逛；散步；漫步；
words.ex: They stroll in the park after dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他们晚饭后在公园里闲逛。
words.en: If you stroll somewhere, you walk there in a slow, relaxed way.

words.tr:
v. 缓行；溜蹄
n. 溜蹄；缓行漫步
words.ex: He amble through the park after dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他晚饭后在公园里缓行。
words.en: To walk at a slow, relaxed pace, especially for pleasure.

words.ex: He likes to ramble about his travels.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢漫谈他的旅行经历。
words.en: To walk for pleasure, especially in the countryside, without a definite route or destination.

words.tr:
v. 缓慢而弯曲地流动；漫步；闲聊
n. 河流的曲折；漫步；迂回曲折的进程
words.ex: The river meanders through the forest.
words.ex_cn: 这条河蜿蜒穿过森林。
words.en: To meander means to follow a winding and turning course, often used to describe the way a river flows or the way a person walks without a clear direction.

words.ex: He used to rove through the forests when he was young.
words.ex_cn: 他年轻时常常在森林里漫游。
words.en: To rove means to travel constantly without a fixed destination; wander.

words.tr:
v. 潜行以觅食；窥伺；逡巡于
n. 悄然潜行；四处觅食；徘徊
words.ex: The cat will prowl around the house at night.
words.ex_cn: 猫会在晚上在房子周围徘徊。
words.en: To move around quietly in a place trying not to be seen or heard, especially when you are looking for something or someone.

words.ex: The cat likes to roam around the garden.
words.ex_cn: 这只猫喜欢在花园里游荡。
words.en: To roam means to move about or travel without any definite purpose or destination.

words.ex: He is loitering near the park.
words.ex_cn: 他正在公园附近闲逛。
words.en: If someone loiters somewhere, they remain there or walk up and down without any real purpose.

words.ex: We waited in the lounge before our flight.
words.ex_cn: 我们在登机前等在休息室里。
words.en: A lounge is a room in a house or public building where people can sit and relax. As a verb, to lounge means to lie, sit, or stand in a relaxed or lazy way.

words.tr:
v. 踩；踏；践踏
n. 脚步声；胎面
words.ex: He tread carefully on the icy path.
words.ex_cn: 他小心地走在结冰的小路上。
words.en: If you tread on something, you put your foot on it when you are walking. The tread of a tyre is the pattern of lines on its surface that prevent it from slipping.

words.ex: The cows trample the grass in the field.
words.ex_cn: 牛在田野里践踏草地。
words.en: If someone tramples something or tramples on it, they step heavily and carelessly on it and damage it.

words.tr: phrase. 踩踏；用力踩在……上；盖章于……上
words.ex: He stamped on the bug with his shoe.
words.ex_cn: 他用鞋踩了那只虫子。
words.en: To crush or extinguish something completely, often by stepping on it.

words.ex: He picked up a spoon, a common utensil.
words.ex_cn: 他拿起了一把勺子，一种常见的餐具。
words.en: An utensil is a tool that you use in your home, especially in the kitchen, for example, a knife, fork, or spoon.

words.ex: We can utilize solar energy to power the house.
words.ex_cn: 我们可以利用太阳能来为房子供电。
words.en: To utilize something means to use it in a practical or effective way.

words.tr: adj. 实用的；功利主义的；
words.ex: The chair is utilitarian and comfortable.
words.ex_cn: 这把椅子实用又舒适。
words.en: Utilitarian means relating to or adhering to the belief that the value of a thing or an action is determined by its utility.

words.ex: The government will implement new rules next month.
words.ex_cn: 政府下个月将实施新规定。
words.en: To implement something means to ensure that what has been planned is done.

words.ex: The kitchen has a new washing appliance.
words.ex_cn: 厨房里有一台新的洗衣机。
words.en: An appliance is a device or machine that is used to perform a particular task, especially in the home.

words.ex: The lab has a new apparatus for measuring temperature.
words.ex_cn: 实验室有一台新的温度测量装置。
words.en: The complex structure of a particular system or organization, or the equipment used for a specific purpose.

words.ex: He scooped soup with a spoon.
words.ex_cn: 他用勺子舀汤。
words.en: A scoop is a tool like a large spoon which is used for picking up substances such as ice cream or an amount of a substance that is held in a scoop. It can also refer to an important or exciting news story that is reported in a newspaper, magazine, or news broadcast before anyone else reports it.

words.tr:
n. 铲；铁锹
v. 铲；铲起
words.ex: He uses a shovel to dig the garden.
words.ex_cn: 他用铲子挖花园。
words.en: A shovel is a tool with a long handle and a broad blade or scoop, used for moving material such as earth, snow, or coal.

words.ex: The restaurant caters to vegetarians.
words.ex_cn: 这家餐厅满足素食者的需求。
words.en: To cater means to provide food and drink at an event, often as a business service, or to provide what is needed or wanted by a particular person or group.

words.ex: The café caters for breakfast and lunch.
words.ex_cn: 这家咖啡馆供应早餐和午餐。
words.en: To cater for something means to provide all the things that are needed or wanted for a particular purpose or event.

words.tr: v. 盛情招待；尽情吃喝；使欢悦
words.ex: He regaled us with stories of his travels.
words.ex_cn: 他给我们讲了他旅行的故事，让我们很开心。
words.en: To regale someone means to entertain them with stories or to provide them with a lot of enjoyable food and drink.

words.ex: He concocted a story to explain his absence.
words.ex_cn: 他编了一个故事来解释他的缺席。
words.en: If you concoct an excuse or explanation, you invent one that is not true.

words.tr: n. 混合物；调制品；捏造
words.ex: He made a strange concoction of juice and spices.
words.ex_cn: 他调制了一种奇怪的果汁和香料混合物。
words.en: A concoction is a mixture of various ingredients or elements, especially one that is unusual or unexpected.

words.ex: The precocious child could read before age five.
words.ex_cn: 这个早熟的孩子在五岁前就会阅读了。
words.en: A precocious child shows intelligence or skill at a very young age, especially in a way that is unusual for their age.

words.tr: n. 煎煮；煎熬的药；煮出的汁
words.ex: She prepared a decoction of herbs to treat her cold.
words.ex_cn: 她准备了一些草药煎煮来治疗感冒。
words.en: A decoction is a method of extraction by boiling herbal or plant material to dissolve the chemicals of the material, which may include stems, roots, bark, and rhizomes.

words.tr:
v. 酿造；沏；酝酿
n. 酿造的饮料；啤酒
words.ex: He brews coffee every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上冲咖啡。
words.en: If you brew tea or coffee, you make it by pouring hot water over tea leaves or ground coffee. If you brew beer, you make it by soaking grain in water and then fermenting it.

words.tr: n. 肉汤；（鱼、肉或蔬菜）汤
words.ex: He is drinking hot broth for dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他正在喝热汤当晚餐。
words.en: A liquid in which meat, fish, cereal grains, or vegetables have been cooked; it forms the basis of many soups and sauces.

words.ex: He was arrested for running a brothel.
words.ex_cn: 他因经营妓院被捕。
words.en: A brothel is a place where people pay to have sex with prostitutes.

words.ex: He is eating soup for lunch.
words.ex_cn: 他正在吃汤当午餐。
words.en: Soup is a liquid food made by boiling meat, fish, or vegetables in water or stock.

words.ex: The soup was palatable after adding salt.
words.ex_cn: 加了盐后，汤变得可口美味了。
words.en: If you describe food or drink as palatable, you mean that it tastes pleasant.

words.tr: n. 上腭；味觉；审美眼光；嗜好；爱好
words.ex: The roof of the mouth is called the palate.
words.ex_cn: 口腔的顶部被称为上腭。
words.en: The palate refers to the roof of the mouth in humans and other mammals, separating the oral cavity from the nasal cavity. It also refers to a person's ability to distinguish between and appreciate different flavors.

words.tr: adj. 美味的；甘美的；满足感官的；性感的
words.ex: The fruit was luscious and sweet.
words.ex_cn: 这种水果甘甜可口。
words.en: If you describe something as luscious, you mean that it is very pleasant to taste, smell, look at, or listen to.

words.ex: The cactus has succulent leaves to store water.
words.ex_cn: 仙人掌有多汁的叶子来储存水分。
words.en: (of food) tender, juicy, and tasty; (of a plant) having thick, fleshy tissues adapted to water storage.

words.ex: The cake was scrumptious.
words.ex_cn: 这个蛋糕非常美味。
words.en: If you describe food as scrumptious, you mean that it tastes extremely good.

words.tr:
n. 一小口；
v. 呷；啜；小口喝；
words.ex: He took a sip of water.
words.ex_cn: 他喝了一小口水。
words.en: To drink something slowly by taking small amounts into your mouth.

words.tr:
v. 大口喝；狂饮
n. 痛饮；一大口
words.ex: He swigged the soda quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他快速地喝了一大口苏打水。
words.en: To take a swig means to drink something quickly in large mouthfuls.

words.tr:
n. 酒；酒宴；暴饮
v. 暴饮；痛饮
words.ex: He drinks too much booze at parties.
words.ex_cn: 他在聚会上喝太多酒。
words.en: To booze means to drink alcohol, especially in large quantities.

words.tr: v. 痛饮狂欢；狂饮作乐
words.ex: They carouse every weekend at the beach.
words.ex_cn: 他们每周末都在海滩上狂欢。
words.en: To engage in a noisy, lively drinking party.

words.tr: v. 狂吃暴饮；大吃大喝；大量消耗
words.ex: He guzzles soda every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天都大口喝苏打水。
words.en: If you guzzle something, you drink it quickly and greedily.

words.tr: v. 豪饮；痛饮；开怀畅饮
words.ex: He quaffed the cold drink quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他快速地喝下了那杯冷饮。
words.en: To drink (a beverage) heartily and with gusto.

words.ex: She added cinnamon spice to the cake.
words.ex_cn: 她往蛋糕里加了肉桂香料。
words.en: Spice refers to a substance used to flavor food, which is usually made from parts of plants, especially their seeds, fruits, or roots. It can also mean something that adds interest or excitement.

words.ex: She added ketchup as a condiment to her fries.
words.ex_cn: 她把番茄酱当作调味品加在薯条上。
words.en: A condiment is a substance such as salt, pepper, or mustard that you add to food when you eat it in order to improve the flavor.

words.tr:
n. 调味品；佐料
v. 给 ... 调味；适应；风干；“season”的现在分词
words.ex: She added seasoning to the soup.
words.ex_cn: 她给汤里加了调味料。
words.en: Seasoning is a substance that is added to food to improve its flavor.

words.ex: The table was replete with food.
words.ex_cn: 桌子上摆满了食物。
words.en: If you are replete with something, you have a lot of it and it fills you up.

words.ex: The drought depletes the water supply.
words.ex_cn: 干旱耗尽了水源。
words.en: If you deplete something, you reduce the amount of it that is available or that exists.

words.ex: She replenished the water bottle after the hike.
words.ex_cn: 她在徒步后补充了水瓶里的水。
words.en: If you replenish something, you make it full or complete again.

words.ex: There is a plethora of choices on the menu.
words.ex_cn: 菜单上有太多的选择。
words.en: A plethora of something is a very large quantity of it, especially an amount that is greater than you need, want, or can cope with.

words.tr:
v. 补充；与…相辅相成；
n. 补足物；补语；余角；
words.ex: The red scarf complements her blue coat.
words.ex_cn: 这条红围巾补充了她的蓝外套。
words.en: To complement something means to make it complete or perfect by adding something to it.

words.tr:
v. 补充；
n. 补充物；附加费；
words.ex: He supplements his income by teaching part-time.
words.ex_cn: 他通过兼职教学来补充收入。
words.en: A supplement is something that is added to something else in order to make it complete or better.

words.ex: He tried to resist the temptation to eat sweets.
words.ex_cn: 他试图抵制吃甜食的诱惑。
words.en: If you resist something such as a change, you refuse to accept it and try to prevent it.

words.tr:
n. 死亡
v. 死；死亡
words.ex: His decease was sudden and unexpected.
words.ex_cn: 他的去世突然且意外。
words.en: The death of a person.

words.ex: The flowers will perish if you don't water them.
words.ex_cn: 如果你不给花浇水，它们会死。
words.en: If people or animals perish, they die as a result of very harsh conditions or as the result of an accident.

words.tr: adj. 赤贫的；贫困的；一无所有的；
words.ex: The destitute family had no food or shelter.
words.ex_cn: 这个赤贫的家庭没有食物和住所。
words.en: If you describe someone as destitute, you mean they have absolutely nothing, especially no money.

words.tr: n. 归还；赔偿；恢复原状
words.ex: The court ordered restitution for the damaged property.
words.ex_cn: 法院命令对受损财产进行赔偿。
words.en: The act of restoring something to its original state or the act of compensating for loss or damage.

words.ex: No example sentences
words.ex_cn: 没有例句
words.en: Prostitution is the practice or occupation of engaging in sexual activity with someone for payment.

words.tr:
n. 成分；
adj. 构成的；
words.ex: Sugar is a constituent of soda.
words.ex_cn: 糖是苏打水的一种成分。
words.en: A constituent is a part of a whole. In politics, a constituent is a person who is represented by an elected official.

words.ex: The politician lost his constituency after the scandal.
words.ex_cn: 这位政客在丑闻后失去了他的支持者。
words.en: A constituency is a group of people in a country or area who are entitled to vote in an election, or the area itself.

words.tr: adj. 穷困的；赤穷的；贫瘠的； v. “impoverish”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The impoverished family lived in a small house with no heating.
words.ex_cn: 这个贫困的家庭住在一个没有暖气的小房子里。
words.en: An impoverished person or area is very poor.

words.ex: The indigent man asked for food at the shelter.
words.ex_cn: 这位贫困的人在收容所里请求食物。
words.en: Someone who is indigent is very poor.

words.ex: He is penurious and never tips the waiter.
words.ex_cn: 他很吝啬，从不给服务员小费。
words.en: If you describe someone as penurious, you mean that they are extremely poor or extremely unwilling to spend money.

words.tr: adj. 没有钱的；身无分文的；贫穷的
words.ex: The impecunious student had to rely on scholarships to continue his education.
words.ex_cn: 这个贫穷的学生不得不依靠奖学金来继续他的学业。
words.en: If you describe someone as impecunious, you mean that they have very little money.

words.tr: adj. 弱势的；下层社会的；贫困的
words.ex: The school helps underprivileged children learn to read.
words.ex_cn: 这所学校帮助弱势儿童学习阅读。
words.en: People who are underprivileged lack the advantages that other people have, such as enough money or a good standard of living.

words.tr: adj. 为贫穷所困恼的，为贫穷所困扰的；非常贫穷的
words.ex: The poverty-stricken family needs food and water.
words.ex_cn: 这个贫困的家庭需要食物和水。
words.en: Extremely poor.

words.ex: His sojourn in Paris lasted two years.
words.ex_cn: 他在巴黎旅居了两年。
words.en: A sojourn is a temporary stay in a place.

words.ex: The sojourner stayed in the city for a few weeks.
words.ex_cn: 这位旅居者在城里住了几周。
words.en: A sojourner is someone who resides temporarily in a place.

words.tr: adj. 日间活动的；昼行性的
words.ex: The bird sings during diurnal hours.
words.ex_cn: 这只鸟在白天活动时鸣叫。
words.en: Relating to or occurring in a 24-hour period; daily.

words.ex: Owls are nocturnal animals.
words.ex_cn: 猫头鹰是夜间活动的动物。
words.en: Nocturnal means happening in the night or active at night.

words.ex: The meeting will adjourn at 5 p.m.
words.ex_cn: 会议将在下午5点休会。
words.en: If a meeting or trial is adjourned, or if it adjourns, it is stopped for a short time.

words.ex: They stayed in a small lodge near the forest.
words.ex_cn: 他们住在森林附近的一座小屋里。
words.en: A lodge is a small house in the country, especially one that is used by people on holiday or by people taking part in a sport such as skiing or hunting. As a verb, to lodge means to stay somewhere, especially temporarily, or to formally submit something, such as a complaint or an application.

words.ex: They traverse the forest to reach the village.
words.ex_cn: 他们横穿森林去到达村庄。
words.en: To traverse something means to move or travel across it, often with some difficulty.

words.tr:
v. 艰难地行走；吃力地行进
n. 劳苦；沉重的脚步（声）
words.ex: He plodded through the snow with heavy boots.
words.ex_cn: 他穿着沉重的靴子艰难地在雪地中行走。
words.en: To plod means to walk slowly with heavy steps, especially because you are tired or working hard. It can also mean to work slowly and steadily at something, especially something that is boring or difficult.

words.tr:
v. 缓慢或吃力地走
n. 长途跋涉
words.ex: He trudges through the snow every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上跋涉穿过雪地。
words.en: To walk slowly and with heavy steps, typically because of exhaustion or harsh conditions.

words.tr:
n. 艰苦跋涉；
v. 长途跋涉；
words.ex: The trek across the mountains took five days.
words.ex_cn: 穿越群山的艰苦跋涉花了五天时间。
words.en: A trek is a long and often difficult journey, especially one made on foot.

words.ex: He staggered home after drinking too much.
words.ex_cn: 他喝多了后摇摇晃晃地走回家。
words.en: If you stagger, you walk very unsteadily, as if you are about to fall.

words.ex: He had a stumble on the rocky path.
words.ex_cn: 他在布满石头的小路上绊了一跤。
words.en: To stumble means to trip or momentarily lose one's balance while walking or running. It can also refer to speaking in a hesitant or faltering manner.

words.tr:
v. 费力地做；苦干；跋涉
n. 苦工；劳累的工作
words.ex: He toils in the field every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天在田里辛苦劳作。
words.en: If you toil, you work very hard doing something that is difficult or tiring.

words.tr: v. 埋头苦干；坚持不懈地努力做某事
words.ex: He slogs away at his homework every night.
words.ex_cn: 他每天晚上埋头苦干做作业。

words.ex: The fugitive hid in the woods for weeks.
words.ex_cn: 这名逃亡者在树林里躲了几个星期。
words.en: A fugitive is someone who is running away or hiding, usually in order to avoid being caught by the police.

words.tr: adj. 短暂的；易逃逸的；难捕捉的；转瞬即逝的
words.ex: The beauty of the sunset was fugacious, lasting only a few moments.
words.ex_cn: 夕阳的美丽是短暂的，只持续了几分钟。
words.en: If you describe something as fugacious, you mean that it lasts for a very short time.

words.ex: He used subterfuge to avoid answering the question.
words.ex_cn: 他用遁词来避免回答问题。
words.en: Deceit used in order to achieve one's goal.

words.ex: The centrifugal force pushes the water outward.
words.ex_cn: 离心力把水向外推。
words.en: Moving or tending to move away from a center.

words.ex: The centrifugal force pushes the water out of the clothes in the washing machine.
words.ex_cn: 离心力把水从衣服上甩出去。
words.en: A force that acts on a body moving in a circular path and is directed away from the center around which the body is moving.

words.ex: The fisherman walked to the pier to check his nets.
words.ex_cn: 渔夫走到码头去检查他的渔网。
words.en: A pier is a platform sticking out into water, usually the sea, which people walk along or use when getting onto or off boats.

words.ex: The boat stops at the wharf near the sea.
words.ex_cn: 船停在海边的码头。
words.en: A wharf is a platform built out into the water where ships can be tied up and goods can be loaded or unloaded.

words.ex: The ship arrived at the dock at sunrise.
words.ex_cn: 船在日出时到达了码头。
words.en: A dock is an enclosed area of water in a port where ships go to be loaded, unloaded, and repaired.

words.tr: n. 上行坡；向上的斜坡
words.ex: The path became steeper as they ascended the acclivity.
words.ex_cn: 随着他们攀登斜坡，道路变得更加陡峭。
words.en: An acclivity is a slope or piece of ground that slopes upward.

words.ex: The ball rolled down the declivity.
words.ex_cn: 球滚下了斜坡。
words.en: A declivity is a downward slope or bend of a surface, especially of the ground.

words.ex: He has a proclivity for solving math problems.
words.ex_cn: 他有解决数学问题的倾向。
words.en: A proclivity is a natural tendency to behave in a particular way or to like a particular thing.

words.tr: v. 躺；靠在；向后倾斜（坐椅）
words.ex: He reclines on the sofa after dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他晚饭后躺在沙发上。
words.en: To recline means to lean or lie back in a relaxed position with the body supported.

words.ex: He used too much jargon in his speech.
words.ex_cn: 他在演讲中用了太多行话。
words.en: Special words or expressions that are used by a particular profession or group and are difficult for others to understand.

words.tr: n. 行话；暗号； 隐语
words.ex: The boys use street argot to talk secretly.
words.ex_cn: 这些男孩用街头黑话秘密交谈。
words.en: A specialized language or set of expressions used by a particular group, especially thieves or other criminals.

words.ex: He lives in seclusion in the mountains.
words.ex_cn: 他住在山里，过着与世隔绝的生活。
words.en: The state of being private and away from other people.

words.ex: He likes to seclude himself in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢把自己 secluded 在森林里。
words.en: To seclude means to keep someone away from other people, or to keep something away from other things.

words.ex: The rain precludes a picnic.
words.ex_cn: 下雨阻止了野餐。
words.en: If something precludes an event or action, it prevents it from happening.

words.ex: The leaf occluded the pipe.
words.ex_cn: 叶子堵住了管道。
words.en: To occlude means to block or stop up a passage, opening, or vessel.

words.ex: He stayed in quarantine for 14 days.
words.ex_cn: 他隔离了14天。
words.en: A quarantine is a period of time during which an animal or person that might have a disease is kept away from other people or animals so that the disease cannot spread.

words.ex: The school used to segregate students by race.
words.ex_cn: 这所学校过去按种族隔离学生。
words.en: To segregate means to separate one group of people, animals, or things from another, especially because they are of different types or belong to different categories.

words.tr: v. 隔离；使隔热；使隔音；使绝缘
words.ex: The walls insulate the house from cold air.
words.ex_cn: 墙壁将房子与冷空气隔离开。
words.en: To insulate something means to protect it from heat, cold, noise, or electricity by covering it in a material that prevents it from passing through.

words.ex: The hospital will isolate the patient to stop the spread.
words.ex_cn: 医院将隔离这名病人以防止传播。
words.en: To isolate someone or something means to separate them from other people or things, often in order to protect them or to prevent the spread of something harmful.

words.ex: He estranged his brother with harsh words.
words.ex_cn: 他用刻薄的话与兄弟疏远了。
words.en: If you estrange someone, especially a member of your family, you cause them to stop being friendly or close to you.

words.tr: n. 隐居者；遁世者；隐士
words.ex: He lives as a recluse in the woods.
words.ex_cn: 他住在树林里，过着隐居的生活。
words.en: A recluse is a person who lives alone and avoids other people.

words.tr: n. 隐士；隐居者；遁世者
words.ex: The hermit lives alone in a small cave.
words.ex_cn: 这位隐士独自住在一个小山洞里。
words.en: A hermit is someone who lives alone and apart from society, often for religious reasons.

words.ex: The jury was sequestered during the trial.
words.ex_cn: 陪审团在审判期间被隔离。
words.en: To sequester means to isolate or hide away; it can also refer to the legal process of seizing property until a debt is paid or a dispute is resolved.

words.ex: He sat with good posture at the desk.
words.ex_cn: 他坐在书桌前，姿势端正。
words.en: Your posture is the way in which you hold your body when you are standing or sitting.

words.ex: After work, she found repose in her garden.
words.ex_cn: 下班后，她在花园里休息。
words.en: A state of rest, sleep, or tranquility. To lie or be placed in a particular position or manner.

words.tr: v. 罢免；废黜；宣誓证明
words.ex: The people deposed the corrupt leader.
words.ex_cn: 人民推翻了腐败的领导人。
words.en: To depose someone means to remove them from a position of power or authority, especially a monarch or political leader.

words.tr: v. 置于某物之上；添加
words.ex: He superimposes a map on the photo.
words.ex_cn: 他把地图叠加在照片上。
words.en: To superimpose something means to place or lay one thing over another, typically so that both are still evident.

words.ex: The unexpected news discomposed her.
words.ex_cn: 突如其来的消息使她不安。
words.en: If something discomposes you, it makes you feel anxious or uneasy.

words.ex: He composes music in his spare time.
words.ex_cn: 他在空闲时间创作音乐。
words.en: To compose something means to make it by combining parts or elements.

words.ex: He juxtaposes old photos with new ones.
words.ex_cn: 他把老照片和新照片放在一起。
words.en: To place or deal with close together for contrasting effect.

words.tr: v. 使掉换顺序；使转移；使换位
words.ex: You need to transpose the elements to solve the equation.
words.ex_cn: 你需要调换元素来解这个方程。
words.en: To transpose something means to change its order, position, or nature, especially in mathematics or music.

words.ex: His answer was apposite to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他的回答与问题很贴切。
words.en: Something that is apposite is suitable for or appropriate to what is happening or being discussed.

words.ex: His calm demeanor made everyone feel safe.
words.ex_cn: 他平静的举止让每个人都感到安心。
words.en: The way in which a person behaves towards others; outward behavior or bearing.

words.tr: n. 举止；行为；仪态；风度
words.ex: Her deportment in the interview impressed the panel.
words.ex_cn: 她在面试中的举止给面试官留下了深刻印象。
words.en: Formal and dignified behavior or bearing, especially in public.

words.ex: He needs time to acclimate to the new climate.
words.ex_cn: 他需要时间来适应新气候。
words.en: When you acclimate or are acclimated to a new situation, place, or climate, you become used to it.

words.tr: v. 使适应（新气候或环境）
words.ex: He needs to acclimatize to the hot weather.
words.ex_cn: 他需要适应炎热的天气。
words.en: To acclimatize means to adjust to a new climate, environment, or situation.

words.ex: He tries to attune his ears to the quiet sound.
words.ex_cn: 他试图让自己的耳朵适应那细微的声音。
words.en: If you attune your ear or your senses to something, you become used to it and can recognize it or understand it.

words.tr: v. 遗赠；遗留；把…传下去
words.ex: He bequeathed his house to his daughter.
words.ex_cn: 他把房子遗赠给了他的女儿。
words.en: If you bequeath your money or property to someone, you legally state that they should have it when you die.

words.ex: He left his books as a bequest to the library.
words.ex_cn: 他把他的书作为遗赠给了图书馆。
words.en: A bequest is money or property which you legally leave to someone when you die.

words.tr:
adj. 习惯于
n. 习惯
words.ex: He wont go to school today.
words.ex_cn: 他今天不去学校。
words.en: Accustomed to doing something; in the habit of.

words.ex: He has a habitude of drinking tea every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他有每天早上喝茶的习惯。
words.en: A habitude is a habitual way of behaving or a fixed custom.

words.ex: He modulates his voice to sound calm.
words.ex_cn: 他调节自己的声音以显得平静。
words.en: To modulate means to change or adjust something, such as your voice or a piece of equipment, to achieve a desired effect or to make it suitable for a particular situation.

words.tr: adj. 必需的；必备的；必不可少的；
words.ex: A passport is a requisite for international travel.
words.ex_cn: 护照是国际旅行所必需的。
words.en: Something that is necessary for a particular purpose.

words.ex: You need basic math as a prerequisite for this course.
words.ex_cn: 你学习这门课程的前提是掌握基础数学。
words.en: A prerequisite is something that must exist or happen before something else can exist or happen.

words.tr: n. 详尽解释；专题讨论；专题演讲；专题论文
words.ex: The professor delivered a lengthy disquisition on the history of philosophy.
words.ex_cn: 教授就哲学史发表了一篇冗长的专题论文。
words.en: A disquisition is a long and detailed explanation or discussion of a particular subject.

words.tr: adj. 渴望获得的；贪得无厌的
words.ex: He is acquisitive and always wants more things.
words.ex_cn: 他很有占有欲，总是想要更多东西。
words.en: If you describe a person or their behavior as acquisitive, you mean they are very interested in acquiring money and possessions, often in a way that is selfish or unfair.

words.ex: The court sequestrated the debtor's assets to repay the creditors.
words.ex_cn: 法院扣押了债务人的资产以偿还债权人。
words.en: To sequestrate means to take temporary possession of someone's property until they have paid what they owe or until a legal dispute has been resolved.

words.tr: adj. 精致的；微妙的；易碎的；脆弱的；
words.ex: She wore a delicate lace dress to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一条精致的蕾丝连衣裙去参加派对。
words.en: Something that is delicate is small and beautifully shaped. It can also be easily broken or damaged.

words.tr: adj. 纵容的；宽厚的；溺爱的
words.ex: Her parents are indulgent and let her stay up late.
words.ex_cn: 她的父母很纵容，让她熬夜。
words.en: If you are indulgent, you treat someone with special kindness, often in a way that is not good for them.

words.ex: He showed indulgence when his son stayed out late.
words.ex_cn: 当他儿子深夜外出时，他表现出了纵容。
words.en: If you have an indulgence, you allow yourself to have or do something that you enjoy, especially something that is considered bad for you.

words.ex: Parents shouldn't indulge their children's bad habits.
words.ex_cn: 父母不应该放任孩子的坏习惯。
words.en: To indulge means to allow yourself or someone else to have something enjoyable, especially more than is good for you.

words.tr: adj. 放任的；纵容的；许可的
words.ex: Her parents are permissive and let her stay out late.
words.ex_cn: 她的父母很宽容，让她很晚才回家。
words.en: A permissive person, society, or system allows people a lot of freedom to do what they want.

words.ex: The sailors cleaned the stern of the boat.
words.ex_cn: 水手们打扫了船尾。
words.en: If you describe someone or their behavior as stern, you mean that they are severe or strict.

words.tr: adj. 刻板的；坚硬的；严格的；
words.ex: He has a rigid attitude toward rules.
words.ex_cn: 他对规则的态度很刻板。
words.en: not able to be changed or adapted; not able to be bent or moved; stiff

words.tr: adj. 严格的；缜密的；严密的；
words.ex: The teacher is rigorous about homework deadlines.
words.ex_cn: 老师对作业截止日期要求严格。
words.en: If you are rigorous in something, you are very thorough and strict in the way you do it.

words.ex: He is frugal with his money.
words.ex_cn: 他花钱很节俭。
words.en: If you describe someone as frugal, you mean that they are careful about spending money and use things only when they need to.

words.ex: She is thrifty and saves money every week.
words.ex_cn: 她很节约，每周都存钱。
words.en: If you say that someone is thrifty, you are praising them for saving money and not spending it on unnecessary things.

words.tr: adj. 少量使用的； v. “spare”的现在分词；
words.ex: He uses sparing amounts of sugar in his tea.
words.ex_cn: 他在茶里只用很少的糖。
words.en: If you describe someone as sparing, you mean that they are careful in the way they use something, especially money or food, because there is very little of it.

words.ex: The mode of transportation is a bike.
words.ex_cn: 出行的方式是骑自行车。
words.en: A mode is a particular way or style in which something is done or experienced.

words.ex: He will modify the plan tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天会更改计划。
words.en: To change something slightly, especially in order to make it more suitable for a particular purpose.

words.ex: She wears modish clothes every day.
words.ex_cn: 她每天穿时髦的衣服。
words.en: If something is modish, it is fashionable and modern.

words.ex: The house has a commodious living room.
words.ex_cn: 这所房子有一个宽敞的客厅。
words.en: A commodious room or building is large and has a lot of space.

words.ex: He ate a moderate amount of food.
words.ex_cn: 他吃了适量的食物。
words.en: If you moderate something or if it moderates, it becomes less extreme or violent, or if you moderate a discussion, you help the people in it to reach an agreement.

words.ex: This plan is viable and can be done with little money.
words.ex_cn: 这个计划是可行的，而且用很少的钱就能完成。
words.en: If something is viable, it is capable of doing what it is intended to do.

words.tr: adj. 不能生长发育的；不可行的
words.ex: The embryo was deemed nonviable after the first trimester.
words.ex_cn: 胚胎在第一孕期后被认为不能存活。
words.en: If something is nonviable, it is not capable of succeeding or continuing, especially because it is not practical or it is too expensive.

words.ex: It is feasible to finish the project in one week.
words.ex_cn: 一周内完成这个项目是可行的。
words.en: If something is feasible, it can be done, made, or achieved.

words.ex: This plan is practicable.
words.ex_cn: 这个计划是可行的。
words.en: If a task, plan, or idea is practicable, it can be successfully done or achieved.

words.tr: adj. 精美的；细腻的；强烈的
words.ex: She wore an exquisite dress to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一条精美的裙子去参加派对。
words.en: Something that is exquisite is extremely beautiful or pleasant, especially in a delicate or refined way.

words.ex: This car is economical because it uses little fuel.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车很经济，因为它耗油少。
words.en: Using money, resources, or time in a careful and effective way.

words.tr:
adj. 奢侈的；慷慨给予的；挥霍的；过多的
v. 浪费；挥霍；慷慨给予
words.ex: He threw a lavish party for his birthday.
words.ex_cn: 他为自己的生日举办了一场奢华的派对。
words.en: If you describe something as lavish, you mean that it is very elaborate and impressive and a lot of money has been spent on it. If you say that someone is lavish in the way they behave, you mean that they give, spend, or use a lot of something.

words.tr:
v. 稀释
adj. 经稀释的
words.ex: He dilutes the juice with water.
words.ex_cn: 他用水稀释果汁。
words.en: To dilute a liquid means to make it thinner or weaker by adding water or another liquid to it.

words.tr:
n. 大洪水；暴雨；泛滥
v. 泛滥；大量涌入
words.ex: The rain caused a deluge in the town.
words.ex_cn: 这场雨在镇上引发了洪水。
words.en: A deluge is a severe flood or a very heavy fall of rain that causes a lot of damage.

words.ex: The volcano spilled hot lava down the mountain.
words.ex_cn: 火山喷出炽热的岩浆流下山。
words.en: Lava is the molten rock that comes out of a volcano during an eruption.

words.ex: The lavatory is down the hall.
words.ex_cn: 洗手间在走廊尽头。
words.en: A lavatory is a room equipped with a toilet and sink for washing hands and face.

words.ex: He is stingy with his money.
words.ex_cn: 他花钱很吝啬。
words.en: If you describe someone as stingy, you are criticizing them for being unwilling to spend money or to give or use a lot of something.

words.ex: He is niggardly with his money.
words.ex_cn: 他对待钱很吝啬。
words.en: If you describe someone as niggardly, you are criticizing them for being too mean or unwilling to spend money.

words.tr: adj. 小气的；吝啬的；太节省的
words.ex: His parsimonious nature made him unpopular among colleagues.
words.ex_cn: 他吝啬的本性使得他在同事中不受欢迎。
words.en: Someone who is parsimonious is very unwilling to spend money.

words.tr:
n. (从事某项活动的)规定期限
v. 吝惜；节省
words.ex: He did a short stint as a teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他短暂地当过一段时间老师。
words.en: A stint is a fixed period of time during which someone does a particular job or activity.

words.tr:
adj. 挥霍的；丰富的；慷慨的；不吝惜的
n. 浪子
words.ex: The prodigal son returned home after years.
words.ex_cn: 那个浪子多年后回到了家。
words.en: A prodigal person spends money or resources in a way that is not careful and is too generous.

words.ex: The boy is a piano prodigy at age six.
words.ex_cn: 这个男孩六岁时就是一位钢琴奇才。
words.en: A prodigy is someone who is unusually young and has a great natural ability in a particular area.

words.tr: adj. 惊人的；巨大的；奇异的；巨大的；
words.ex: He showed a prodigious memory for names.
words.ex_cn: 他对名字有着惊人的记忆力。
words.en: If you describe something as prodigious, you are emphasizing that it is very large or impressive.

words.ex: He believes in monogamy and stays with one partner.
words.ex_cn: 他相信一夫一妻制，并且只与一个伴侣在一起。
words.en: The practice or condition of having a single sexual partner during a period of time.

words.ex: He committed bigamy by marrying two women at the same time.
words.ex_cn: 他同时娶了两个女人，犯了重婚罪。
words.en: Bigamy is the act of marrying someone while already legally married to another person.

words.ex: Polygamy is illegal in many countries.
words.ex_cn: 一夫多妻制在许多国家是非法的。
words.en: Polygamy is the custom or practice of having more than one wife or husband at the same time.

words.ex: Polyandry is a rare form of marriage in which one woman is married to several men.
words.ex_cn: 一妻多夫制是一种罕见的婚姻形式，其中一个女人与几个男人结婚。
words.en: Polyandry is a form of marriage in which a woman has more than one husband at the same time.

words.ex: He has a monopoly on selling ice cream in this town.
words.ex_cn: 他在这座小镇上垄断了冰淇淋的销售。
words.en: If a company, person, or state has a monopoly on something such as an industry, they have complete control over it, so that it is impossible for others to become involved in it.

words.ex: He lives in a monocracy where one person controls everything.
words.ex_cn: 他生活在一个由一个人掌控一切的独裁政体中。
words.en: A system of government by one person only.

words.ex: The monarch ruled the country for 50 years.
words.ex_cn: 这位君主统治这个国家长达50年。
words.en: A monarch is a king, queen, emperor, or empress.

words.tr: n. 独白；独角戏；长篇大论
words.ex: He gave a monologue on stage.
words.ex_cn: 他在舞台上发表了一段独白。
words.en: A monologue is a long speech by one person, especially in a play or film, or a long speech by one person during a conversation.

words.tr: n. 单调；枯燥；千篇一律
words.ex: He felt bored because of the monotony of his daily work.
words.ex_cn: 他因为日常工作的单调而感到无聊。
words.en: If you refer to the monotony of something, you are criticizing it because it is boring and has no variety.

words.ex: The farmer shears sheep every spring.
words.ex_cn: 农夫每年春天给羊剪毛。
words.en: To shear means to cut the wool off a sheep or to cut or trim something with scissors or shears.

words.ex: He always keeps his garden trim and neat.
words.ex_cn: 他总是把花园打理得整洁有序。
words.en: To trim something means to make it tidier or more level by cutting a small amount off it.

words.ex: I watched a clip of the movie on YouTube.
words.ex_cn: 我在YouTube上看了这部电影的一个片段。
words.en: A clip is a small device, usually made of metal or plastic, that is specially shaped for holding things together. As a verb, to clip means to cut something, especially to make it shorter or neater.

words.tr:
n. 长柄大镰刀
v. 用长柄大镰刀割
words.ex: The farmer swings the scythe to cut grass.
words.ex_cn: 农夫挥动镰刀割草。
words.en: A scythe is a tool with a long curved blade at right angles to a long handle, used for cutting grass, grain, or other crops.

words.ex: The farmer used a sickle to cut the wheat.
words.ex_cn: 农夫用镰刀割小麦。
words.en: A tool with a curved blade used for cutting crops such as wheat or grass.

words.ex: The subterranean tunnel connects two buildings.
words.ex_cn: 这条地下的隧道连接着两栋大楼。
words.en: Existing, occurring, or done under the earth's surface.

words.ex: The terrestrial animals live on land.
words.ex_cn: 陆地动物生活在陆地上。
words.en: Of, on, or relating to the earth.

words.tr: adj. 地球外的；地外的；外星球的；
words.ex: The movie shows an extraterrestrial life form.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影展示了一种地球外的生命形式。
words.en: An extraterrestrial is a creature that comes from or exists outside the planet Earth.

words.ex: The house has a small terrace with chairs.
words.ex_cn: 这所房子有一个带椅子的小平台。
words.en: A terrace is a flat area of stone or grass next to a building where people can sit.

words.ex: The hikers struggled across the rough terrain.
words.ex_cn: 徒步者艰难地穿越了崎岖的地形。
words.en: Terrain is used to refer to an area of land or a type of land when you are considering its physical features.

words.ex: He inter his dog in the backyard.
words.ex_cn: 他把他的狗关在后院里。
words.en: To place a dead body in the ground or in a tomb.

words.ex: They disinterred the body last week.
words.ex_cn: 他们上周把尸体挖了出来。
words.en: To dig up something that has been buried, especially a corpse.

words.tr:
n. 谜语；费解的事
v. 解谜；出谜；使布满窟窿；打洞
words.ex: He told me a riddle and I solved it.
words.ex_cn: 他给我出了一道谜语，我解出来了。
words.en: A riddle is a question or statement that is deliberately very confusing and has a clever or amusing answer.

words.ex: No example sentences
words.ex_cn: 没有例句
words.en: A conundrum is a confusing and difficult problem or question.

words.ex: The ancient symbol remains an enigma.
words.ex_cn: 这个古代符号仍然是一个谜。
words.en: An enigma is something that is mysterious and difficult to understand.

words.ex: The old man gave an enigmatic smile.
words.ex_cn: 那位老人露出了一个神秘的微笑。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as enigmatic, you mean they are mysterious and difficult to understand.

words.tr: n. 斯芬克斯之谜（指古希腊神话中斯芬克斯提出的难以解答的谜题）
words.ex: He solved the sphinx's riddle like Oedipus did.
words.ex_cn: 他像俄狄浦斯一样解开了斯芬克斯的谜题。

words.ex: The movie had a sequel that came out last year.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影有一部去年上映的续集。
words.en: A sequel is a book, film, or play that continues the story of a previous one.

words.tr: adj. 奉承的；逢迎的；谄媚的
words.ex: He was obsequious to his boss to get a promotion.
words.ex_cn: 他为了得到晋升，对老板阿谀奉承。
words.en: If you describe someone as obsequious, you are criticizing them because they are too eager to help or agree with someone more important than them.

words.ex: He missed three consecutive days of school.
words.ex_cn: 他连续三天没上学。
words.en: Consecutive events, numbers, etc. follow one after another without an interruption.

words.ex: They persecute people for their beliefs.
words.ex_cn: 他们因人们的信仰而迫害他们。
words.en: If someone is persecuted, they are treated cruelly and unfairly, often because of their race, religion, or political beliefs.

words.ex: The court will prosecute him for theft.
words.ex_cn: 法院将因盗窃罪起诉他。
words.en: To prosecute means to institute legal proceedings against someone or to carry on a legal action against a defendant in a court of law. It also means to continue with or carry on an activity or enterprise.

words.tr: v. 接着发生；因而产生
words.ex: The storm ended, and peace ensued.
words.ex_cn: 风暴结束后，和平随之而来。
words.en: If something ensues, it happens immediately after another event, usually as a result of it.

words.tr: n. 编舞艺术；舞蹈编排；
words.ex: The dancer praised the choreography of the ballet.
words.ex_cn: 这位舞者称赞了这部芭蕾舞的编舞艺术。
words.en: Choreography is the art of designing sequences of movements in which motion, form, or both are specified. Choreography may also refer to the design itself. A choreographer is one who creates choreographies by practicing the art of choreography.

words.tr:
v. 合唱；异口同声地说
n. 合唱团；合唱
words.ex: They chorus when the song reaches the bridge.
words.ex_cn: 当歌曲进行到桥段时，他们一起合唱。
words.en: A chorus is a part of a song which is repeated after each verse, or a group of people who sing together.

words.ex: The choir sings every Sunday in church.
words.ex_cn: 唱诗班每周日在教堂唱歌。
words.en: A choir is a group of people who sing together, especially in a church or school.

words.ex: The choreographer taught the dancers new moves.
words.ex_cn: 舞蹈指导教舞者新的动作。
words.en: A choreographer is a person who designs and directs the dance movements in a ballet, show, or film.

words.tr: n. 骑士精神；骑士制度；
words.ex: He showed chivalry by helping the lady carry her bags.
words.ex_cn: 他帮助那位女士提包，展现了骑士精神。
words.en: Chivalry is a set of qualities such as bravery, courtesy, honor, and gallantry toward women, associated with the medieval institution of knighthood.

words.tr: adj. 有骑士风度的；彬彬有礼的；侠义的
words.ex: The knight was chivalrous and helped the lady.
words.ex_cn: 这位骑士有骑士精神，帮助了那位女士。
words.en: A chivalrous man is polite, kind, and unselfish, especially towards women.

words.tr: v. 逐步康复；渐愈；复原
words.ex: He is convalescing at home after surgery.
words.ex_cn: 他手术后在家休养。
words.en: To convalesce means to recover health and strength gradually after sickness or weakness.

words.tr:
n. 骑士；勋章获得者；骑士风度的男子
adj. 傲慢的；豪强的；（对女人）献殷勤的；大方的
words.ex: The knight rode on a horse like a cavalier.
words.ex_cn: 这位骑士骑着马，像个骑士一样。
words.en: If you describe someone as cavalier, you are criticizing them because you think that they do not consider other people's feelings or take account of the seriousness of a situation.

words.ex: The cavalry charged quickly across the field.
words.ex_cn: 骑兵迅速冲过田野。
words.en: The cavalry refers to the part of an army that originally fought on horseback, now typically used in modern armies to refer to units that are mobile and intended for rapid deployment.

words.ex: The knightly virtues of courage and honor were highly valued in medieval times.
words.ex_cn: 勇气和荣誉的骑士美德在中世纪时期被高度重视。
words.en: Relating to or characteristic of a knight; chivalrous.

words.ex: She embellished the dress with flowers.
words.ex_cn: 她用花朵装饰了这条裙子。
words.en: To embellish something means to make it more attractive by adding decorative details or features.

words.ex: She adorned her room with flowers.
words.ex_cn: 她用鲜花装饰了房间。
words.en: To adorn something means to make it more beautiful by adding something to it.

words.tr:
v. （在食物上）加装饰菜；装饰
n. （食物上的）装饰菜；装饰
words.ex: She puts a lemon slice to garnish the drink.
words.ex_cn: 她放一片柠檬来装饰这杯饮料。
words.en: To garnish something means to decorate it with something, especially food with small amounts of different foods.

words.ex: The knight's shield was emblazoned with his family crest.
words.ex_cn: 骑士的盾牌上装饰着他的家族徽章。
words.en: To decorate or adorn with heraldic or other symbols; to celebrate or proclaim something publicly.

words.ex: She bedecks her room with flowers.
words.ex_cn: 她用鲜花装饰她的房间。
words.en: To decorate or adorn something, often in a showy or elaborate manner.

words.tr: v. 加浮雕花纹于；饰以浮饰；使凸出
words.ex: He embosses the card with his name.
words.ex_cn: 他把名字压印在卡片上。
words.en: To decorate a surface by making raised designs or patterns on it.

words.tr: v. 刺绣；绣（花）；加以渲染（或润色）
words.ex: She embroiders flowers on the pillow.
words.ex_cn: 她在枕头上刺绣花朵。
words.en: To embroider means to decorate cloth or other material by sewing patterns or pictures on it with colored threads.

words.ex: She made an embroidery of a flower on the pillow.
words.ex_cn: 她在枕头上绣了一朵花。
words.en: Embroidery is the craft of decorating fabric or other materials using a needle to apply thread or yarn. It may also incorporate other materials such as pearls, beads, quills, and sequins.

words.ex: The Industrial Revolution was a new epoch in history.
words.ex_cn: 工业革命是历史上一个新时代。
words.en: An epoch is a period of time in history or a person's life, typically one marked by notable events or particular characteristics.

words.ex: The invention of the internet changed our era.
words.ex_cn: 互联网的发明改变了我们的时代。
words.en: An era is a period of time that is considered as a single unit because of a particular characteristic or event.

words.tr: n. 时代精神；时代思潮
words.ex: The film captures the zeitgeist of the 1960s.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影捕捉到了20世纪60年代的时代精神。
words.en: The defining spirit or mood of a particular period of history as shown by the ideas and beliefs of the time.

words.ex: The school's ethos is respect for everyone.
words.ex_cn: 这所学校的社會精神特质是尊重每一个人。
words.en: The fundamental character or spirit of a culture; the underlying sentiment that informs the beliefs, customs, or practices of a group or society.

words.tr: adj. 初始的；早期的；未形成的
words.ex: His idea was still inchoate.
words.ex_cn: 他的想法还很不成熟。
words.en: If something is inchoate, it is just beginning to form or is not fully developed or clear.

words.ex: The incipient fire was put out quickly.
words.ex_cn: 初期的小火被迅速扑灭了。
words.en: An incipient situation or quality is one that is just beginning to develop or become noticeable.

words.ex: The embryonic stage is the earliest phase of development.
words.ex_cn: 胚胎阶段是发育的最早时期。
words.en: In an early stage of development; rudimentary.

words.tr: adj. 外来的；外国来的；奇异的；
words.ex: The market sells exotic fruits from other countries.
words.ex_cn: 这个市场出售来自其他国家的外来水果。
words.en: Something that is exotic is unusual and interesting because it comes from or is related to a distant country.

words.ex: He loves eating foreign food.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢吃什么外国食物。
words.en: belonging to or connected with a country that is not your own

words.tr:
n. 外星人；外国人；外侨；
adj. 外国的；陌生的；相异的；
words.ex: The boy saw an alien in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 男孩在森林里看到了一个外星人。
words.en: An alien is someone who is not a citizen of the country in which they live, or a creature from outer space.

words.ex: The butterfly has perfect symmetry.
words.ex_cn: 这只蝴蝶有完美的对称性。
words.en: Symmetry is the quality of being made up of exactly similar parts facing each other or around an axis.

words.ex: The painting has asymmetry in its design.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画的构图不对称。
words.en: The quality of being asymmetrical; lack of symmetry.

words.tr: n. 地震仪；地震检波器
words.ex: The seismometer detected a small earthquake.
words.ex_cn: 地震仪检测到了一次小地震。
words.en: An instrument that measures and records details of earthquakes, such as force and duration.

words.ex: He checked the thermometer to see the temperature.
words.ex_cn: 他看了温度计来查看温度。
words.en: A thermometer is an instrument for measuring and indicating temperature.

words.ex: The barometer shows that the weather will be fine.
words.ex_cn: 晴雨表显示天气会很好。
words.en: A barometer is an instrument that measures atmospheric pressure, used especially in forecasting the weather and determining altitude.

words.ex: The company developed a countermeasure to combat the new security threat.
words.ex_cn: 公司制定了一项对策来应对新的安全威胁。
words.en: A countermeasure is an action or strategy that is intended to counteract or offset another action or situation.

words.tr: adj. 不可估量的；不可测量的；无限的
words.ex: The love between them is immeasurable.
words.ex_cn: 他们之间的爱是无法衡量的。
words.en: If you describe something as immeasurable, you are emphasizing that it is extremely great in size or degree.

words.ex: The mountain is immense.
words.ex_cn: 这座山非常巨大。
words.en: Extremely large or great, especially in scale or degree.

words.ex: He inscribes his name on the stone.
words.ex_cn: 他把名字刻在石头上。
words.en: To write, mark, or engrave (words, symbols, etc.) on a surface, especially as a formal or permanent record.

words.tr: v. 禁止；使失去法律保护
words.ex: The law proscribes selling alcohol to minors.
words.ex_cn: 法律禁止向未成年人出售酒精。
words.en: If a government or other authority proscribes a group or an activity, it officially forbids it or makes it illegal.

words.ex: The ancient stone has an inscription in Latin.
words.ex_cn: 这块古老的石头上有一段拉丁文碑文。
words.en: An inscription is a piece of writing or a short message that is written or carved on something, especially as a formal or permanent record.

words.ex: The lab technician transcribes the DNA sequence into RNA.
words.ex_cn: 实验室技术员将DNA序列转录成RNA。
words.en: To transcribe something means to write it down or to copy it from one form of recording to another.

words.ex: The law circumscribes what companies can do.
words.ex_cn: 法律限制了公司能做的事情。
words.en: To circumscribe something means to limit its size, activity, or scope, often by setting boundaries or restrictions.

words.tr:
n. 插图说明；标题；字幕
v. 加上说明；加上标题；加上字幕
words.ex: The photo has a caption that says 'Happy birthday'.
words.ex_cn: 这张照片有一个标题，写着‘生日快乐’。
words.en: A caption is a short piece of text under a picture in a book, magazine, or newspaper that describes the picture or explains what is happening in it.

words.ex: The book opens with an epigraph from a famous philosopher.
words.ex_cn: 这本书以一位著名哲学家的题词开篇。
words.en: An epigraph is a short quotation or saying at the beginning of a book or chapter, intended to suggest its theme.

words.ex: The epitaph on his grave says, 'Beloved father and friend.'
words.ex_cn: 他墓碑上的墓志铭写着：‘受人爱戴的父亲和朋友。’
words.en: An epitaph is a short piece of writing or a poem about a dead person, especially one written on their gravestone.

words.tr:
v. 潦草地写；匆匆地写；乱涂乱画
n. 潦草的字迹；涂鸦
words.ex: He scribbled his name on the paper.
words.ex_cn: 他在纸上潦草地写了名字。
words.en: To scribble means to write or draw something quickly or carelessly.

words.ex: The walls had colorful graffiti on them.
words.ex_cn: 墙上有着五颜六色的涂画。
words.en: Graffiti is words or pictures that are written or drawn in public places, for example on walls or posters.

words.tr:
v. 乱写；乱画；涂鸦
n. 乱画；乱写；涂鸦
words.ex: He doodled on his notebook during class.
words.ex_cn: 他在上课时在笔记本上乱画。
words.en: If you doodle, you draw small, simple pictures or patterns on a piece of paper, often while you are thinking about something else.

words.tr:
v. 潦草地写；涂写
n. 潦草的笔迹
words.ex: He scrawled his name on the paper.
words.ex_cn: 他在纸上潦草地写了自己的名字。
words.en: If you scrawl something, you write it in a careless and untidy way.

words.ex: The actors rehearse their lines every evening.
words.ex_cn: 演员们每天晚上排练他们的台词。
words.en: To rehearse means to practice a play, piece of music, or other work for later public performance.

words.ex: The actors had a rehearsal before the play.
words.ex_cn: 演出前，演员们进行了一次排练。
words.en: A rehearsal of a play, dance, or piece of music is a practice of it in preparation for a performance.

words.ex: The hearse drove slowly down the street.
words.ex_cn: 灵车缓缓驶过街道。
words.en: A hearse is a vehicle used to carry a coffin to a cemetery or crematorium.

words.ex: He will rehear the case next week.
words.ex_cn: 他下周将重新审理这个案件。
words.en: To hear or consider (a case, argument, etc.) again in a court of law or other official context.

words.ex: He overheard them talking about the party.
words.ex_cn: 他无意中听到他们在谈论派对。
words.en: To overhear is to hear what someone is saying without them knowing that you are listening.

words.ex: He tried to eavesdrop on their conversation.
words.ex_cn: 他试图偷听他们的对话。
words.en: To eavesdrop means to listen secretly to other people's conversations.

words.tr:
n. 搭线窃听装置；窃听或偷录
v. 用窃听器监听；在…装窃听器
words.ex: The police installed a wiretap on the suspect's phone.
words.ex_cn: 警方在嫌疑人的电话上安装了窃听装置。
words.en: A wiretap is a device used to listen secretly to other people's telephone conversations, or the act of using such a device.

words.tr:
v. 利用；
n. 水龙头；轻拍；轻敲；轻击；
words.ex: The company tapped local talent to grow its business.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司利用本地人才来发展业务。
words.en: If you tap something, you hit it with a quick light blow or a series of quick light blows. A tap is a device that controls the flow of a liquid or gas from a pipe or container, for example on a sink.

words.tr: n. 传闻；谣传；道听途说
words.ex: He believed the hearsay without checking the facts.
words.ex_cn: 他没有核实事实就相信了这些流言。
words.en: Information received from other people that one cannot adequately substantiate; rumor.

words.ex: The smell of bread pervades the kitchen.
words.ex_cn: 面包的香味弥漫在整个厨房里。
words.en: If something pervades a place or thing, it is present throughout it.

words.ex: The smell of flowers was pervasive in the garden.
words.ex_cn: 花的香味遍布整个花园。
words.en: Something that is pervasive is present or noticeable throughout a place or thing.

words.ex: He tried to evade the police by driving fast.
words.ex_cn: 他试图通过高速驾驶来逃避警察。
words.en: If you evade something, you find a way of not doing something that you really ought to do.

words.tr: v. 趟水；涉水；艰苦地进行
words.ex: He wades through the shallow river.
words.ex_cn: 他涉水走过浅河。
words.en: To walk through water or another liquid or soft substance that impedes movement.

words.tr:
v. 摇摇摆摆地走；蹒跚
n. 摇摆的步子；蹒跚而行
words.ex: The duck waddle across the pond.
words.ex_cn: 鸭子摇摆着走过池塘。
words.en: To walk with short steps, swaying from side to side, like a duck.

words.ex: The smell of bread permeate the kitchen.
words.ex_cn: 面包的香味弥漫了整个厨房。
words.en: If something permeates a place, it spreads throughout it.

words.tr: v. 使充满；灌注；使怀孕
words.ex: The rain impregnates the soil quickly.
words.ex_cn: 雨水迅速浸透了土壤。
words.en: To make a woman or female animal pregnant; to saturate or fill something with a substance.

words.tr:
v. 弥漫；
adj. 分散的；
words.ex: Smoke began to diffuse through the room.
words.ex_cn: 烟开始弥漫在整个房间里。
words.en: If something such as knowledge or information is diffused, or if it diffuses, it is made known over a wide area or to a lot of people.

words.ex: They will renovate the old house next month.
words.ex_cn: 他们下个月将翻新那栋老房子。
words.en: To renovate means to restore something to a good state of repair or to make it as good as new.

words.ex: He is a novice at playing the guitar.
words.ex_cn: 他是个吉他新手。
words.en: A novice is someone who has just started learning or doing something and does not have much experience.

words.ex: The company values innovation in its products.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司重视产品的创新。
words.en: Innovation is the introduction of new ideas, methods, or things.

words.ex: They plant trees to commemorate the fallen soldiers.
words.ex_cn: 他们种树以纪念阵亡的士兵。
words.en: To commemorate an important event or person means to remember them by means of a special action, ceremony, or specially created object.

words.ex: They placed a memorial at the site of the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他们在事故地点放置了一座纪念物。
words.en: A memorial is a structure or event established to remind people of a person or event.

words.ex: He tries to memorize the words every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天试着记住这些单词。
words.en: To memorize something means to learn it so well that you can remember it perfectly.

words.ex: He has amnesia and cannot remember his name.
words.ex_cn: 他患有失忆症，想不起自己的名字。
words.en: Amnesia is a medical condition that affects someone's memory and they are unable to remember events or information.

words.ex: The government gave amnesty to political prisoners.
words.ex_cn: 政府向政治犯提供了赦免。
words.en: An amnesty is an official pardon granted to a group of people by a government, especially for political offenses.

words.ex: They planted a tree in memory of her.
words.ex_cn: 他们种了一棵树以纪念她。
words.en: If you do something in memory of a dead person, you do it as a way of showing that you want to remember them and that you respect them.

words.ex: Reading books is his favorite pastime.
words.ex_cn: 读书是他最喜欢的消遣。
words.en: A pastime is something that you do because you enjoy it or are interested in it, rather than as a job.

words.ex: The loud music was a diversion from his worries.
words.ex_cn: 那嘈杂的音乐分散了他对烦恼的注意力。
words.en: A diversion is an action or event that attracts your attention away from what you are doing or should be doing.

words.ex: The loud music was a distraction while I tried to study.
words.ex_cn: 当我试图学习时，大声的音乐让我分心。
words.en: Something that makes it difficult for you to concentrate on what you are doing.

words.tr: n. 娱乐；消遣；休闲活动
words.ex: Reading books is his favorite recreation.
words.ex_cn: 读书是他最喜欢的消遣。
words.en: Recreation is activity that you do for enjoyment or amusement when you are not working.

words.ex: The village holds a rite every spring.
words.ex_cn: 这个村庄每年春天都举行一场仪式。
words.en: A rite is a traditional ceremony that is carried out by a particular group or society, especially a religious one.

words.tr: n. （宗教等的）仪式；例行习惯；
words.ex: The village holds a ritual every spring to pray for good weather.
words.ex_cn: 这个村庄每年春天都举行一个仪式，祈求好天气。
words.en: A ritual is a religious service or other ceremony which involves a series of actions performed in a fixed order.

words.ex: He knows good etiquette at dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他知道晚餐时的礼貌规矩。
words.en: Etiquette refers to the customary code of polite behavior in society or among members of a particular profession or group.

words.ex: The old temple is a relic from ancient times.
words.ex_cn: 这座古老的寺庙是来自古代的遗迹。
words.en: An object surviving from an earlier time, especially one of historical or sentimental interest.

words.ex: The remainder of the cake was given to the neighbors.
words.ex_cn: 蛋糕的剩余部分给了邻居。
words.en: The remainder is what is left over after other parts have been taken away or used.

words.ex: He was accused of heresy for rejecting the church's teachings.
words.ex_cn: 他因拒绝教会的教义而被指控为异端。
words.en: Heresy is a belief or opinion that is contrary to the orthodox religious doctrine, especially in Christianity.

words.ex: His views were considered heretical by the religious authorities.
words.ex_cn: 他的观点被宗教权威认为是异端的。
words.en: If someone's beliefs or actions are heretical, they are contrary to the official or accepted beliefs or practices of a particular religion or group.

words.ex: He was called a heretic for his strange beliefs.
words.ex_cn: 因为他奇怪的信仰，他被称为异端。
words.en: A heretic is someone whose beliefs or actions are considered wrong by most people, because they disagree with beliefs that are generally accepted.

words.tr:
n. 异教徒；无宗教信仰者
adj. 异教的；异教徒的；无宗教信仰的
words.ex: He lived in a pagan village long ago.
words.ex_cn: 他很久以前住在一个异教村庄里。
words.en: A pagan is someone who worships many gods or no god, especially one who belongs to a religion that existed before Christianity.

words.ex: Some people follow that cult blindly.
words.ex_cn: 有些人盲目追随那个狂热崇拜。
words.en: A cult is a group of people who have extreme admiration for a particular person, idea, or thing, often following unusual or extreme practices or beliefs.

words.tr:
v. 弄脏；亵渎；玷污
n. 小道；狭谷
words.ex: They defile the river with trash.
words.ex_cn: 他们用垃圾污染了这条河。
words.en: To defile something means to make it dirty or impure. As a noun, it refers to a narrow pass or gorge between mountains.

words.ex: The light bulb has a thin filament.
words.ex_cn: 灯泡有一根细灯丝。
words.en: A filament is a very thin thread or fiber of natural or artificial material.

words.tr:
n. 去骨鱼片；无骨肉片
v. 剔除（鱼或肉）的骨头
words.ex: He cooked a fish fillet for dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他为晚餐烹制了一块鱼排。
words.en: A fillet is a piece of meat or fish that has no bones in it.

words.tr: n. 受公众注意的程度；简介；轮廓；
words.ex: The celebrity's profile rose after the TV interview.
words.ex_cn: 这位名人经过电视采访后，受公众注意的程度提高了。
words.en: A profile is a side view of something, especially a person's face, or a brief description of someone or something.

words.ex: The river is contaminated by factory waste.
words.ex_cn: 这条河被工厂废料污染了。
words.en: To contaminate something means to make it impure or polluted by contact or mixture with something unclean or harmful.

words.ex: He sullied his reputation by lying.
words.ex_cn: 他通过撒谎玷污了自己的声誉。
words.en: To sully something means to spoil or reduce the value of something, especially someone's reputation or the purity of something.

words.tr:
n. 污染；腐坏；玷污
v. 污染；使腐坏；玷污
words.ex: The water has a taint from the factory waste.
words.ex_cn: 这种水因工厂废料而受到污染。
words.en: If something is tainted, it is affected by something bad or undesirable.

words.tr:
v. （使）失去光泽；使晦暗；玷污
n. 晦暗；污渍
words.ex: The silver spoon will tarnish if not cleaned.
words.ex_cn: 如果银勺不清洗，就会变暗。
words.en: If you say that something tarnishes someone's reputation or image, you mean that it causes people to have a worse opinion of them than they would otherwise have had.

words.tr: n. 亵渎上帝；亵渎神明
words.ex: He said it was blasphemy to speak against the holy book.
words.ex_cn: 他说诋毁圣书就是亵渎。
words.en: Blasphemy is the act of insulting or showing contempt or lack of reverence for a god or sacred things.

words.ex: He blasphemed during the prayer.
words.ex_cn: 他在祈祷时说了亵渎的话。
words.en: To blaspheme means to speak in a way that shows irreverence or contempt for God or sacred things.

words.ex: His blasphemous remarks offended many people in the congregation.
words.ex_cn: 他的亵渎神明的言论激怒了教会中的许多人。
words.en: If you describe something as blasphemous, you mean that it is very offensive to people who are religious.

words.tr:
adj. 亵渎的；不敬神的；世俗的
v. 亵渎神灵；亵圣
words.ex: He used profane words during the argument.
words.ex_cn: 他在争吵中说了脏话。
words.en: If someone uses profane language, they use language that is considered to be rude or offensive, especially because it refers to sex or other bodily functions in a way that is considered inappropriate.

words.tr: adj. 虔诚的；衷心的；诚挚的；
words.ex: He is a devout Christian who goes to church every Sunday.
words.ex_cn: 他是一名虔诚的基督徒，每周日都去教堂。
words.en: If you describe someone as devout, you mean that they have a deep religious faith.

words.ex: He devotes his time to helping children.
words.ex_cn: 他投入时间帮助孩子们。
words.en: If you devote yourself, your time, or your energy to something, you spend all or most of your time or energy on it.

words.tr: v. 神化；把…奉若神明；崇拜
words.ex: They deify their ancient heroes.
words.ex_cn: 他们崇拜自己的古代英雄。
words.en: To treat someone or something as a god or goddess, or to consider them as if they were divine.

words.ex: The ancient people worshipped a sun deity.
words.ex_cn: 古人崇拜太阳神。
words.en: A deity is a god or goddess, or anything revered as divine.

words.ex: They hallow the old church on Halloween.
words.ex_cn: 他们在万圣节时敬拜那座老教堂。
words.en: To make holy or set apart as holy; to honor as sacred.

words.ex: It is a taboo to speak his name in this village.
words.ex_cn: 在这个村子里，提到他的名字是禁忌。
words.en: A taboo is a social or religious custom prohibiting or restricting a particular practice or forbidding association with a particular person, place, or thing.

words.ex: The school prohibits students from using phones in class.
words.ex_cn: 学校禁止学生在课堂上使用手机。
words.en: If a law or someone in authority prohibits something, they forbid it or make it illegal.

words.tr: v. 禁止；使失去法律保护
words.ex: The law proscribes selling alcohol to minors.
words.ex_cn: 法律禁止向未成年人出售酒精。
words.en: If a government or other authority proscribes a group or an activity, it officially forbids it or makes it illegal.

words.tr:
n. （法庭的）禁令；禁止
v. 禁止（行动）；阻断
words.ex: The court issued an interdict to stop the construction.
words.ex_cn: 法院发布了一项禁令，以停止施工。
words.en: If someone is interdicted from doing something, they are officially prevented from doing it by a law or a rule.

words.ex: Smoking is verboten in this building.
words.ex_cn: 在这栋楼里吸烟是被禁止的。
words.en: If something is verboten, it is not allowed or is forbidden by law or by someone in authority.

words.tr: n. 避难所；庇护所；庇护；
words.ex: The birds found sanctuary in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 这些鸟在森林里找到了避难所。
words.en: A sanctuary is a place where people or animals are protected from danger or trouble.

words.tr: adj. 极神圣的；神圣不可侵犯的
words.ex: The church's rules were considered sacrosanct and unchangeable.
words.ex_cn: 教堂的规定被认为是神圣不可侵犯的，不可改变的。
words.en: If you describe something as sacrosanct, you mean that it is considered to be special and should not be changed or interfered with.

words.tr:
n. 批准；允许；认可；制裁；处罚
v. 批准；认可；制裁；处罚
words.ex: The company got official sanction to open a new branch.
words.ex_cn: 该公司获得了开设新分公司的正式批准。
words.en: A sanction is a penalty for disobeying a law or rule, or an official permission or approval for an action.

words.tr: adj. 装作圣洁的；伪善的
words.ex: He gave a sanctimonious speech about honesty.
words.ex_cn: 他做了一番关于诚实的伪善演讲。
words.en: If you describe someone as sanctimonious, you disapprove of them because you think that they are trying to appear morally better than other people.

words.ex: They pray to sanctify the new home.
words.ex_cn: 他们祈祷来圣化这个新家。
words.en: To sanctify something means to make it holy or to purify it, often through a religious ceremony or blessing.

words.tr: n. 神龛；神社；圣地；圣殿
words.ex: People visit the shrine to pray.
words.ex_cn: 人们去神社祈祷。
words.en: A shrine is a place of worship which is associated with a particular holy person or object.

words.tr:
n. 保护区；储备；保留；
v. 预订；
words.ex: The wildlife reserve is home to many endangered animals.
words.ex_cn: 这个自然保护区是许多濒危动物的家园。
words.en: If you reserve something such as a table, ticket, or magazine, you arrange for it to be kept for you and not given to anyone else.

words.tr:
v. 保存；保护；保持；
n. （某群体）专有的活动；
words.ex: She preserves fresh fruit by making jam.
words.ex_cn: 她通过做果酱来保存新鲜水果。
words.en: To preserve something means to maintain it in its original or existing state.

words.tr: v. 承认；公开宣称声明
words.ex: He avows his love for her.
words.ex_cn: 他坦承自己对她的爱。
words.en: If you avow something, you declare it or admit it openly.

words.ex: He disavow any connection to the crime.
words.ex_cn: 他否认与这起犯罪有任何关联。
words.en: If you disavow something, you say that you are not responsible for it or you do not agree with it.

words.ex: No one can gainsay the truth.
words.ex_cn: 没有人能否认这个事实。
words.en: If there is no gainsaying something, it is not possible to deny that it is true or that it exists.

words.ex: He visits a religious temple every Sunday.
words.ex_cn: 他每周日都去一座宗教寺庙。
words.en: Relating to or believing in a religion.

words.tr: adj. 虔诚的；信神的；伪善的
words.ex: He is a pious man who prays every day.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个每天祈祷的虔诚的人。
words.en: Someone who is pious is very religious and moral.

words.ex: He shows piety by praying every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天祈祷，表现出虔诚。
words.en: Piety is strong religious belief, or behaviour that is religious or morally correct.

words.ex: The pilgrim walked to the holy place.
words.ex_cn: 朝圣者步行前往圣地。
words.en: A pilgrim is a person who journeys to a sacred place for religious reasons.

words.ex: He is an apprentice in a car repair shop.
words.ex_cn: 他是汽车修理店的一名学徒。
words.en: An apprentice is a young person who works for someone in order to learn their skill.

words.ex: He was a faithful disciple of the teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他是老师的一名忠实弟子。
words.en: A disciple is a follower or student of a teacher, leader, or philosopher.

words.tr: v. 置入神龛中；入庙祀奉；奉为神圣；珍藏
words.ex: They enshrined the ancient statue in a golden shrine.
words.ex_cn: 他们把这尊古代雕像置入了一个金色神龛中。
words.en: If something such as a tradition or a right is enshrined in something such as a constitution or law, it is protected by it.

words.tr: v. 奉为神圣；贡献；奉献
words.ex: They consecrate the church with prayer and song.
words.ex_cn: 他们用祈祷和歌声将教堂奉为神圣。
words.en: To consecrate something means to officially declare it to be holy and to be used for religious purposes.

words.tr: n. 亵渎；亵圣；悖理逆天的行为
words.ex: He committed sacrilege by breaking the holy statue.
words.ex_cn: 他砸了圣像，犯下了亵渎之罪。
words.en: If someone's behaviour or actions are described as sacrilege, they are considered to show a lack of respect for something that is regarded as holy or very important.

words.ex: They tried to desecrate the holy church.
words.ex_cn: 他们试图亵渎那座神圣的教堂。
words.en: To desecrate something means to spoil or damage something that is considered to be holy or very important.

words.ex: He execrates lies and dishonesty.
words.ex_cn: 他痛恨谎言和不诚实。
words.en: To express great loathing for; to curse or denounce vehemently.

words.ex: The priest stood at the pulpit and spoke loudly.
words.ex_cn: 牧师站在讲坛上大声讲话。
words.en: A pulpit is a raised platform in a church from which the preacher delivers a sermon.

words.tr: n. （教堂中的）诵经台；（演讲的）讲台；斜面高腿小桌
words.ex: The professor stood behind the lectern to deliver his speech.
words.ex_cn: 教授站在讲台后面发表演讲。
words.en: A lectern is a tall desk with a sloping top from which someone, typically a speaker or lecturer, can read while standing up.

words.ex: The mayor stood on the dais to give a speech.
words.ex_cn: 市长站在讲台上发表演讲。
words.en: A dais is a raised platform in a room for a speaker or honored guest.

words.tr: n. 鬼怪；幽灵；缠绕心头的恐惧
words.ex: The specter of famine haunted the war-torn region.
words.ex_cn: 饥荒的幽灵在饱受战争蹂躏的地区徘徊。
words.en: A specter is a ghost or a phantom, or something that haunts or perturbs the mind.

words.ex: The phantom appeared in the mist near the old house.
words.ex_cn: 幻影出现在老房子附近的薄雾中。
words.en: A phantom is a ghost or a figment of the imagination.

words.ex: An apparition appeared in the dark hallway.
words.ex_cn: 一个幽灵出现在黑暗的走廊里。
words.en: An apparition is a ghost or ghostlike image of a person.

words.ex: The prophet told the people about the coming storm.
words.ex_cn: 预言者告诉人们即将到来的风暴。
words.en: A prophet is a person who is believed to be chosen by God to lead the people and to tell them what God wants them to do.

words.ex: The old woman made a prophecy about the rain.
words.ex_cn: 那位老妇人预言了会有雨。
words.en: A prophecy is a statement that something will happen in the future, especially one made by someone with religious or magical powers.

words.ex: The old woman prophesied rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 那位老妇人预告明天会下雨。
words.en: To say that something will happen in the future, especially as a result of divine inspiration.

words.ex: He criticized others for lying, but his own actions showed hypocrisy.
words.ex_cn: 他批评别人撒谎，但自己的行为却表现出虚伪。
words.en: The practice of claiming to have moral standards or beliefs to which one's own behavior does not conform; pretense.

words.ex: He is hypocritical when he says he hates lying but lies all the time.
words.ex_cn: 他说他讨厌撒谎，却总是撒谎，这很虚伪。
words.en: If you accuse someone of being hypocritical, you mean that they pretend to have qualities, beliefs, or feelings that they do not really have.

words.ex: He is a hypocrite because he says he loves peace but fights often.
words.ex_cn: 他是个伪君子，因为他声称热爱和平，却经常打架。
words.en: A hypocrite is someone who pretends to have certain beliefs or opinions that they do not really have, especially in order to deceive people.

words.ex: Hypotension can lead to dizziness and fainting.
words.ex_cn: 血压过低可能导致头晕和昏厥。
words.en: Hypotension is a condition in which a person's blood pressure is abnormally low, which can lead to symptoms such as dizziness and fainting.

words.tr: adj. 过分活跃的；多动的；亢奋的
words.ex: The hyperactive child runs around the room all day.
words.ex_cn: 这个多动的孩子整天在房间里跑来跑去。
words.en: If someone is hyperactive, they are extremely active and find it difficult to relax or concentrate on one thing for very long.

words.ex: He uses hyperbole when he says he is dying of hunger.
words.ex_cn: 当他说到自己快饿死了时，他用了夸张的说法。
words.en: Hyperbole is a way of speaking or writing that makes someone or something sound bigger, better, more, etc. than they are.

words.tr: n. 天花乱坠的广告宣传；炒作；
words.ex: The new phone got a lot of hype before its release.
words.ex_cn: 这款新手机在发布前受到了大量天花乱坠的广告宣传。
words.en: If someone or something is hyped, they are praised or advertised a lot in newspapers, on television, etc., especially in a way that is intended to make them seem very exciting or important.

words.ex: He used an analogy to explain how the heart works.
words.ex_cn: 他用了一个类比来解释心脏是如何工作的。
words.en: If you make or draw an analogy between two things, you show that they are similar in some way.

words.ex: The two situations are analogous.
words.ex_cn: 这两种情况是相似的。
words.en: If one thing is analogous to another, the two things are similar in some way.

words.ex: The two dogs are similar in color.
words.ex_cn: 这两只狗的颜色很相似。
words.en: If one thing is similar to another, or if two things are similar, they have features that are the same.

words.tr:
adj. 平行的；
n. 类似的事物；
words.ex: The two lines are parallel and never meet.
words.ex_cn: 这两条线是平行的，永远不会相交。
words.en: Something that is parallel to something else is similar to it in many ways, or happens at the same time as it.

words.ex: His altruism made him donate all his money to the poor.
words.ex_cn: 他的利他主义让他把所有钱捐给了穷人。
words.en: Altruism is the belief in or practice of disinterested and selfless concern for the well-being of others.

words.ex: He gave his last dollar to the homeless man, showing an altruistic heart.
words.ex_cn: 他把最后一美元给了那个无家可归的人，表现出一颗无私的心。
words.en: If you describe someone as altruistic, you mean that they show unselfish concern for the welfare of others.

words.tr: vi. 争吵，发生口角；争论
words.ex: They altercate over small things every day.
words.ex_cn: 他们每天为小事争吵。
words.en: To argue or dispute vehemently.

words.tr:
adj. 交替的；轮流的；间隔的；
v. （使）交替；（使）轮流；
words.ex: We take alternate days off work.
words.ex_cn: 我们隔天休息一次。
words.en: If something alternates between two things, it repeatedly changes from one to the other and back again.

words.tr: n. 不在犯罪现场证明；辩解；托辞
words.ex: He gave an alibi that he was at home.
words.ex_cn: 他提供了一个他在家的不在场证明。
words.en: An alibi is a form of defense used in criminal procedure wherein a defendant attempts to prove that he or she was in some other place at the time the alleged offense was committed.

words.tr:
n. 别名；化名
adv. 又被称为；另外地
words.ex: He uses an alias to hide his real name.
words.ex_cn: 他使用一个化名来隐藏他的真实姓名。
words.en: An alias is a false or assumed identity, especially one used by a criminal.

words.tr: n. 自我主义；利己主义
words.ex: He acts out of egoism, not kindness.
words.ex_cn: 他出于利己主义行事，而不是善意。
words.en: Egoism is the belief that you should think about your own interests and needs rather than those of other people.

words.tr: adj. 自我中心的；利己的；
words.ex: He is egocentric and only talks about himself.
words.ex_cn: 他以自我为中心，只谈论自己。
words.en: If you describe someone as egocentric, you mean that they are only concerned with their own needs and desires, and not with those of other people.

words.ex: The priest placed the offering on the altar.
words.ex_cn: 牧师把供品放在祭坛上。
