words.ex: The room is airy with windows on all sides.
words.ex_cn: 这个房间四面都有窗户，通风很好。
words.en: If a place or room is airy, it has a lot of fresh air because it is large or has a lot of windows.

words.tr:
adj. 精神错乱的；疯狂的
v. 使（精神）错乱；打乱；“derange”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: The deranged man shouted at the sky.
words.ex_cn: 那个精神错乱的人对着天空大喊。
words.en: If someone is deranged, they are behaving in a way that is not normal because they are mentally ill.

words.ex: The loud noise deranges the baby.
words.ex_cn: 巨大的噪音让婴儿烦躁不安。
words.en: To derange something is to disturb the normal arrangement or functioning of it, often causing confusion or disorder.

words.tr: adj. 发狂的；精神错乱状态的
words.ex: The demented man laughed loudly in the street.
words.ex_cn: 那个精神失常的男人在街上大声笑。
words.en: Someone who is demented behaves in a wild and uncontrolled way because they are mentally ill.

words.tr: adj. 神志不清的；极度兴奋的；发狂的
words.ex: He was delirious after the fever.
words.ex_cn: 他发烧后神志不清。
words.en: If someone is delirious, they are not able to think or speak in a sensible and reasonable way, usually because they are very ill and have a fever.

words.ex: The loud noise startle the bird.
words.ex_cn: 巨大的噪音惊动了那只鸟。
words.en: If something or someone startles you, they surprise and frighten you slightly.

words.tr: v. 使说不出话来；使目瞪口呆
words.ex: The magic trick dumbfound everyone.
words.ex_cn: 这个魔术让所有人都惊呆了。
words.en: If someone or something dumbfounds you, they surprise you so much that you cannot think or speak for a moment.

words.tr: v. 使惊呆；使惊愕；使神志不清
words.ex: The sudden noise stupefied everyone.
words.ex_cn: 突然的噪音让所有人都惊呆了。
words.en: To stupefy someone means to make them unable to think clearly or to be surprised or shocked.

words.tr: adj. 渴望的；失意的；留恋的
words.ex: She gave a wistful glance at the old photo.
words.ex_cn: 她对着那张旧照片投以怀念的一瞥。
words.en: If you are wistful, you are thinking about something that you want but cannot have, especially something that you used to have in the past.

words.tr:
n. 渴望；向往
adj. 渴望的；向往的
v. 渴望；渴求；“yearn”的现在分词
words.ex: He has a yearning for home.
words.ex_cn: 他渴望回家。
words.en: A yearning is a strong feeling of wanting something, especially something that you know you may not be able to have.

words.tr:
n. 渴望；热望
adj. 渴望的；热望的
v. 渴望；热望；“long”的现在分词
v. 用练马绳训练马的各种步态
words.ex: Her longing for home grew stronger each day.
words.ex_cn: 她对家的渴望与日俱增。
words.en: A strong feeling of wanting something or someone.

words.ex: He covets his neighbor's car.
words.ex_cn: 他垂涎邻居的车。
words.en: If you covet something, you have a very strong desire to possess it, especially something that belongs to someone else.

words.tr: adj. 贪心的；贪婪的；渴望的
words.ex: He is covetous of his neighbor's new car.
words.ex_cn: 他垂涎邻居的新车。
words.en: If you are covetous, you have a strong desire to possess something, especially something that belongs to someone else.

words.ex: The smell of food whetted his appetite.
words.ex_cn: 食物的香味刺激了他的食欲。
words.en: To whet something means to make it sharper or more intense.

words.tr: v. 压制；平息；消除；减轻
words.ex: The police tried to quell the riot.
words.ex_cn: 警察试图平息暴乱。
words.en: To quell something, especially a feeling, means to stop it or reduce its intensity.

words.tr:
v. 发扑哧声；嘎吱嘎吱的走；压制；遏制
n. 嘎吱声；扑哧声
words.ex: He tried to squelch the rumors about him.
words.ex_cn: 他试图压制关于他的谣言。
words.en: To squelch means to suppress or silence something, often forcefully, or to make a sucking sound as when walking through mud.

words.ex: The cat got enmeshed in the old net.
words.ex_cn: 猫被缠在旧网里了。
words.en: To involve someone or something in a difficult situation from which it is hard to escape.

words.ex: The cat got entangled in the string.
words.ex_cn: 猫被绳子缠住了。
words.en: If something is entangled in something else, it is caught or twisted around it, or mixed with it so that it is difficult to separate the two things.

words.tr: v. 使卷入；使陷入；牵连
words.ex: He didn't want to embroil his friend in the argument.
words.ex_cn: 他不想让朋友卷入这场争吵。
words.en: To involve someone in a difficult or complicated situation.

words.tr: v. 使气馁；使胆怯；吓倒
words.ex: The loud noise did not daunt her.
words.ex_cn: 巨大的噪音并没有吓倒她。
words.en: If something daunts you, it makes you feel slightly afraid or worried about dealing with it.

words.ex: The memory of the accident still haunts him.
words.ex_cn: 那场事故的记忆仍然长期困扰着他。
words.en: If something unpleasant haunts you, you keep thinking or worrying about it over a long period of time. A place that is haunted is believed to be visited regularly by a ghost.

words.ex: He likes to flaunt his new car.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢炫耀他的新车。
words.en: If you flaunt something, you show it off in a way that is intended to attract people's attention and make them envious.

words.tr:
v. 吹嘘；自夸
n. 吹嘘；自夸
words.ex: He likes to vaunt his new car.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢炫耀他的新车。
words.en: To boast about or praise (something) excessively.

words.ex: He taunted his brother for losing the game.
words.ex_cn: 他奚落弟弟比赛输了。
words.en: If someone taunts you, they say unkind or insulting things to you, especially about your weaknesses or failures.

words.tr:
n. 远足；短途旅游
v. 远足；短途旅游
words.ex: We decided to take a jaunt to the countryside.
words.ex_cn: 我们决定去乡间远足。
words.en: A short journey or excursion, especially one taken for pleasure.

words.tr: adj. 轻松活泼的；得意洋洋的；自信满满的
words.ex: He walked with a jaunty step, clearly pleased with himself.
words.ex_cn: 他步伐轻快，显然对自己感到很满意。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as jaunty, you mean that they are full of confidence and energy.

words.tr:
v. 闲逛；漫步
n. 闲逛；漫步
words.ex: We decided to saunter along the beach.
words.ex_cn: 我们决定沿着海滩漫步。
words.en: If you saunter somewhere, you walk there in a slow, relaxed way.

words.tr: adj. 触觉的；能触知的；手感好的
words.ex: The child learns through tactile objects like blocks.
words.ex_cn: 孩子通过触觉物体如积木来学习。
words.en: Relating to the sense of touch; perceptible by touch.

words.tr: n. 中风；划水动作；一击；
words.ex: He had a stroke last year.
words.ex_cn: 他去年中风了。
words.en: A stroke is a medical condition in which poor blood flow to the brain results in cell death. It can also refer to an act of hitting or striking someone or something, or a gentle movement of the hand over a surface.

words.tr:
n. 爱抚；抚摸；吻
v. 爱抚；抚摸；吻
words.ex: Her caress made the baby feel safe.
words.ex_cn: 她的爱抚让婴儿感到安全。
words.en: A caress is a gentle, loving touch or gesture, often given to show affection.

words.ex: He fondled the old photo gently.
words.ex_cn: 他轻轻抚摸着那张旧照片。
words.en: To handle or touch (someone or something) in a tender and loving way.

words.tr:
v. 轻拍；轻触；轻敷
n. 轻拍；少量；能手；比目鱼
words.ex: He dabbed paint on the wall with a brush.
words.ex_cn: 他用刷子在墙上点了一些颜料。
words.en: To dab means to touch something lightly and quickly, often with a cloth or your fingers, in order to clean it, dry it, or apply something to it.

words.tr: v. 用鼻擦、触、推；紧挨；偎依
words.ex: The cat nuzzled its owner's hand.
words.ex_cn: 那只猫在主人的手上蹭来蹭去。
words.en: If an animal nuzzles you, it pushes or rubs its nose or head against you in a gentle and affectionate way.

words.tr:
v. （使）发痒；胳肢；逗乐
n. 痒；胳肢；呵痒
words.ex: The feather tickles my arm.
words.ex_cn: 羽毛挠得我手臂发痒。
words.en: If something tickles you, it touches you in a way that makes you laugh or feel slightly uncomfortable, usually because it is touching a sensitive part of your body. If something tickles you, it also makes you feel amused or pleased.

words.tr:
v. 目瞪口呆地看；裂开
n. 目瞪口呆地看；裂口
words.ex: The children gape at the magic show.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们张大嘴看着魔术表演。
words.en: To open the mouth wide; to stare with open mouth, as in wonder.

words.tr:
n. 凝视；注视；
v. 凝视；注视；
words.ex: His gaze fixed on the sunset.
words.ex_cn: 他的凝视固定在日落上。
words.en: If you gaze at someone or something, you look steadily at them for a long time, for example because you find them attractive or interesting, or because you are thinking about something else.

words.tr:
v. 偷看；微露出；唧唧叫
n. 窥视；隐现；唧唧声
words.ex: He peeped through the keyhole to see what was inside.
words.ex_cn: 他从钥匙孔里偷看里面是什么。
words.en: To look quickly and often secretively at something or someone.

words.tr:
v. 偷看；窥视
n. 偷看；窥见
words.ex: He peeked through the keyhole.
words.ex_cn: 他从钥匙孔里偷看。
words.en: To peek means to look at something quickly and secretly, especially through a small opening or from behind something.

words.tr:
n. 同辈；同等的人；
v. 凝视；
words.ex: He feels comfortable talking to his peers.
words.ex_cn: 他觉得和同辈交谈很自在。
words.en: A peer is someone who is equal to another in abilities, qualifications, age, background, or social status. As a verb, to peer means to look keenly or with difficulty at someone or something.

words.tr:
v. 眯着眼看；斜视
n. 斜视；一瞥
words.ex: He squints to see the small letters.
words.ex_cn: 他眯着眼睛看那些小字。
words.en: To squint means to look at something with your eyes partly closed in order to see better, or because of bright light. It can also refer to a condition where the eyes do not look in the same direction.

words.tr:
v. 嬉戏
n. 嬉戏；欢乐的活动
words.ex: The children were frolicking in the park.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在公园里嬉戏。
words.en: If people or animals frolic, they play or move in a lively, happy way.

words.ex: The puppy frisks around the garden.
words.ex_cn: 小狗在花园里活蹦乱跳。
words.en: To frisk someone means to search them for weapons or illegal items by feeling their body with your hands.

words.tr: n. 云雀；百灵鸟；玩乐；嬉戏
words.ex: The lark sings loudly at sunrise.
words.ex_cn: 云雀在日出时大声歌唱。
words.en: A lark is a small brown bird that is known for its beautiful song. It is also used to describe a carefree adventure or a playful activity.

words.ex: The children cavort in the park.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在公园里嬉戏。
words.en: If people cavort, they leap about in a noisy and excited way because they are very happy.

words.tr:
v. 雀跃；欢跃
n. 刺山柑花蕾；雀跃；不法活动；胡闹
words.ex: The children capered around the playground.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在操场上雀跃。
words.en: A caper is a playful leap or jump. It can also refer to a prank or a mischievous act. Additionally, it denotes the pickled flower bud of the caper bush, used as a condiment.

words.tr:
v. （使）磨损；（使）烦躁；（使）紧张
n. 磨损处；吵闹；争吵
words.ex: The rope began to fray after years of use.
words.ex_cn: 这根绳子用了多年后开始磨损。
words.en: If something such as cloth or rope frays, or if something frays it, its threads or fibres start to come apart from each other and it becomes weaker. A situation of conflict or intense competition can also be referred to as a fray.

words.tr: n. 打群架；小骚乱；吵架；闹事
words.ex: The police quickly dispersed the affray in the market.
words.ex_cn: 警察迅速驱散了市场上的骚乱。
words.en: An affray is a noisy and violent fight, especially in a public place.

words.ex: He gave her a gift to appease her anger.
words.ex_cn: 他送她一份礼物来平息她的怒气。
words.en: If you try to appease someone, you try to stop them from being angry by giving them what they want.

words.ex: The government tried appeasement to calm the protests.
words.ex_cn: 政府试图通过平息来安抚抗议活动。
words.en: The action or process of appeasing.

words.tr:
v. 使迷惑；使不知所措
n. 迷惑；困惑；为难
words.ex: The tricky question nonplused the teacher.
words.ex_cn: 这个棘手的问题让老师不知所措。
words.en: To cause to be at a loss as to what to say, think, or do; perplex.

words.ex: The old eggs began to addle in the heat.
words.ex_cn: 这些旧鸡蛋在热中开始腐臭。
words.en: If something addles someone's mind or brain, it confuses them and makes them unable to think clearly.

words.ex: The teacher helps students demystify math problems.
words.ex_cn: 老师帮助学生弄明白数学问题。
words.en: To make something easier to understand by explaining it in a clear and simple way.

words.ex: He tried to mollify his angry friend with an apology.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用道歉来安抚他生气的朋友。
words.en: To mollify someone means to make them feel calmer and less angry, upset, or worried.

words.tr:
adj. 柔软的
n. 润肤剂；软化剂
words.ex: The cream is an emollient for dry skin.
words.ex_cn: 这种乳霜是用于干皮肤的润肤剂。
words.en: An emollient is a substance that softens or soothes the skin, or a statement or action that calms or reduces tension.

words.ex: The child found a mollusk on the beach.
words.ex_cn: 孩子在海滩上发现了一只软体动物。
words.en: A mollusk is a type of animal with a soft body, often protected by a hard shell, such as a snail or clam.

words.ex: They will demolish the old building next week.
words.ex_cn: 他们下周会拆掉那座旧建筑。
words.en: To demolish something such as a building means to destroy it completely. It can also mean to defeat someone completely in a discussion, argument, or competition.

words.ex: The wind began to abate after the storm.
words.ex_cn: 风暴过后，风开始减弱。
words.en: If something bad or undesirable abates, it becomes much less strong or severe.

words.tr:
n. 折扣；退款
v. 减少
words.ex: He got a rebate on his new TV.
words.ex_cn: 他买新电视时得到了一笔回扣。
words.en: A rebate is a partial refund to someone who has paid too much for tax, rent, or a utility.

words.ex: The conductor waved the baton to start the symphony.
words.ex_cn: 指挥家挥动指挥棒，开始交响乐。
words.en: A baton is a stick that is used by conductors to direct an orchestra or choir, by a relay runner to pass on the race, or by a police officer as a weapon.

words.tr:
v. 猛击；重打
n. 猛击；重击；盛会
words.ex: He bashed the door with his fist.
words.ex_cn: 他用拳头猛击门。
words.en: To hit someone or something very hard; a big party or celebration.

words.tr: n. 迷信；迷信观念（或思想）；
words.ex: He avoids walking under ladders because of superstition.
words.ex_cn: 他因为迷信而不愿从梯子下走过。
words.en: A superstition is a belief or practice resulting from ignorance, fear of the unknown, trust in magic or chance, or a false conception of causation.

words.tr: adj. 迷信的；有迷信观念的
words.ex: He is superstitious about walking under ladders.
words.ex_cn: 他迷信地认为走过梯子下面会带来厄运。
words.en: Having or showing a belief in superstitions.

words.ex: He immersed the cloth in water.
words.ex_cn: 他把布浸在水里。
words.en: To immerse something or someone means to put them into a liquid so that they are completely covered by it. It can also mean to involve oneself deeply in a particular activity or interest.

words.ex: He immerses himself in reading books every night.
words.ex_cn: 他每晚都埋头读书。
words.en: To plunge or dip into a liquid; to submerge.

words.ex: The virtual reality game is immersive.
words.ex_cn: 这个虚拟现实游戏非常沉浸式。
words.en: Providing, involving, or characterized by deep absorption or immersion in something (especially a particular activity or environment).

words.ex: The two companies will merge next year.
words.ex_cn: 这两家公司明年将合并。
words.en: To combine or unite to form a single entity.

words.ex: The diver submerge to explore the coral reef.
words.ex_cn: 潜水员潜水去探索珊瑚礁。
words.en: To submerge something means to put it below the surface of a liquid, especially water. If something submerges, it goes below the surface of a liquid.

words.tr:
v. 投入；跳入
n. 跳进；骤降
words.ex: He plunged into the cold water.
words.ex_cn: 他跳进了冰冷的水里。
words.en: If something or someone plunges in a particular direction, especially into water, they fall, rush, or throw themselves in that direction.

words.ex: There was a dip in sales last month.
words.ex_cn: 上个月销售额有所下降。
words.en: To dip something means to put it into a liquid and then take it out again.

words.tr: adj. 乐天的；自信的；红润的
words.ex: Despite the setbacks, he remained sanguine about the future.
words.ex_cn: 尽管遭遇挫折，他对未来仍然充满希望。
words.en: If you are sanguine about something, you are cheerful and confident that things will happen in the way that you want them to.

words.tr: adj. 红润的；红的；淡红色
words.ex: Her complexion was ruddy from the cold weather.
words.ex_cn: 她的脸色因寒冷的天气而变得红润。
words.en: Having a healthy red color, especially in the face.

words.ex: The roller coaster exhilarates the children.
words.ex_cn: 过山车让孩子们感到兴奋。
words.en: To make someone feel very happy and excited.

words.ex: The movie was hilarious and made us laugh a lot.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影非常搞笑，让我们笑得很开心。
words.en: If you describe something as hilarious, you mean that it is extremely funny and it makes you laugh a lot.

words.ex: The movie caused hilarity among the audience.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影让观众们哄堂大笑。
words.en: Hilarity is great amusement and laughter.

words.ex: He felt remorse after lying to his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他在对朋友撒谎后感到后悔。
words.en: Remorse is a strong feeling of sadness and regret about something wrong that you have done.

words.tr:
adj. 尖刻的；刻薄的；尖锐讥讽的
n. 媒染剂
words.ex: His mordant wit made everyone laugh.
words.ex_cn: 他尖刻的幽默让大家笑了。
words.en: A mordant remark is one that is critical and sarcastic. In chemistry, a mordant is a substance used to set dyes on fabrics or tissue sections by forming a coordination complex with the dye which then attaches to the fabric or tissue.

words.ex: She took a tiny morsel of cake and savored it slowly.
words.ex_cn: 她咬了一小口蛋糕，慢慢地品味着。
words.en: A morsel is a small piece or amount of something, especially food.

words.ex: He felt contrition after lying to his mother.
words.ex_cn: 他在对母亲撒谎后感到悔恨。
words.en: The state of feeling remorseful and penitent.

words.tr: adj. 空虚的；茫然的；空洞的
words.ex: His vacuous smile made no sense.
words.ex_cn: 他空洞的微笑毫无意义。
words.en: If you describe someone's mind or smile as vacuous, you are critical of them because they lack intelligence, understanding, or seriousness.

words.ex: The police told everyone to evacuate the building.
words.ex_cn: 警察让所有人撤离大楼。
words.en: To evacuate means to remove people from a place of danger to a safer place.

words.tr: adj. 很快消失的；渐消散的；短暂的
words.ex: The evanescent mist disappeared at sunrise.
words.ex_cn: 那消散的薄雾在日出时消失了。
words.en: Something that is evanescent quickly disappears or fades away.

words.ex: He bought a new mirror because of his vanity.
words.ex_cn: 他因为虚荣心买了一面新镜子。
words.en: The quality of being vain; excessive pride in or admiration of one's own appearance or achievements.

words.tr: adj. 非常自负的；自命不凡的
words.ex: He was so vainglorious that he believed his own press clippings.
words.ex_cn: 他非常自负，以至于相信了自己的新闻剪报。
words.en: If you describe someone as vainglorious, you are critical of them because they are very proud of their own status, abilities, or achievements.

words.ex: The void on the page made the text look empty.
words.ex_cn: 页面上的空白让文字看起来空荡荡的。
words.en: If you describe a situation or a feeling as a void, you mean that it seems empty because there is nothing interesting or worthwhile about it.

words.ex: The room was devoid of any furniture.
words.ex_cn: 这个房间里全无家具。
words.en: If you say that someone or something is devoid of a quality or thing, you are emphasizing that they have none of it.

words.ex: The soda begins to effervesce when you open it.
words.ex_cn: 当你打开汽水时，它开始冒泡。
words.en: If a liquid effervesces, it produces small bubbles of gas.

words.ex: He was a fervid supporter of the cause.
words.ex_cn: 他是这一事业的热心支持者。
words.en: Having or displaying a passionate intensity.

words.tr: adj. 热烈的；强烈的；热情的
words.ex: He is a fervent supporter of environmental protection.
words.ex_cn: 他是环境保护的热心支持者。
words.en: having or showing very strong and sincere feelings about something

words.tr: adj. 极端或过分热情的
words.ex: His perfervid speech inspired the crowd.
words.ex_cn: 他那热情洋溢的演讲激励了群众。
words.en: Having or showing intense and fervent feeling or enthusiasm.

words.tr: n. 漠不关心；无动于衷
words.ex: He showed nonchalance when the glass fell.
words.ex_cn: 当玻璃杯掉下来时，他表现得若无其事。
words.en: The state of being nonchalant; a casual lack of concern or indifference.

words.ex: The song evokes happy memories of childhood.
words.ex_cn: 这首歌唤起了对童年的美好回忆。
words.en: To evoke a particular memory, idea, emotion, or response means to cause it to occur.

words.ex: The president convoked an emergency meeting.
words.ex_cn: 总统召集了一次紧急会议。
words.en: To call together for a meeting or assembly.

words.ex: The teacher will revoke his privilege to use the computer.
words.ex_cn: 老师将撤销他使用电脑的权限。
words.en: If someone in authority revokes something such as a law, license, or agreement, they cancel it.

words.ex: He invoked the law to protect his rights.
words.ex_cn: 他援引法律来保护自己的权利。
words.en: If you invoke a law, rule, or principle, you refer to it as a reason or justification for something.

words.ex: His rude words provoked her anger.
words.ex_cn: 他粗鲁的话激怒了她。
words.en: If you provoke someone, you deliberately annoy them and try to make them behave aggressively.

words.ex: His provocative words made everyone angry.
words.ex_cn: 他挑衅的话让所有人都生气了。
words.en: If you describe something as provocative, you mean that it is intended to make people react angrily or argue against it.

words.tr: adj. 大声喊叫的；喧嚷的
words.ex: The vociferous crowd shouted for change.
words.ex_cn: 喧闹的人群大声要求变革。
words.en: If you describe someone as vociferous, you mean that they speak with great energy and determination, because they want their views to be heard.

words.tr: adj. 模棱两可的；含糊其词的；难以解释的
words.ex: His answer was equivocal.
words.ex_cn: 他的回答模棱两可。
words.en: If you are equivocal, you are deliberately vague in what you say, because you want to avoid speaking the truth or making a decision.

words.tr:
n. 燃料；燃油；
v. 加剧；
words.ex: The rocket uses fuel 627 for propulsion.
words.ex_cn: 火箭使用627号燃料推进。
words.en: Fuel is a substance such as coal, gas, or oil that is burned to provide heat or power.

words.tr:
v. 触发；引起；发动；
n. 诱因；触发；
words.ex: The loud noise triggered the alarm.
words.ex_cn: 巨大的噪音触发了警报。
words.en: A trigger is a device that activates a mechanism when it is pulled or pressed. It can also refer to something that causes a particular reaction or development.

words.tr:
adj. 麻木的；失去知觉的
v. 使麻木；使迟钝
words.ex: His fingers felt numb after being in the cold.
words.ex_cn: 他的手指在寒冷中变得麻木。
words.en: If a part of your body is numb, you cannot feel it, usually for a short time.

words.ex: The cold caused a numbness in my fingers.
words.ex_cn: 寒冷导致我的手指麻木。
words.en: Numbness is a lack of feeling in part of your body, often caused by cold, injury, or emotion.

words.tr:
n. 麻醉剂；麻醉药
adj. 麻醉的
words.ex: The doctor gave him an anesthetic before the surgery.
words.ex_cn: 医生在手术前给他用了麻醉剂。
words.en: An anesthetic is a substance that causes loss of sensation or consciousness, used especially to prevent pain during medical procedures.

words.tr:
n. 喧嚷；大声的要求
v. 喧嚷；大声地要求
words.ex: The crowd made a loud clamor for justice.
words.ex_cn: 人群为正义发出大声喧哗。
words.en: If people are clamoring for something, they are demanding it in a noisy or angry way.

words.tr: v. 否认；放弃；拒绝承认
words.ex: He disclaims any responsibility for the mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他否认对这个错误负有任何责任。
words.en: If you disclaim knowledge of something or disclaim responsibility for something, you say that you did not know about it or are not responsible for it.

words.tr: v. 慷慨陈词；高声朗诵
words.ex: He likes to declaim poetry in front of the class.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢在全班面前朗诵诗歌。
words.en: To declaim means to speak or recite something in a dramatic or impassioned way, often in public.

words.tr: v. 要求归还；收回；开垦；感化
words.ex: He wants to reclaim his lost wallet.
words.ex_cn: 他想要要求归还他丢失的钱包。
words.en: If you reclaim something that you have lost or that has been taken away from you, you succeed in getting it back. If you reclaim land, you make it suitable for use, for example by draining it or by getting rid of unwanted buildings or plants.

words.ex: Hiking up the mountain was a strenuous task.
words.ex_cn: 爬山是一项艰苦的任务。
words.en: Requiring or using great effort or exertion.

words.ex: Climbing the mountain was an arduous task.
words.ex_cn: 爬山是一项艰巨的任务。
words.en: Something that is arduous is difficult and tiring, and involves a lot of effort.

words.tr: n. 严酷的考验；痛苦的经历；煎熬
words.ex: He went through a long ordeal before he found peace.
words.ex_cn: 他在找到平静之前经历了一段漫长的磨难。
words.en: An ordeal is a very unpleasant and prolonged experience.

words.ex: The doctor ran a trial to test the new medicine.
words.ex_cn: 医生进行了试验来测试这种新药。
words.en: A trial is a formal meeting in a law court, at which a judge and jury listen to evidence and decide whether a person is guilty of a crime.

words.ex: The family is in a difficult plight after losing their home.
words.ex_cn: 这家人在失去家园后陷入了困境。
words.en: A plight is a difficult or adverse situation, especially one that is hard to escape. It can also refer to a solemn promise or pledge.

words.tr: n. 困境；窘境；困惑之境；进退两难
words.ex: He is in a quandary about what to do.
words.ex_cn: 他对于该做什么感到困惑。
words.en: A situation in which you are unsure or confused about what to do.

words.ex: He found himself in a predicament when he lost his wallet.
words.ex_cn: 当他丢掉钱包时，他陷入了困境。
words.en: A predicament is a difficult, perplexing, or trying situation.

words.tr: n. 绝境；僵局；死路；死胡同
words.ex: The talks reached an impasse and no one could move forward.
words.ex_cn: 谈判陷入了僵局，没有人能继续前进。
words.en: An impasse is a situation in which no progress can be made or no advancement is possible, especially because of disagreement; a deadlock.

words.ex: The two teams are in a deadlock over the budget.
words.ex_cn: 两个团队在预算上陷入了僵局。
words.en: A deadlock is a situation in which no progress can be made or no agreement is reached, especially because of a disagreement between two or more parties.

words.tr:
n. 僵局；和棋；僵持状态
v. 使陷入僵局
words.ex: The two players are in a stalemate.
words.ex_cn: 两位选手陷入了僵局。
words.en: A situation in which further action or progress by opposing parties seems impossible.

words.tr:
v. 神气十足地走；大摇大摆地走
n. 大摇大摆；神气十足
words.ex: He walks with swagger down the street.
words.ex_cn: 他大摇大摆地走在街上。
words.en: If someone swaggers, they walk in a very proud and confident way, often in a way that annoys other people.

words.tr:
n. 撑杆；支柱
v. 趾高气扬地走；昂首阔步
words.ex: The bridge has metal struts to support the weight.
words.ex_cn: 这座桥有金属撑杆来支撑重量。
words.en: If someone struts, they walk in a proud way, with their chest out and trying to look important.

words.tr: v. 腾跃；阔步行走；神气地快速走动
words.ex: The horse prances across the field.
words.ex_cn: 那匹马在田野上欢快地跳跃。
words.en: If a horse prances, it moves with high, springy steps.

words.ex: The game simulates real traffic conditions.
words.ex_cn: 这个游戏模拟了真实的交通状况。
words.en: To simulate is to create a model or representation of a situation, process, or system for the purpose of study, analysis, or training. It involves imitating the conditions of a real event or environment to understand its effects or to practice responses to it.

words.ex: The two events happened simultaneously.
words.ex_cn: 这两个事件同时发生了。
words.en: Happening, existing, or done at the same time.

words.tr: n. 复制本；摹本；仿制品；传真
words.ex: He sent a facsimile of the document to his office.
words.ex_cn: 他把文件的传真发到了办公室。
words.en: An exact copy of a document, picture, or piece of writing, especially one that has been made by a machine.

words.ex: He tries to assimilate new words every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天努力吸收新单词。
words.en: To assimilate means to take in and understand fully ideas, information, or culture, or to make something become part of a group or system.

words.ex: He feigns sleep to avoid talking.
words.ex_cn: 他假装睡觉以避免交谈。
words.en: If someone feigns a particular feeling, attitude, or physical condition, they try to make other people think that they have it or are experiencing it, although this is not true.

words.tr:
n. 佯攻；虚击；假象
v. 佯攻；佯击；假装
words.ex: He made a feint to the left, then kicked right.
words.ex_cn: 他假装向左，然后右脚踢球。
words.en: A feint is a movement or an action that is intended to deceive someone, for example by making them think that you are going to do one thing when you are really going to do something else.

words.ex: The bonus is an incentive to work harder.
words.ex_cn: 奖金是努力工作的动机。
words.en: Something that encourages a person to do something or to work harder.

words.ex: The bright light was a stimulus for the baby to open his eyes.
words.ex_cn: 明亮的光线是让婴儿睁开眼睛的刺激物。
words.en: Something that causes growth or activity.

words.tr:
n. （赶牲畜的）尖头棒；激励；刺激
v. 刺激；驱使
words.ex: The farmer used a goad to guide the oxen.
words.ex_cn: 农夫用一根尖头棒赶牛。
words.en: If you goad someone, you deliberately make them feel angry or irritated, often causing them to react by doing something.

words.ex: The new law gave impetus to environmental protection.
words.ex_cn: 新法律为环境保护提供了推动力。
words.en: Something that gives a process impetus or an impetus makes it happen or progress more quickly.

words.ex: The noise infuriates my neighbor.
words.ex_cn: 噪音让我的邻居非常生气。
words.en: To make someone extremely angry.

words.ex: He shouted with fury when he lost the game.
words.ex_cn: 当他输掉比赛时，他愤怒地大喊。
words.en: Fury is a feeling of intense anger.

words.tr: adj. 狂怒的；暴怒的；激烈的
words.ex: He was furious when he lost his keys.
words.ex_cn: 他丢了钥匙时非常生气。
words.en: If someone is furious, they are extremely angry.

words.tr: v. 激怒；使急躁；使疼痛
words.ex: Loud noises irritate my baby.
words.ex_cn: 噪音会激怒我的宝宝。
words.en: If something irritates you, it keeps annoying you.

words.ex: The loud noise vexes my little brother.
words.ex_cn: 嘈杂的声音让我的小弟弟很烦。
words.en: If someone or something vexes you, they make you feel annoyed, puzzled, and frustrated.

words.ex: She picked up a needle to sew the button.
words.ex_cn: 她拿起一根针来缝纽扣。
words.en: A needle is a thin, pointed piece of metal that is used in sewing. It has a hole at one end for thread to pass through.

words.tr:
n. 荨麻
v. 激怒
words.ex: The child touched the nettle and got a rash.
words.ex_cn: 孩子碰了荨麻，皮肤起了疹子。
words.en: A nettle is a wild plant with leaves that sting when you touch them. If you are nettled by something, it makes you annoyed or angry.

words.ex: His comments about her appearance really riled her.
words.ex_cn: 他对她外貌的评论真的激怒了她。
words.en: To make someone annoyed or irritated.

words.tr:
n. 熏香；熏香的烟
v. 使愤怒；激怒
words.ex: The smell of incense fills the room.
words.ex_cn: 香火的气味充满了房间。
words.en: Incense is a substance that is burned for its pleasant smell, often used in religious ceremonies. As a verb, to incense means to make someone very angry.

words.tr: v. 使人耿耿于怀；令人怀恨
words.ex: The unfair comment still rankles him.
words.ex_cn: 那句不公平的话仍让他耿耿于怀。
words.en: If something rankles, it continues to cause you irritation, bitterness, or pain, often because you think it was unfair.

words.ex: The loud noise exasperates me.
words.ex_cn: 巨大的噪音让我感到烦躁。
words.en: If someone or something exasperates you, they annoy you and make you feel frustrated or impatient.

words.ex: His crabbed handwriting made it hard to read the note.
words.ex_cn: 他难辨认的笔迹让这张便条很难阅读。
words.en: If you describe someone's writing or behavior as crabbed, you mean that it is small and difficult to read or understand, often because it is written in a very small space.

words.tr: adj. 刻薄的；尖刻的；脾气坏的
words.ex: His waspish remarks stung more than he intended.
words.ex_cn: 他尖刻的评论比他预期的更伤人。
words.en: If you describe someone as waspish, you mean that they are rather bad-tempered and critical.

words.tr: adj. 易怒的；坏脾气的；乖戾的
words.ex: She had a peevish tone when she spoke.
words.ex_cn: 她说话时带着一种易怒的语气。
words.en: If you describe someone as peevish, you mean that they are easily irritated by unimportant things.

words.tr: adj. 肝病的；易怒的；情绪烦躁的
words.ex: He felt liverish after eating too much fried food.
words.ex_cn: 他吃了太多油炸食物后感到不舒服。

words.tr: adj. 胆汁的；患胆病的；脾气暴躁的；恶心头痛的；让人恶心的
words.ex: He had a bilious complexion due to his illness.
words.ex_cn: 由于生病，他的脸色发黄。
words.en: If someone is bilious, they are bad-tempered or irritable, often because of a problem with their liver or digestion.

words.tr: adj. 脾气坏的；爱吵架的；爱发牢骚的
words.ex: The cantankerous old man yells at his neighbors every morning.
words.ex_cn: 那位脾气暴躁的老人每天早上都对邻居大喊大叫。
words.en: Someone who is cantankerous is bad-tempered and quarrels with people.

words.tr: adj. 脾气坏的；乖戾的；傲慢的
words.ex: The surly man refused to say hello.
words.ex_cn: 那个脾气暴躁的人拒绝打招呼。
words.en: If someone is surly, they are unfriendly and bad-tempered.

words.ex: He could espy a small boat in the distance.
words.ex_cn: 他能隐约看见远处有一条小船。
words.en: If you espy something, you see or notice it, often when it is not easy to do so.

words.ex: The spy practiced espionage to get secret information.
words.ex_cn: 间谍从事间谍活动以获取秘密信息。
words.en: The practice of spying or of using spies, typically by governments to obtain political and military information.

words.ex: He was circumspect before signing the contract.
words.ex_cn: 他在签署合同之前非常谨慎。
words.en: If you are circumspect, you think carefully about something before doing it, because there may be risks involved.

words.ex: He tries to introspect about his mistakes.
words.ex_cn: 他试图反省自己的错误。
words.en: If you introspect, you examine your own ideas, thoughts, and feelings.

words.tr:
n. 回想
v. 回想
words.ex: In retrospect, I should have studied harder.
words.ex_cn: 回顾过去，我本该更努力学习的。
words.en: When you consider something in retrospect, you think about it afterwards, and often have a different opinion about it from the one that you had at the time.

words.ex: He speculates that it will rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他推测明天会下雨。
words.en: If you speculate about something, you make guesses about its nature or identity, or about what might happen.

words.ex: He was a despicable liar who hurt everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个可鄙的骗子，伤害了所有人。
words.en: If you say that a person or action is despicable, you are emphasizing that they are extremely nasty, cruel, or evil.

words.tr: adj. 既胖又圆的；洪亮的
words.ex: The old man has a rotund belly.
words.ex_cn: 这位老人有一个圆滚滚的肚子。
words.en: If someone is rotund, they are round and fat.

words.ex: The wheel rotates slowly.
words.ex_cn: 轮子缓慢地转动。
words.en: To rotate means to turn or cause to turn around an axis or center.

words.tr: n. 死记硬背；机械的做法；生搬硬套
words.ex: He learned the poem by rote.
words.ex_cn: 他通过死记硬背学会了这首诗。
words.en: Rote is the process of learning something by repeating it many times without thinking about it or understanding it.

words.tr: adj. 转动的；旋转的；轮流的
words.ex: The rotatory motion of the blades generated lift.
words.ex_cn: 叶片的旋转运动产生了升力。
words.en: Relating to or causing rotation; revolving.

words.tr: adj. 左旋的；使平面偏振光向左旋转的
words.ex: The solution is levorotatory, so it turns polarized light to the left.
words.ex_cn: 该溶液是左旋的，因此使偏振光向左旋转。

words.tr: adj. 右旋的；使偏振光向右旋转的
words.ex: The sugar solution is dextrorotatory and turns polarized light to the right.
words.ex_cn: 糖溶液是右旋的，使偏振光向右旋转。

words.tr:
v. 调情；轻率地对待
n. 与多人调情的人
words.ex: He flirts with her at the coffee shop.
words.ex_cn: 他在咖啡店向她调情。
words.en: If you flirt with someone, you behave as if you are sexually attracted to them, in a playful or not very serious way.

words.tr: adj. 轻浮的；调情的；爱调戏的
words.ex: She had a flirtatious smile that made him feel uneasy.
words.ex_cn: 她那轻浮的微笑让他感到不安。
words.en: If you describe someone as flirtatious, you mean that they behave towards people in a way which suggests they are sexually attracted to them, usually in a playful or not very serious way.

words.tr:
adj. 本国的；地方的
n. 方言；土语
words.ex: He wrote the poem in the vernacular language.
words.ex_cn: 他用本国语言写了这首诗。
words.en: The vernacular is the language or dialect spoken by the ordinary people in a particular country or region.

words.ex: He speaks a local dialect in his village.
words.ex_cn: 他在村子里说一种地方方言。
words.en: A dialect is a form of a language that is spoken in a particular area and that uses some of its own words, grammar, and pronunciations.

words.ex: You must comply with the rules.
words.ex_cn: 你必须遵守规则。
words.en: To act in accordance with a wish or command.

words.ex: The company showed compliance with safety rules.
words.ex_cn: 该公司遵守了安全规定。
words.en: The act of complying with a wish, request, or demand; obedience.

words.ex: He conform to the rules of the school.
words.ex_cn: 他遵守学校的规章制度。
words.en: To conform means to behave in a way that is accepted by most people or to obey a rule, law, or custom.

words.tr: phrase. 一致的；连贯的；始终如一的
words.ex: He is consistent in doing his homework every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天坚持做作业。
words.en: Remain uniform and unchanging over time.

words.tr:
n. 诡计；花言巧语
v. 欺骗；诱骗；消磨
words.ex: He used a clever wile to deceive his enemies.
words.ex_cn: 他使用了一个巧妙的诡计来欺骗他的敌人。
words.en: If you say that someone uses wiles to achieve something, you mean that they use clever methods to persuade people to do what they want.

words.tr: adj. 狡猾的；诡计多端的
words.ex: The wily fox tricked the chicken.
words.ex_cn: 狡猾的狐狸骗了鸡。
words.en: If you describe someone or their behaviour as wily, you mean that they are clever at achieving what they want, especially by tricking people.

words.ex: He used guile to trick the guard.
words.ex_cn: 他用诡计骗过了守卫。
words.en: Guile is the quality of being skilled at deceiving people in order to achieve something.

words.ex: He gave an artful answer to the tricky question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个棘手的问题给出了一个巧妙的回答。
words.en: If you describe someone as artful, you mean that they are clever and skillful at achieving what they want, especially by deceiving people.

words.ex: The crafty fox stole the chicken at night.
words.ex_cn: 那只狡猾的狐狸在夜里偷了鸡。
words.en: If you describe someone as crafty, you mean they are clever at achieving their aims by indirect or deceitful methods.

words.ex: The mole dug a tunnel under the garden.
words.ex_cn: 鼹鼠在花园下挖了一条隧道。
words.en: A mole is a small animal with black fur that lives underground. It can also refer to a small dark spot on the skin or a person who secretly gives information to an enemy.

words.tr:
n. 雀斑；小斑点
v. （使）生雀斑
words.ex: He has freckles on his nose.
words.ex_cn: 他的鼻子上有雀斑。
words.en: A freckle is a small, brownish spot on the skin, often becoming more pronounced through exposure to the sun.

words.ex: He has a small birthmark on his arm.
words.ex_cn: 他的手臂上有一个小胎记。
words.en: A birthmark is a mark on the skin that is present at birth or appears shortly after birth.

words.tr: n. 皮肤上的红色小疱
words.ex: He has a small pimple on his nose.
words.ex_cn: 他鼻子上有个小痘痘。
words.en: A pimple is a small raised spot on the skin that is often red and may contain pus.

words.ex: He has a dimple when he smiles.
words.ex_cn: 他笑的时候有一个酒窝。
words.en: A dimple is a small natural indentation in the flesh on a part of the human body, especially one formed in the cheeks when someone smiles.

words.ex: The army besiege the small town.
words.ex_cn: 军队围攻这座小镇。
words.en: To surround a place with armed forces in order to capture it or force its surrender; to overwhelm someone with requests or complaints.

words.ex: The castle endured a long siege during the war.
words.ex_cn: 这座城堡在战争中经历了长期的围攻。
words.en: A siege is a military operation in which enemy forces surround a town or building, cutting off essential supplies, with the aim of compelling those inside to surrender.

words.ex: The castle was beleaguered by enemy soldiers.
words.ex_cn: 城堡被敌军围攻。
words.en: To beleaguer means to lay siege to or to cause trouble or difficulty for someone over a period of time.

words.ex: The book encompasses all basic math skills.
words.ex_cn: 这本书包含了所有基础数学技能。
words.en: If something encompasses particular things, it includes them.

words.ex: He acquiesced to his boss's decision.
words.ex_cn: 他默许了老板的决定。
words.en: If you acquiesce in something, you agree to do what someone wants or to accept what they do even though you may not agree with it.

words.tr: adj. 默认的；默许的；顺从的
words.ex: He was acquiescent when they asked him to wait.
words.ex_cn: 当他们让他等待时，他顺从了。
words.en: If you are acquiescent, you are ready to agree to do what someone wants, or to accept what they do.

words.tr: n. 解脱；平息；死亡；静止
words.ex: He gave the old machine a quietus.
words.ex_cn: 他让那台旧机器彻底停了下来。
words.en: A quietus is a final release or discharge, especially from life; a death or something that causes death.

words.ex: The volcano is quiescent now.
words.ex_cn: 这座火山现在处于休眠状态。
words.en: Someone or something that is quiescent is quiet and inactive.

words.ex: He crammed the suitcase with clothes.
words.ex_cn: 他把衣服塞满了行李箱。
words.en: If you cram things or people into a place, you put them into it even though there is hardly enough room for them.

words.tr: v. 刻苦学习；n. 刻苦学习的人
words.ex: He is swotting for his math exam.
words.ex_cn: 他正在为数学考试拼命学习。
words.en: To study hard, especially for an examination; a person who studies hard.

words.ex: The heavy snow cumbered our progress.
words.ex_cn: 大雪阻碍了我们的前进。
words.en: To hinder or obstruct the movement or progress of someone or something.

words.ex: The old system is cumbersome and slow.
words.ex_cn: 这个旧系统复杂而低效。
words.en: Something that is cumbersome is large and heavy and therefore difficult to carry, wear, or handle.

words.ex: He is encumbered by too many debts.
words.ex_cn: 他被太多的债务拖累。
words.en: To encumber someone or something means to weigh them down or to block or hinder them.

words.tr: adj. 斜躺的；斜靠的；侧卧的
words.ex: The old man sat in a recumbent chair.
words.ex_cn: 那位老人坐在一张躺椅上。
words.en: A recumbent position or posture is one in which a person is lying down or leaning back in a relaxed manner.

words.tr: adj. 在职的；负有义务的；
words.ex: The incumbent mayor won the election again.
words.ex_cn: 现任市长再次赢得了选举。
words.en: An incumbent is someone who currently holds a particular office or position, especially in politics. It can also refer to something that is necessary as a duty or responsibility.

words.ex: He succumbed to the illness after a long fight.
words.ex_cn: 经过长期抗争后，他最终死于疾病。
words.en: If you succumb to temptation, pressure, or something such as an illness, you do something that you want to do, or you give in to the pressure or illness, often after a period of trying not to.

words.ex: The hen incubate eggs until they hatch.
words.ex_cn: 母鸡孵化鸡蛋直到小鸡孵出。
words.en: to keep eggs warm so that they develop and hatch, or to keep cells, bacteria, etc. at a suitable temperature so that they develop

words.tr: n. 梦淫妖；沉重的精神负担
words.ex: He felt like an incubus pressing on his chest at night.
words.ex_cn: 他感觉晚上有个梦魇压在胸口。
words.en: An incubus is a male demon believed to have sexual intercourse with sleeping women. In a broader sense, it can also refer to a cause of distress or anxiety.

words.ex: He had a concubine in the old palace.
words.ex_cn: 他在旧宫殿里有一个妾。
words.en: A concubine is a woman who lives with a man but has a lower status than his wife or wives.

words.ex: He spoke with candor about his mistakes.
words.ex_cn: 他坦率地谈到了自己的错误。
words.en: the quality of being open and honest in expression; frankness.

words.tr: adj. 坦率的；坦诚的；偷拍的
words.ex: He gave a candid answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了坦率的回答。
words.en: If you are candid, you are honest and say what you really think.

words.ex: The incandescent bulb gives off a warm light.
words.ex_cn: 白炽灯发出温暖的光。
words.en: Emitting light as a result of being heated.

words.tr:
n. 熏香；熏香的烟
v. 使愤怒；激怒
words.ex: The smell of incense fills the room.
words.ex_cn: 香火的气味充满了房间。
words.en: Incense is a substance that is burned for its pleasant smell, often used in religious ceremonies. As a verb, to incense means to make someone very angry.

words.tr:
n. 佯攻；虚击；假象
v. 佯攻；佯击；假装
words.ex: He made a feint to the left, then kicked right.
words.ex_cn: 他假装向左，然后右脚踢球。
words.en: A feint is a movement or an action that is intended to deceive someone, for example by making them think that you are going to do one thing when you are really going to do something else.

words.tr:
n. 毛孔；小孔
v. 细看；钻研；凝视
words.ex: Sweat comes out through the pores of the skin.
words.ex_cn: 汗水通过皮肤上的毛孔排出。
words.en: A pore is a tiny opening in a surface that allows liquids or gases to pass through. As a verb, to pore means to read or study something very carefully.

words.ex: The sponge is porous and absorbs water easily.
words.ex_cn: 海绵是多孔的，容易吸水。
words.en: If something is porous, it has a lot of tiny holes in it that allow water or air to pass through slowly.

words.ex: The nonporous surface does not absorb water.
words.ex_cn: 这个无孔隙的表面不吸水。
words.en: Not allowing liquid or air to pass through; impermeable.

words.ex: He sat by the window to ponder his future.
words.ex_cn: 他坐在窗边深思自己的未来。
words.en: If you ponder something, you think about it carefully.

words.ex: He peruses the newspaper every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上浏览报纸。
words.en: To read or examine something carefully or thoroughly.

words.tr: v. 考虑；深思；凝视；思考…的可能性
words.ex: He contemplates quitting his job.
words.ex_cn: 他正在考虑辞去工作。
words.en: If you contemplate an action, you think about whether to do it or not.

words.tr:
n. 伪装；伪装物；
v. 伪装；掩饰；
words.ex: He wore a hat and glasses as a disguise.
words.ex_cn: 他戴了帽子和眼镜作为伪装。
words.en: To disguise means to change your appearance or behavior so that people will not recognize you, or to make something seem different from what it really is.

words.ex: He spoke in the guise of a friend.
words.ex_cn: 他以朋友的伪装说话。
words.en: An external form, appearance, or manner of presentation, typically concealing the true nature of something.

words.ex: His smile belieed his true feelings.
words.ex_cn: 他的微笑掩饰了他真实的情感。
words.en: If one thing belies another, it hides the true situation and so creates a false idea or image of someone or something.

words.ex: The soldier wore camouflage to hide in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 士兵穿着伪装服在森林中隐藏自己。
words.en: Camouflage is the way in which some animals are colored and shaped so that they cannot easily be seen in their natural surroundings.

words.ex: She wore a white veil on her wedding day.
words.ex_cn: 她在婚礼那天戴了一条白色的面纱。
words.en: A veil is a piece of thin soft cloth that women sometimes wear over their heads and which can also cover their face.

words.ex: He dissimulated his anger to keep the peace.
words.ex_cn: 他掩饰了自己的愤怒以维持和平。
words.en: To dissimulate means to hide your real feelings, character, or intentions.

words.ex: He dissembles when he is nervous.
words.ex_cn: 当他紧张时，他会假装。
words.en: To dissemble means to conceal one's true motives, feelings, or beliefs.

words.tr:
v. 注意；留心
n. 注意；留心
words.ex: He did not heed the warning.
words.ex_cn: 他没有理会那个警告。
words.en: If you heed someone's advice or warning, you pay attention to it and do what they suggest.

words.tr: adj. 不留心的；不注意的
words.ex: He was heedless of the warning signs.
words.ex_cn: 他对警告信号毫不在意。
words.en: If you are heedless of someone or something, you do not take any notice of them.

words.tr:
n. 火花；火星；
v. 激发；
words.ex: The match produced a small spark.
words.ex_cn: 火柴产生了一个小火花。
words.en: A spark is a small fiery particle thrown off from a fire, alight in ashes, or produced by striking together two hard surfaces such as stone or metal.

words.tr:
n. 打巴掌
v. 用巴掌打
adv. 恰好地；猛地
words.ex: He gave the table a loud smack.
words.ex_cn: 他重重地拍了一下桌子。
words.en: If you smack someone or something, you hit them with your open hand. It can also refer to the sound made by a quick, sharp blow or the taste or flavor of something.

words.ex: He showed spunk when he stood up to the bully.
words.ex_cn: 当他勇敢地对抗欺凌者时，他表现出了勇气。
words.en: Courage and determination.

words.tr:
v. 诋毁；诽谤；中伤
n. 诋毁；诽谤；中伤
words.ex: He spread slander about his neighbor.
words.ex_cn: 他散布了关于他邻居的诽谤。
words.en: Slander is the action or crime of making a false spoken statement damaging to a person's reputation.

words.tr:
v. 含混不清地说话；诋毁；诽谤
n. 诽谤；诋毁；污辱
words.ex: He slurrs his words when he is tired.
words.ex_cn: 当他累了的时候，说话含糊不清。
words.en: If someone slurs their speech or if their speech slurs, they do not pronounce each word clearly, because they are drunk, ill, or sleepy. A slur is an insulting remark which could damage someone's reputation.

words.tr:
n. （文字）诽谤
v. 发表文字诽谤（某人）
words.ex: He wrote a false story about her, and it was libel.
words.ex_cn: 他写了一篇关于她的虚假文章，这是诽谤。
words.en: A libel is a published false statement that is damaging to a person's reputation; a written defamation.

words.ex: He tries to denigrate his rival's ideas.
words.ex_cn: 他试图贬低对手的想法。
words.en: If you denigrate someone or something, you criticize them unfairly or insult them.

words.ex: He never disparages his classmates.
words.ex_cn: 他从不贬低他的同学。
words.en: If you disparage someone or something, you speak about them in a way which shows that you do not have a good opinion of them.

words.ex: He did not agree with the policy, but he did not want to vilify those who supported it.
words.ex_cn: 他不同意这项政策，但不想诋毁那些支持它的人。
words.en: To vilify someone means to say or write very unpleasant things about them in order to hurt their reputation.

words.ex: He was reviled by his opponents for his controversial views.
words.ex_cn: 由于他的有争议的观点，他受到了对手的辱骂。
words.en: To revile someone means to criticize them in an abusive or angrily insulting manner.

words.ex: The train runs on the rail.
words.ex_cn: 火车在铁轨上行驶。
words.en: A rail is a horizontal bar, typically made of metal or wood, used as a support or barrier; or a track made of steel rails along which trains run.

words.ex: The injury incapacitated him for weeks.
words.ex_cn: 这次受伤使他几周无法行动。
words.en: To make someone unable to do something, especially because of injury or illness.

words.tr: adj. 吹毛求疵的；挑剔的
words.ex: He made a captious comment about the small mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他对一个小错误发表了挑剔的评论。
words.en: Tending to find fault or raise petty objections.

words.ex: The magic show captivates the children.
words.ex_cn: 魔术表演吸引了孩子们。
words.en: If you are captivated by someone or something, you find them fascinating and attractive.

words.tr:
v. 挑毛病；吹毛求疵
n. 挑剔；挑毛病
words.ex: He cavils at every small mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他挑剔每一个小错误。
words.en: If you say that someone cavils at something, you mean that they make criticisms of it that you think are unimportant or unnecessary.

words.ex: He caught a big carp in the river.
words.ex_cn: 他在河里钓到了一条大鲤鱼。
words.en: To complain or find fault continually, typically about trivial matters.

words.ex: He abnegates his own needs for his family.
words.ex_cn: 他为了家人而放弃自己的需求。
words.en: If you abnegate something, you renounce or reject it.

words.ex: He tries to negate the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他试图否认事实。
words.en: If someone negates something, they say that it does not exist or is not true.

words.ex: He reneged on his promise to help me.
words.ex_cn: 他背弃了帮助我的承诺。
words.en: If someone reneges on a promise or an agreement, they do not do what they have promised or agreed to do.

words.tr:
n. 叛徒；变节者；叛教者
adj. 背叛的；变节的
v. 背叛
words.ex: He is a renegade who left the team suddenly.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个突然离开团队的叛徒。
words.en: A renegade is a person who deserts and betrays an organization, country, or set of principles.

words.ex: The error is negligible.
words.ex_cn: 这个误差可以忽略。
words.en: If you describe something as negligible, you mean that it is so small or unimportant that it is not worth considering or worrying about.

words.tr:
adj. 沮丧的；低落的；垂头丧气的
v. 使…情绪低落；使沮丧；“deject”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: He felt dejected after failing the test.
words.ex_cn: 他考试没及格后感到沮丧。
words.en: If you are dejected, you feel miserable or unhappy, especially because you have just been disappointed by something.

words.tr: adj. 郁闷的；抑郁的；孤僻的
words.ex: He was morose after losing his job.
words.ex_cn: 他失业后变得忧郁。
words.en: If you describe someone as morose, you mean that they are very unhappy, bad-tempered, and unwilling to talk or be sociable.

words.tr: adj. 沮丧的；泄气的；失望的
words.ex: He became despondent after losing his job.
words.ex_cn: 他失业后变得沮丧。
words.en: If you are despondent, you are very unhappy because you have been experiencing difficulties that you think you will not be able to overcome.

words.tr: adj. 精力充沛的；热情洋溢的；
words.ex: The exuberant children ran around the park.
words.ex_cn: 那些精力充沛的孩子们在公园里跑来跑去。
words.en: If you are exuberant, you are full of energy, excitement, and cheerfulness.

words.tr: adj. 奔放的；兴高采烈的；沸腾的
words.ex: He is ebullient after winning the prize.
words.ex_cn: 他赢得奖后非常兴奋。
words.en: If you describe someone as ebullient, you mean that they are lively and full of enthusiasm or excitement about something.

words.ex: He tried to dissuade her from quitting her job.
words.ex_cn: 他试图劝她不要辞掉工作。
words.en: If you dissuade someone from doing something, you persuade them not to do it.

words.ex: He tried to persuade her to stay.
words.ex_cn: 他试图说服她留下。
words.en: If you persuade someone to do something, you cause them to do it by giving them good reasons for doing it.

words.tr: v. 以甜言蜜语哄骗；勾引
words.ex: He tried to cajole his sister into lending him money.
words.ex_cn: 他试图哄骗妹妹把钱借给他。
words.en: If you cajole someone into doing something, you persuade them to do it by flattery or by making promises.

words.tr: v. 哄；用好话劝诱；哄骗
words.ex: He tried to coax the cat out from under the bed.
words.ex_cn: 他试图哄猫从床底下出来。
words.en: To coax someone means to persuade them to do something by gentle persuasion or flattery.

words.tr:
n. 骗局；恶作剧；戏弄
v. 愚弄
words.ex: The news was a hoax to scare people.
words.ex_cn: 这则新闻是个骗局，为了吓唬人。
words.en: A hoax is a plan to deceive someone, such as telling the police there is a bomb somewhere when there is not, or a trick in which someone tells people a lie.

words.ex: He tried to inveigle her into lending him money.
words.ex_cn: 他试图哄骗她借钱给他。
words.en: If you inveigle someone into doing something, you cleverly persuade them to do it when they do not really want to.

words.ex: The shop tries to entice customers with cheap prices.
words.ex_cn: 这家商店试图以低价吸引顾客。
words.en: If you entice someone, you attract them to a particular place or activity by making it seem attractive or interesting.

words.ex: He tried to seduce her with flowers and gifts.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用鲜花和礼物引诱她。
words.en: To seduce someone means to persuade them to do something, especially something wrong or unwise, by making it seem attractive or exciting.

words.ex: He abetted his friend to steal the car.
words.ex_cn: 他教唆朋友偷车。
words.en: To abet someone to do something wrong means to help or encourage them to do it.

words.ex: Please verify your email address.
words.ex_cn: 请核实你的电子邮件地址。
words.en: To verify something means to check or prove that it is true, accurate, or justified.

words.ex: The veracity of his story was questioned by the police.
words.ex_cn: 他的故事的真实性受到了警方的质疑。
words.en: Veracity refers to the quality of being true or accurate.

words.tr: adj. 诚实的；说实话的；准确的
words.ex: He is a veracious person who always tells the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个诚实的人，总是说真话。
words.en: Someone who is veracious is truthful and honest.

words.tr: adj. 貌似真实的; 可能的
words.ex: The story she told sounded verisimilar, but we later found out it was fabricated.
words.ex_cn: 她讲述的故事听起来很真实，但我们后来发现它是捏造的。
words.en: Having the appearance of truth; probable or likely.

words.ex: The jury gave a guilty verdict.
words.ex_cn: 陪审团作出了有罪裁决。
words.en: A verdict is a decision made after a lot of consideration, especially one made by a jury in a court of law.

words.ex: The doctor will certify that you are healthy.
words.ex_cn: 医生将证明你身体健康。
words.en: To officially declare something to be true, correct, or genuine, often in writing.

words.ex: The witness corroborated his story with photos.
words.ex_cn: 证人用照片证实了他的说法。
words.en: To corroborate something that has been said or reported means to provide evidence or information that supports it.

words.ex: He needs to substantiate his claim with evidence.
words.ex_cn: 他需要用证据来证实他的说法。
words.en: To substantiate a statement or a story means to supply evidence which proves that it is true.

words.tr: adj. 无故的；无必要的；无偿的；免费的
words.ex: He made a gratuitous comment about her clothes.
words.ex_cn: 他对她的衣服做了毫无必要的评论。
words.en: If you describe something as gratuitous, you mean that it is unnecessary, and often harmful or upsetting.

words.tr: n. 小费；赏钱；退职金；退伍金
words.ex: She left a small gratuity on the table for the waiter.
words.ex_cn: 她在桌上给服务员留下了一点小费。
words.en: A gratuity is a sum of money given to someone, typically to a service worker, in addition to the payment due for the service provided.

words.ex: He gratifies his parents by getting good grades.
words.ex_cn: 他通过取得好成绩来让父母感到欣慰。
words.en: If you are gratified by something, it gives you pleasure or satisfaction.

words.ex: He tries to ingratiate himself with his boss by bringing coffee every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上送咖啡给老板，试图讨好他。
words.en: If someone tries to ingratiate themselves with you, they do things to try and make you like them.

words.ex: He was an ingrate who never thanked anyone for their help.
words.ex_cn: 他是个忘恩负义的人，从不感谢别人的帮助。
words.en: An ingrate is a person who is not grateful for something that has been done for them.

words.ex: They revere their grandfather for his wisdom.
words.ex_cn: 他们因祖父的智慧而尊敬他。
words.en: If you revere someone or something, you respect and admire them greatly.

words.ex: He showed reverence for his grandfather.
words.ex_cn: 他对祖父表示尊敬。
words.en: A feeling of profound respect for someone or something.

words.ex: People venerate the ancient sage for his wisdom.
words.ex_cn: 人们因他的智慧而崇敬这位古代圣人。
words.en: To regard with respect or reverence.

words.ex: He earned the esteem of his colleagues through hard work.
words.ex_cn: 他通过努力工作赢得了同事们的尊重。
words.en: If you esteem someone or something, you respect or admire them.

words.tr:
n. 崇拜；崇敬；礼拜；
v. 崇拜；尊崇；做礼拜；
words.ex: The ancient people showed worship to the sun.
words.ex_cn: 古人对太阳进行崇拜。
words.en: The feeling or expression of reverence and adoration for a deity.

words.tr:
v. 喷涌；滔滔不绝地说
n. 涌出；喷出
words.ex: Water gushed from the broken pipe.
words.ex_cn: 水从破裂的管道中喷涌而出。
words.en: If someone gushes, they express their admiration or pleasure in an exaggerated way.

words.tr:
v. 使安静；使肃静
n. 安静
words.ex: Please hush, the baby is sleeping.
words.ex_cn: 请安静，宝宝在睡觉。
words.en: If you hush someone or if they hush, they stop speaking or making a noise.

words.ex: The lush grass looked green after the rain.
words.ex_cn: 雨后，葱翠的草地显得格外绿。
words.en: A lush area has a lot of green, healthy plants, grass, and trees.

words.ex: The hotel has a plush lobby with velvet chairs.
words.ex_cn: 这家酒店有一个豪华的大堂，配有丝绒椅子。
words.en: Plush refers to something that is luxurious and expensive, or a type of fabric that is very soft and thick.

words.tr:
n. 笨活；拙劣的工作
v. 做事拙劣；把…搞糟
words.ex: He did a botch on the painting, leaving it messy.
words.ex_cn: 他把这幅画搞成了个笨活，弄得一团糟。
words.en: If you botch something that you are doing, you do it badly or clumsily.

words.tr:
v. 拙劣地做；搞砸
n. 搞糟了的事情；失误
words.ex: He bungled the simple task.
words.ex_cn: 他把简单的任务搞砸了。
words.en: To bungle something means to do it badly or clumsily, often resulting in failure or mistakes.

words.tr: v. 笨拙地弄糟；笨手笨脚地走动；语无伦次
words.ex: He bumbled the presentation and forgot his lines.
words.ex_cn: 他笨拙地搞砸了演讲，忘记了台词。
words.en: To bumble is to move or act in an awkward or confused manner, often making mistakes or being inefficient.

words.tr: phrase. 搞砸：犯错误，导致事情失败或出现问题。
words.ex: He might screw up the presentation if he doesn't practice.
words.ex_cn: 如果他不练习，他可能会搞砸演讲。
words.en: To make a mistake or to fail at something.

words.tr: phrase. 弄乱；搞砸；犯错；使陷入困境
words.ex: He might mess up the plan if he doesn't listen.
words.ex_cn: 如果他不听，他可能会把计划搞砸。
words.en: To make a mistake or do something badly.

words.tr: v. 招手示意；举手召唤；引诱
words.ex: He beckoned to the boy to come closer.
words.ex_cn: 他向那个男孩招手示意过来。
words.en: If you beckon to someone, you signal to them to come to you, usually by a gesture of your hand.

words.ex: The beacon shines at night to guide ships.
words.ex_cn: 灯塔在夜晚发光以引导船只。
words.en: A beacon is a light or a fire, usually on a hill or tower, which acts as a signal or a warning.

words.ex: He ate eggs and bacon for breakfast.
words.ex_cn: 他早餐吃了鸡蛋和培根。
words.en: Bacon is a type of salt-cured pork made from various cuts, typically from the pork belly or from back cuts, which are less fatty than the belly.

words.tr:
n. 信号；
v. 用信号通知；
words.ex: The traffic light is a signal to stop.
words.ex_cn: 交通灯是一个停止的信号。
words.en: A signal is a gesture, sound, or action which is intended to give a particular message to the person who sees or hears it.

words.tr:
v. 吹嘘；自吹自擂
adj. 一流的；极好的
words.ex: He brags about his new car.
words.ex_cn: 他炫耀自己的新车。
words.en: If you brag, you say in a very proud way that you have something or have done something.

words.tr:
n. 吹牛者；自夸者
adj. 吹牛的
words.ex: He is a braggart who always talks about his wins.
words.ex_cn: 他是个自吹自擂的人，总是谈论自己的胜利。
words.en: A braggart is someone who boasts about their achievements or possessions in a way that is annoying to others.

words.tr: n. 夸耀；吹牛；自夸的行为
words.ex: His bragadocio made everyone feel uncomfortable at the party.
words.ex_cn: 他的吹牛让派对上的每个人都感到不舒服。

words.tr: n. 谦虚式自夸；以看似谦虚的方式炫耀自己
words.ex: He said, 'I'm so bad at sports, but I won the marathon last week,' which was a humblebrag.
words.ex_cn: 他说：'我运动很差，但上周我赢得了马拉松比赛。' 这是一种谦虚式炫耀。

words.tr: v. 自夸；夸耀；自豪地拥有
words.ex: He boasts about his new car.
words.ex_cn: 他夸耀自己的新车。
words.en: If someone boasts about something that they have done or that they own, they talk about it very proudly, in a way that other people may find irritating or offensive.

words.tr: adj. 夸大的；言过其实的
words.ex: He gave a bombastic speech full of big words.
words.ex_cn: 他做了一篇充满华丽辞藻的演讲。
words.en: If you describe someone as bombastic, you are criticizing them for trying to impress other people by saying things that sound impressive but have little meaning.

words.tr: v. 猛冲；猛投；猛烈碰撞
words.ex: The car hurtled down the hill.
words.ex_cn: 汽车飞速冲下山坡。
words.en: If someone or something hurtles somewhere, they move there very quickly, often in a uncontrolled way.

words.tr:
n. 跨栏；障碍；难关
v. 越过障碍；克服
words.ex: He jumped over the hurdle quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他迅速跳过了跨栏。
words.en: A hurdle is a problem or difficulty that you must deal with before you can achieve something.

words.ex: Add a dash of salt to the soup.
words.ex_cn: 给汤里加一点盐。
words.en: If you dash somewhere, you run or go there quickly and suddenly. A dash is a straight, horizontal line used in writing, for example to separate two main clauses whose meanings are closely connected.

words.tr:
n. 猛冲；冲刺；扑
v. 猛冲；冲刺；扑
words.ex: He made a sudden lunge at the ball.
words.ex_cn: 他突然向前扑向球。
words.en: If you lunge in a particular direction, you move in that direction suddenly and forcefully.

words.ex: The hawk made a sudden swoop to catch the mouse.
words.ex_cn: 老鹰突然俯冲下来抓老鼠。
words.en: To move very quickly and easily through the air, especially down from a height in order to attack.

words.ex: The power will devolve to the local government.
words.ex_cn: 权力将下放给地方政府。
words.en: If you devolve power, authority, or responsibility to a less powerful person or group, or if it devolves upon them, it is transferred to them.

words.tr: adj. 健谈的；滔滔不绝的
words.ex: He is a voluble speaker who talks all day.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个健谈的人，整天说个不停。
words.en: If you describe someone as voluble, you mean that they talk a lot with great energy and enthusiasm.

words.tr:
adj. 旋绕的；费解的
v. 盘旋；卷绕；“convolute”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: The path through the garden was convoluted.
words.ex_cn: 花园里的小路蜿蜒曲折。
words.en: If you describe something such as a story, explanation, or system as convoluted, you mean that it is complicated and difficult to understand.

words.ex: The Earth revolves around the Sun.
words.ex_cn: 地球围绕太阳转。
words.en: If something revolves or if you revolve something, it moves or turns around a central point or line.

words.tr:
v. 叛乱；反叛；（使）厌恶
n. 叛乱；厌恶；反感
words.ex: The people revolt against the unfair rules.
words.ex_cn: 人们反抗不公平的规则。
words.en: If a large number of people revolt, they refuse to be controlled or ruled, and take action against authority, often violent action.

words.tr:
v. 避开；躲避
n. 躲避；诡计
words.ex: He dodged the ball quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他迅速躲开了球。
words.en: If you dodge, you move quickly, often to avoid being hit, caught, or seen.

words.ex: He shuns loud parties because he is shy.
words.ex_cn: 他因为害羞而避开热闹的派对。
words.en: If you shun someone or something, you deliberately avoid them or keep away from them.

words.ex: He tries to eschew sugar for health reasons.
words.ex_cn: 他为了健康尽量避免吃糖。
words.en: If you eschew something, you deliberately avoid doing it or becoming involved in it.

words.tr: v. 绕行；设法避开；智胜；围住
words.ex: He circumvented the traffic by taking a small road.
words.ex_cn: 他通过走一条小路绕过了交通拥堵。
words.en: If someone circumvents a rule or restriction, they avoid having to obey it, usually in a clever and dishonest way.

words.tr:
v. 遭遇；遇到；邂逅；
n. 遭遇；
words.ex: He encountered a bear while hiking in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 他在森林里徒步时遭遇了一只熊。
words.en: If you encounter problems or difficulties, you experience them.

words.ex: The sudden jolt woke me up.
words.ex_cn: 突然的震动把我惊醒了。
words.en: If something jolts or if something jolts it, it moves suddenly and quite violently.

words.tr:
v. 脱毛；换毛
n. 脱毛；换毛
words.ex: The bird molts its feathers every spring.
words.ex_cn: 这只鸟每年春天都会脱毛。
words.en: When an animal molts, it loses its feathers, hair, or skin so that new ones can grow.

words.ex: He is a dolt who doesn't understand simple math.
words.ex_cn: 他是个连简单数学都不懂的傻瓜。
words.en: A dolt is a person who is not very intelligent and who often makes mistakes.

words.ex: The mechanic tightened the bolt with a wrench.
words.ex_cn: 机械师用扳手拧紧了螺栓。
words.en: A bolt is a type of fastener consisting of a threaded pin or rod with a head at one end, designed to be inserted through holes in assembled parts and tightened by a nut from the other end. It can also refer to a sudden dash or run, or to eat food quickly and without chewing.

words.ex: The colt runs fast across the field.
words.ex_cn: 小马在田野上快速奔跑。
words.en: A colt is a young male horse, especially one that is less than four years old.

words.tr:
v. 轻摇；摇动；摇曳；啮合
n. 轻摇；摇动；啮合扣
words.ex: He joggles the table to make the cup move.
words.ex_cn: 他晃动桌子，让杯子移动。
words.en: To move or cause to move with repeated small bobs or jerks.

words.tr:
n. 探测器；
v. 探查；
words.ex: The probe sent back photos from Mars.
words.ex_cn: 探测器从火星传回了照片。
words.en: If you probe into something, you ask questions or try to discover facts about it. A probe is also a long thin instrument that doctors and dentists use to examine parts of the body.

words.ex: He is on probation for one year.
words.ex_cn: 他被判缓刑一年。
words.en: Probation is a period of time during which someone who has committed a crime has to behave well and not commit any more crimes in order to avoid being sent to prison.

words.tr:
n. 遗嘱检验；遗嘱认证
v. 核实（或检验）遗嘱
words.ex: The lawyer is handling the probate of the estate.
words.ex_cn: 律师正在处理遗产的遗嘱认证。
words.en: Probate is the legal process in which a will is reviewed to determine whether it is valid and authentic.

words.ex: He is known for his probity in business.
words.ex_cn: 他以商业中的正直著称。
words.en: Probity is the quality of having strong moral principles and honesty.

words.tr: n. 堕落的人；不道德的人
words.ex: The townspeople shunned the reprobate, fearing his influence.
words.ex_cn: 镇上的人们都避开那个堕落的人，害怕他的影响。
words.en: A reprobate is a person who behaves in a way that is morally wrong and who shows no regret or shame for their actions.

words.ex: The teacher reproved the student for being late.
words.ex_cn: 老师因为学生迟到而责骂了他。
words.en: If you reprove someone, you speak angrily or seriously to them because they have behaved in a wrong or foolish way.

words.ex: His work finally received the approbation of his peers.
words.ex_cn: 他的工作最终得到了同行的认可。
words.en: Official approval or agreement.

words.tr: n. 不赞成；持反对意见；非难
words.ex: He felt disapprobation when he saw the messy room.
words.ex_cn: 当他看到凌乱的房间时，他感到不满。
words.en: Disapprobation is a strong feeling of disapproval or condemnation.

words.ex: The mirror distorts my face.
words.ex_cn: 这面镜子扭曲了我的脸。
words.en: If you distort a statement, fact, or idea, you report or represent it in an untrue way.

words.tr: n. 侵权行为（不构成刑事犯罪但可引起民事诉讼)
words.ex: He was charged with tort for damaging the car.
words.ex_cn: 他因损坏汽车被指控为侵权。
words.en: A tort is a wrongful act or an infringement of a right leading to civil legal liability.

words.ex: He contorts his face to make the kids laugh.
words.ex_cn: 他扭曲面部表情来逗孩子们笑。
words.en: If someone's face or body contorts or is contorted, it moves into an unnatural and unattractive shape or position.

words.ex: The gang tried to extort money from the shop owner.
words.ex_cn: 这个帮派试图向店主敲诈钱财。
words.en: To extort is to obtain something, especially money, through force, threats, or other unfair means.

words.tr:
v. 反驳；回嘴
n. 反驳；顶嘴
words.ex: He gave a quick retort when she criticized him.
words.ex_cn: 当她批评他时，他迅速回了一句。
words.en: If you retort, you reply angrily to someone.

words.tr:
n. 酷刑；拷打
v. 拷打；折磨
words.ex: The prisoner suffered from torture during the war.
words.ex_cn: 这名囚犯在战争期间遭受了酷刑。
words.en: Torture is the act of deliberately inflicting severe physical or psychological pain on someone, typically to extract information or a confession, or as a punishment.

words.tr:
n. 痛苦；折磨；令人痛苦的东西
v. 折磨；使痛苦；烦扰；纠缠；戏弄
words.ex: The loss of his dog was a deep torment.
words.ex_cn: 失去他的狗是一种深深的痛苦。
words.en: Torment refers to severe physical or mental suffering, or to cause someone to experience such suffering.

words.tr: adj. 折磨人的；充满痛苦（或苦恼）的
words.ex: The torturous hike made him want to quit.
words.ex_cn: 那条折磨人的徒步路线让他想放弃。
words.en: If you describe something as torturous, you mean that it causes great suffering or anxiety.

words.ex: The tortuous road wound through the mountains.
words.ex_cn: 这条弯曲的道路蜿蜒穿过山脉。
words.en: If you describe something as tortuous, you mean that it is very long, complicated, and difficult to understand.

words.ex: He tried to falsify the report.
words.ex_cn: 他试图篡改报告。
words.en: To falsify means to change something in order to deceive people, or to make a false statement.

words.ex: The doctor helped the sick child.
words.ex_cn: 医生帮助了生病的孩子。
words.en: A doctor is someone who is qualified in medicine and treats people who are ill.

words.tr: v. 拨弄；玩弄；篡改；收买
words.ex: Don't tamper with the machine.
words.ex_cn: 不要拨弄这台机器。
words.en: If someone tampers with something, they interfere with it or make unauthorized changes to it, often in order to cause damage or make it work differently.

words.tr: v. 歪曲；不实报道；曲解
words.ex: He misrepresents the facts to win the debate.
words.ex_cn: 他歪曲事实以赢得辩论。
words.en: To give a false or misleading account of the nature of something.

words.ex: Parents should foster good habits in children.
words.ex_cn: 父母应该培养孩子的好习惯。
words.en: To foster something means to encourage and promote its development.

words.tr: v. 促进；使便利；使容易；
words.ex: The teacher facilitates learning by asking questions.
words.ex_cn: 老师通过提问来促进学习。
words.en: To make an action or process easier or more likely to happen.

words.tr: phrase. 换高速挡； 改进…以适应提高生产的需要； 使做好行动准备
words.ex: They gear up for the new school year.
words.ex_cn: 他们为新学年做准备。
words.en: To prepare or make ready for a particular event or situation.

words.tr:
n. 教养；养育；培育；
v. 培养；
words.ex: Her parents gave her good nurture.
words.ex_cn: 她的父母给了她良好的教养。
words.en: To nurture someone or something is to care for and encourage their growth or development.

words.ex: Behold the beautiful sunset.
words.ex_cn: 看那美丽的日落。
words.en: To see or observe (someone or something, especially something remarkable or impressive).

words.ex: The judge will uphold the law.
words.ex_cn: 法官将维护法律。
words.en: If you uphold something such as a law, a principle, or a decision, you support and maintain it.

words.ex: The company will withhold his salary until he signs the contract.
words.ex_cn: 公司会扣留他的工资，直到他签署合同。
words.en: If you withhold something that someone wants, you refuse to let them have it.

words.tr: v. 切断；脱离；切成两段
words.ex: He severed the rope with a knife.
words.ex_cn: 他用刀把绳子割断了。
words.en: To sever something means to cut through it or to break it off completely.

words.tr:
adj. 分开的；分离的；单独的；
v. 分离；隔离；
words.ex: They live in separate houses.
words.ex_cn: 他们住在分开的房子里。
words.en: To cause to move or be apart; to divide or keep apart.

words.ex: The teacher will assess your homework tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 老师明天会评估你的作业。
words.en: to judge or decide the amount, value, quality, or importance of something

words.ex: He obsesses over small mistakes.
words.ex_cn: 他 obsesses 于微小的错误。
words.en: If something or someone obsesses you, you think or worry about them all the time and you cannot think about anything else.

words.ex: He was beset by problems at work.
words.ex_cn: 他被工作中的问题困扰。
words.en: If someone or something is beset by problems or fears, they have many problems or fears which affect them severely.

words.tr: n. 一段时间；会议；会期；开庭；学年；
words.ex: We had a long session of studying together.
words.ex_cn: 我们一起学习了一段时间。
words.en: A session is a meeting of a court, parliament, or other official group, or a period of time used for a particular activity, especially by a group of people.

words.ex: The shopkeeper will evaluate the old watch.
words.ex_cn: 店主将估价这块旧手表。
words.en: If you evaluate something or someone, you consider them in order to make a judgment about them, for example about how good or bad they are.

words.ex: The teacher will appraise my essay next week.
words.ex_cn: 老师下周会评价我的作文。
words.en: If you appraise something or someone, you consider them carefully and form an opinion about them.

words.tr:
n. 价值；（数）值；
v. 估价；重视；
words.ex: The value of this painting is very high.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画的价值很高。
words.en: If you value something or someone, you think that they are important and you appreciate them.

words.ex: I can't recollect where I put my keys.
words.ex_cn: 我想不起来把钥匙放在哪儿了。
words.en: If you recollect something, you remember it.

words.tr:
v. 回忆起；召回；
n. 记忆力；
words.ex: I recall my first day at school.
words.ex_cn: 我想起了我上学的第一天。
words.en: If you recall something, you remember it and tell others about it.

words.ex: We sit together and reminisce about old times.
words.ex_cn: 我们坐在一起回忆过去的时光。
words.en: If you reminisce about something from your past, you write or talk about it, often with pleasure.

words.tr: adj. 贪赃枉法的；腐败的
words.ex: The official was venal and took bribes.
words.ex_cn: 这位官员贪腐，接受了贿赂。
words.en: If you describe someone as venal, you disapprove of them because they are prepared to do almost anything in return for money, even things which are dishonest or immoral.

words.ex: The venality of the officials led to widespread corruption.
words.ex_cn: 官员的唯利是图导致了普遍的腐败。
words.en: The quality or state of being venal; readiness to sell one's services or influence for money or other benefits.

words.ex: He made a venial mistake in the report.
words.ex_cn: 他在报告中犯了一个可以原谅的错误。
words.en: If you describe a wrong action as venial, you mean that it is not very serious or grave, and therefore easy to forgive.

words.ex: The vernal equinox marks the beginning of spring.
words.ex_cn: 春分标志着春天的开始。
words.en: Relating to or occurring in spring.

words.ex: The venerable teacher has taught for over 40 years.
words.ex_cn: 这位值得尊敬的老师已经教书40多年了。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as venerable, you mean that they are old and respected.

words.ex: She dotes on her little grandson.
words.ex_cn: 她非常疼爱她的孙子。
words.en: If you say that someone dotes on a person or a thing, you mean that they love or care about them very much and spend a lot of time with them.

words.ex: He endow a library with books.
words.ex_cn: 他捐赠了一图书馆的书。
words.en: If someone is endowed with a particular quality or ability, they naturally have it.

words.ex: Her family gave a dowry when she married.
words.ex_cn: 她结婚时，她的家人给了嫁妆。
words.en: A dowry is property or money that a woman brings to her husband when they marry.

words.ex: The teacher will not condone cheating in exams.
words.ex_cn: 老师不会容忍考试作弊。
words.en: To condone something means to accept or allow behavior that is considered wrong.

words.ex: The country will extradite the suspect to Canada.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家将把嫌疑人引渡到加拿大。
words.en: If someone is extradited, they are officially sent back to their own or another country to be tried for a crime that they have been accused of.

words.ex: Parents shouldn't indulge their children's bad habits.
words.ex_cn: 父母不应该放任孩子的坏习惯。
words.en: To indulge means to allow yourself or someone else to have something enjoyable, especially more than is good for you.

words.ex: She pampered her baby with warm baths and soft blankets.
words.ex_cn: 她用温水浴和柔软的毯子细心照顾她的婴儿。
words.en: To treat someone very kindly, often too kindly, by letting them have or do whatever they want.

words.tr:
v. 宠爱；娇养；纵容
n. 宠儿
words.ex: She cosseted her baby with soft blankets and gentle songs.
words.ex_cn: 她用柔软的毯子和轻柔的歌声呵护她的婴儿。
words.en: To cosset someone means to treat them with great care and attention, often in a way that is excessive or indulgent.

words.ex: She coddles her little brother too much.
words.ex_cn: 她太宠着她的弟弟了。
words.en: To treat someone in an indulgent or overprotective way.

words.tr:
v. 娇惯；纵容
n. 娇惯的男人；女性化的男人
words.ex: Don't mollycoddle the child; let him learn from mistakes.
words.ex_cn: 不要过分溺爱这个孩子；让他从错误中学习。
words.en: To mollycoddle someone is to treat them in an overprotective or indulgent way.

words.ex: He decided to discard his old habits.
words.ex_cn: 他决定抛开旧习惯。
words.en: To discard something means to get rid of it because you no longer want it or need it.

words.ex: The cardiac patient needs to rest daily.
words.ex_cn: 这位心脏病人需要每天休息。
words.en: Cardiac means relating to the heart.

words.tr:
adj. 首要的；大红色的
n. 红衣主教；枢机主教；基数
words.ex: This is a cardinal rule in our school.
words.ex_cn: 这是我们学校的一项首要规则。
words.en: A cardinal rule or quality is the most important one.

words.tr:
adj. 热诚的；友好的
n. 甜露酒
words.ex: He gave a cordial smile to his neighbor.
words.ex_cn: 他对着邻居露出了热情的微笑。
words.en: warm and friendly

words.ex: The two countries reached a concord on trade.
words.ex_cn: 这两个国家在贸易上达成了一致。
words.en: Concord is a state of agreement or harmony between people or groups.

words.ex: They had a discord about the movie ending.
words.ex_cn: 他们对电影的结局有分歧。
words.en: Disagreement or strife between people or groups.

words.ex: The farmer dug a ditch to water the fields.
words.ex_cn: 农夫挖了一条沟来给田地浇水。
words.en: A ditch is a long narrow trench or furrow dug in the ground, especially for drainage or irrigation.

words.tr:
v. 丢弃；放弃；扔掉
n. 投弃；抛弃；投弃货物
words.ex: The pilot had to jettison extra fuel to land safely.
words.ex_cn: 飞行员不得不抛掉多余的燃料以安全着陆。
words.en: To jettison something means to throw it away or get rid of it, usually because it is not wanted or needed.

words.ex: He insinuated that she was lying.
words.ex_cn: 他暗示她在撒谎。
words.en: If you say that someone insinuates that something bad is the case, you mean that they say it in an indirect way.

words.ex: The river has a sinuous path through the forest.
words.ex_cn: 这条河在森林中蜿蜒流淌。
words.en: Something that is sinuous has many smooth turns and curves.

words.ex: The doctor examined the sinus in her nasal cavity.
words.ex_cn: 医生检查了她鼻腔中的窦。
words.en: A sinus is a cavity within a bone or other tissue, especially one in the bones of the face or skull connecting with the nasal cavities.

words.ex: His insinuation made her feel uncomfortable.
words.ex_cn: 他的暗示让她感到不舒服。
words.en: An insinuation is an indirect suggestion or hint, especially one that is derogatory or unpleasant.

words.ex: They have an intimate friendship.
words.ex_cn: 他们有着亲密的友谊。
words.en: having a close, friendly, or personal relationship with someone; private and personal

words.tr: n. 暗指；影射；间接提及
words.ex: He made an allusion to Shakespeare in his speech.
words.ex_cn: 他在演讲中提到了莎士比亚。
words.en: An allusion is an indirect reference to someone or something.

words.tr: n. 含意；可能的影响（或后果）；暗示；
words.ex: The implication of his words was that he was sorry.
words.ex_cn: 他话中的含意是他很抱歉。
words.en: An implication is a possible future effect or result of an action or decision, often one that is not immediately obvious.

words.tr:
n. 影射；暗指
v. 旁敲侧击地表达；含沙射影
words.ex: He made an innuendo about her being late.
words.ex_cn: 他暗示她迟到了。
words.en: An indirect or subtle, usually derogatory implication in expression; an insinuation.

words.ex: He contrived to finish the project on time.
words.ex_cn: 他设法按时完成了项目。
words.en: If you contrive an event or situation, you succeed in making it happen, often by tricking someone.

words.ex: The machine is a clever contrivance that saves a lot of time.
words.ex_cn: 这台机器是一个节省大量时间的发明。
words.en: A contrivance is a device or plan that is used to achieve a particular result, often in a way that is clever but not always honest or straightforward.

words.ex: The bird hatched her eggs after three weeks.
words.ex_cn: 这只鸟在三周后孵出了她的蛋。
words.en: To hatch means to cause an egg to break open so that a young animal can come out, or to plan secretly with other people to do something bad or illegal.

words.ex: The police discovered a scheme to steal money.
words.ex_cn: 警方发现了一个偷钱的阴谋。
words.en: A scheme is a plan or arrangement, especially one produced by a government or other organization, or a secret plan to do something, especially something illegal or dishonest.

words.ex: They conspire to cheat on the test.
words.ex_cn: 他们密谋在考试中作弊。
